modo: DP-1 (headset) disconnected at DRM level after switching KDE Plasma Wayland -> GNOME Wayland session, no cable touched
driver: USB companion enumerates fine (5/5 devices), Monado wmr_hmd_activate_reverb sends activation report successfully, but /sys/class/drm/card0-DP-1/status=disconnected edid_bytes=0 both before and after. jack-in-wayland.sh (mode 1, also retried with WMR_DISPLAY_INIT_SLEEP_SECONDS=6) fails identically both times: 'Found no connectors available for direct mode' -> XRT_ERROR_VULKAN. GNOME/mutter correctly publishes wp_drm_lease_device_v1 (not a compositor/lease-policy bug, DP-1 just isn't hotplugged at all). User confirms physically: adapter status LED (combined DP+power/USB) lit, USB and DP seated as always, nothing moved -- but HP logo fully OFF (not even boot logo, unlike the DP-training-fails-but-panel-lit cases in docs/13). Matches the T025 precedent (post-reboot enumeration failure fixed by a plain cable unplug/replug, no port/orientation change). Testing next: cut power to the headset for 20s and replug.
veredicto: Power cut 20s + replug: USB re-enumerated cleanly (new bus/device numbers, 5/5 present), but DP-1 still disconnected/0 EDID bytes before and after. Retried jack-in-wayland.sh mode 1: same 'Found no connectors available for direct mode' failure. User confirms physically with Monado still running (activation report sent): HP logo screen itself is black, panel fully black - not even the boot logo (different from the historically-documented 'HP logo on, panel off' 90Hz failure mode in docs/13). Power cycle did not fix it. Next: check dmesg/journalctl broadly for any DP/AUX/HPD kernel-level event around the replug moment.

modo: USB-only replug (not power-cut), casco combo cable, DP untouched
driver: Testing the T025 precedent specifically: does a plain USB replug (adapter status LED confirmed OFF while unplugged, ON when replugged -- so the LED tracks USB power, not DP link health) fix DP-1 on its own, without touching the DP side or cutting power.
veredicto: USB re-enumerated cleanly again (new bus/device numbers, 5/5 present). Relaunched jack-in-wayland.sh mode 1 to send a fresh activation report against the newly-enumerated companion (previous monado-service instance predated this replug and never re-activated). Same result: DP-1 stays disconnected/0 EDID, 'Found no connectors available for direct mode'. Rules out USB enumeration/re-activation timing as the cause -- confirms this is isolated to the DP path specifically, not USB. Decision: stop software-side probing, reboot the PC as the next simple test before the more invasive DP-1<->DP-2 port swap (which needs relocating a desktop monitor). Session state and full context saved to CLAUDE.md for continuity across the reboot.

modo: Plain PC reboot, DP-1 status check first thing after boot

veredicto: Reboot did NOT fix it. Fresh boot, GNOME/Wayland session active, USB 5/5 enumerated cleanly -- but /sys/class/drm/card0-DP-1/status is still 'disconnected', 0 EDID bytes, checked as the very first thing after login. Software/session-state causes are now fully exhausted (config unchanged, driver unchanged, fresh boot, correct session, USB fine). Moving to the physical discriminator: swap the headset's cable to DP-2 (currently the working port for a desktop monitor) to separate cable/dongle fault from GPU port fault.

modo: Headset cable moved from DP-1 to DP-2 (a port already proven healthy - the monitor that was on it works fine elsewhere/moved), discriminating port vs cable/dongle

veredicto: Headset moved to DP-2: still disconnected, 0 EDID bytes. User confirms physically: no HP logo, panel still dark. DP-1 now shows 'connected, 128 EDID bytes' with the monitor that moved there in the headset's place -- proving DP-1 itself works fine for a normal display, and by extension DP-2 was already known-good (it drove that same monitor before the swap). The fault followed the headset's cable/dongle across ports, not the GPU side. This rules out 'bad GPU DP port' as the cause -- narrows it to the headset's own combo cable/dongle, or the headset's DP output stage itself (bridge chip side), not the host.

modo: Same headset + same cable/dongle tested on the Windows machine
driver: Discriminator test: if the headset also fails to light on Windows with this exact physical cable, it confirms a hardware fault in the cable/dongle/headset DP output stage, not anything specific to this Linux rig. If it works fine on Windows, the fault is somehow host-specific despite DP-1/DP-2 both failing here (would need to reopen investigation).
veredicto: Tested on Windows with the same physical headset+cable: SteamVR throws error 422 (generic 'SteamVR failed to open', no further detail) and the panel itself does not light -- BUT the HP boot logo DOES show, unlike the total blackout seen on this Linux rig (both DP-1 and DP-2). So the DP link trains enough on Windows to reach the logo stage, further than it gets here. Error 422 researched: it's a generic SteamVR-open failure, documented as common specifically with HP Reverb G2 + the Oasis WMR driver (github.com/mbucchia/Oasis-Driver-for-Windows-Mixed-Reality/issues/26), not headset-hardware-specific by itself. This complicates the pure 'dead cable' theory (a fully dead DP line shouldn't produce a logo on any host) -- leaves open whether it's a marginal/degrading connection (enough for a low-bandwidth logo mode, not enough for full panel init) vs. a software/driver-side failure on the Windows side coincidentally happening at the same time. User has since reconnected everything back to the original Linux layout (headset on DP-1, monitor back on DP-2) and also reseated/flipped the USB-C connector.

Software/session/port axis fully exhausted -- confirmed hardware fault in the headset's cable/dongle/DP output stage, not GPU-side.

This kills the T037 leading suspect (residual software state on the lab Linux SSD) -- no shared software remains between the failing configs. What IS shared across every failing test: the headset itself, its cable (with its inline active electronics/combiner box), and the G2 power brick. Conclusion: progressive hardware failure in that shared chain.

Maybe the USB cable is bad?' x8, 'Device not responding to setup address', 'device not accepting address 21, error -71' (~21 enumeration attempts), plus automatic port power-cycles - all failed. So the failure is still PROGRESSING: DP+panel died first, the USB2 pair died hours later, USB3 pairs still alive. Independent conductor groups in the same cable failing one after another = the cable (or its visor-end connector) failing wholesale. The kernel's own diagnosis matches the community's classic G2 cable-death pattern. Practical verdict: replacement cable (rev 2A). Remaining cheap test: flex/wiggle localization with a live USB monitor.

modo: Controller stress: 10 power-cycles of both controllers against a LIVE session, must reconnect 10/10
driver: NEXT-STEP item 1 adapted: instead of 10 service boot cycles, 10 controller power-cycles against the running session - exercises the same reconnect path the input patches (0001-0008) fixed. Monitored live via jack-in-wayland.log.
veredicto: COULD NOT BE COMPLETED - blocked by the degrading cable contact, and productive anyway. What it established: (1) HOT-ADD DOES NOT EXIST: controllers powered on against a running session never reach Monado (log silent, trigger does nothing in the player - user: 'sigue de largo'); the second controller vibration is only the headset firmware accepting the BT link. jack-in.sh's comment ('Monado only probes at startup') is correct; NEXT-STEP's 'before or after no longer matters' overstated T025, which was a pairing completing seconds late during startup, not a late power-on. (2) User's BT-layer power-cycle stats: 4 cycles both OK, then left controller missed its 2nd vibration once, then all OK - left slightly less reliable at the BT layer, consistent with their earlier anecdote. (3) The service-restart protocol (the real test: 10 boots with controllers on, 10/10 connects) aborted: v1 cycle invalid (started during post-screen-off companion re-enumeration, protocol error); v2 aborted twice on companion absence (T044 recurrence); after the USB replug recovery, the next activation attempt triggered violent USB2-branch flapping (companion device number jumped 036->091 within a minute, wmr_hmd_activate_reverb Send/Get all -1) - a NEW failure mode: enumerates but HID I/O fails, correlated with panel-activation power transitions hitting the marginal contact (the docs/06 'hub reset scales with panel load' mechanism, amplified). The one cycle that completed before abort: left=yes right=NO in 40s - not clean controller data, just the flapping. VERDICT: 10/10 boot-cycle test deferred until the rev2A replacement cable is installed; panel on/off cycling is the worst-case workload for the degraded contact and should be minimized meanwhile. Steady-state sessions remain fine (T042: 25 min flawless).

modo: RECURRENCE: USB2 branch dropped again ~40 min after the visor reseat, following the stability run's screen-off + a service restart
driver: Same signature as pre-reseat (T039): SuperSpeed branch present, USB2 hub/companion/audio absent, kernel silent (not even retrying). The docs/12 screen-off-induced re-enumeration appears to have hit the marginal contact and the branch never re-trained. This is the recurrence docs/22 said would move the rev2A replacement cable back onto the table. Recovery attempt order: USB replug at PC, then visor-end reseat.
veredicto: Recovered with step (a) of the docs/22 ladder alone: a USB replug at the PC end brought the full USB2 branch back instantly and cleanly (5/5, zero -71 retries in the kernel log - contrast with T039's ~21-retry storm). So this recurrence was SOFT: the screen-off-induced re-enumeration lost the branch, but the contact itself was recoverable without touching the visor connector. Updated read: the marginal contact has good and bad states; panel/screen-off cycling can knock the USB2 branch out, and how hard it is to recover varies. The rev2A replacement cable is now a firm recommendation (first recurrence ~40 min after the reseat), but the system remains usable meanwhile with the ladder. Proceeding to re-run the 10-boot-cycle controller test, which doubles as a screen-off-cycling endurance probe for this same contact.

modo: TRACKING DEAD investigation: 3DoF orientation was NOT working during T041/T042 (image glued to the face), user confirmed retroactively
driver: Player was the correct modern build (all 5 patches). Session was jack-in-wayland (WMR_SLAM=0 WMR_CAMERAS=0, IMU-only). HoloLens Sensors device was enumerated all night. The T042 session log was destroyed (jack-in-wayland.sh truncates on every start; the controller cycles overwrote it). Reproducing live with WMR_LOG=debug + HELLO_XR_POSE_STATS=1: inter-frame rotation ~0 while the user moves their head = tracking dead, measured.
veredicto: NOT REPRODUCIBLE today - tracking works, measured and user-confirmed. New session on the x3600 (after a panel.py pre-activation rescued the panel from an intermittent screen_on HID -1 failure): HELLO_XR_POSE_STATS shows the documented 3DoF jitter floor at rest (mean 0.0003-0.0016 deg/frame, max 0.056 - byte-identical to the historical measurement) and real tracked movement when the user turns their head (windows of mean 0.85-1.5 deg/frame, peaks 2.9 deg, at steady 90fps). User: 'la imagen sigue, todo bien'. VERDICT on T041/T042's dead tracking: session-specific, best hypothesis = the WMR reading thread (wmr_run_thread, the IMU packet reader) died mid-session from a USB hiccup on the degraded cable contact and Monado never restarts it - pose freezes while compositor/video/panel continue perfectly. Supporting context: this same night showed intermittent HID write failures (screen_on -1) seconds after successful writes. Direct proof impossible: jack-in-wayland.sh truncates its log on every start and the controller-cycle runs destroyed the T042 session log. Countermeasure applied: log rotation added to jack-in-wayland.sh (.prev.log). Field symptom guide: image glued to face + everything else fine -> grep the live log for 'Exiting reading thread'; a session restart recovers.

modo: PANEL DEAD investigation on iashur: after T041-T045 closed the night clean, a new session found the panel never powering on (no HP logo, DP disconnected on all 3 ports) despite the USB2 branch recovering twice via visor-end reseat
driver: Session opened with USB at 3/5 (companion+audio missing, same signature as T039/T044) and Monado failing 'Found no connectors available for direct mode'. Two visor-end connector reseats (behind the face gasket) both restored USB to a stable 5/5 -- but neither one budged the panel: still completely dark, zero logo, DP-1/DP-2/DP-3 all 'disconnected' with 0B EDID throughout. This decouples the USB2 data-pin fault (fixed twice by reseating) from a SEPARATE fault in the power-rail path, something not previously isolated this cleanly.
veredicto: UNRESOLVED, escalated to hardware-replacement territory. Systematic elimination, in order: (1) brick verified receiving wall power (own indicator LED lit); (2) barrel connector brick-to-breakout exercised via a deliberate 12V-only disconnect/reconnect test -- unexpected finding: disconnecting ONLY the 12V barrel caused ALL 5 USB devices to drop simultaneously too (kernel log: 5 simultaneous 'USB disconnect' lines at the same timestamp), meaning the physical act of handling the breakout box jostles the whole marginal cable, not just the connector being touched -- reconnecting 12V brought USB back to a clean stable 5/5 within seconds, panel still dark; (3) GPU-side ruled out: the DP cable was moved to a different physical port on the same card, jack-in-wayland.sh (mode 1) still reports 'Found no connectors available', all three DP connectors on card0 read disconnected regardless of which one the cable occupies. With brick, breakout barrel, USB branch and GPU port all cleared, the remaining suspects are (a) the power-pin subset specifically inside the visor-end connector -- distinct physical contacts from the USB data pins that keep recovering -- or (b) an actual break in the power conductors somewhere in the cable run. Neither is fixable by reseating, which has now been tried twice with 0/2 success on power despite 2/2 success on USB. This is the strongest evidence yet for the rev2A replacement cable docs/22 already flagged as a firm recommendation -- next escalation would be opening the breakout box to inspect the internal 12V wiring directly, not attempted tonight (undocumented procedure, more invasive than anything tried so far).

modo: Windows confirmation session, morning after T046 (power rail found dead on Linux, 0/2 reseats fixed it there)
driver: Sanity-check the cable/connector on Windows before deciding on the rev2A replacement: does securing the cable recover it there too, and does it hold across restarts?
veredicto: User report, not yet transcribed to file by the agent: on Windows, the two already-documented SteamVR errors reproduced first (422 'bad connection'-type and 108 'not detected'/no-logo, matching T034/T038) -- consistent with prior findings, not new. Securing/reseating the cable then recovered it, and 3 consecutive Windows restarts all came back clean with no drama. New observation, not previously recorded: at cold boot the HP logo starts OFF (dark), but once SteamVR is entered a single time, the logo/panel stops going dark afterward for the rest of the session. Notable tension with T046: on Linux the same reseat action fixed the USB2 branch 2/2 but never recovered the panel/power rail (0/2); on Windows this morning, securing the cable recovered the panel too and held across 3 restarts. Possible readings: (a) Windows' driver/EDID retry behavior tolerates the marginal contact better than nvidia-drm's HPD path, (b) this session's reseat happened to land on a better contact than T046's two attempts, or (c) the fault is intermittent enough that a fixed verdict from either OS alone is unreliable. Not discriminated yet.

modo: Fresh Linux boot (iashur, ~7min uptime): USB was already 5/5 healthy with no reseat needed, but DP-1/2/3 all disconnected -- same dead-panel signature as T046 end state. Ran panel.py activate (no sudo needed, hidraw6 is plugdev-writable) as a pure power/HID diagnostic before touching the cable/connector at all.
driver: Windows this morning showed the same pattern: HP logo starts OFF at cold boot and only lights once SteamVR is entered once (T047). Testing whether Linux panel death is actually the same cold-boot-needs-explicit-activation behavior, not a separate dead power rail as T046 concluded -- T046 never explicitly re-ran panel.py activate after its two successful USB reseats, it went straight to physical elimination (brick/barrel/GPU port) with DP still dark.
veredicto: CONFIRMED: panel.py activate alone (HID reports 0x09/0x08/0x06 returned valid identification data, no -1s -- healthy, unlike T043/T046's -1 failures) brought the panel up. User confirmed physically: 'prendio logo'. DP-1 immediately went disconnected -> connected, 384-byte EDID (the known-healthy signature). This directly challenges T046's 'separate dead power rail, escalate to rev2A' verdict: with USB already 5/5 and no cable/connector touched at all this boot, the panel was fully recoverable by software activation alone. Strong candidate explanation for T046: DP hotplug on this headset may simply never happen on its own at cold power-on and always requires the WMR activation HID sequence -- which is normal G2 behavior (Windows/SteamVR do the same thing, hence T047's logo-stays-dark-until-SteamVR observation) -- and T046's two reseats, done while chasing the USB fault, may never have been followed by a clean activate() call before escalating to hardware theories. Next: bring up the full stack (jack-in-wayland.sh) to confirm Monado/mutter lease + real 90Hz content still works end-to-end from this state, and re-read T046 for whether activate was actually tried post-reseat.

modo: Full stack confirmation on iashur (5600) after T048: jack-in-wayland.sh mode 1 (4320x2160@90) + play360.sh playlist-test (3 clips), -t 60, following the panel.py activate that brought DP-1 up from cold-boot-dead
driver: Confirm end-to-end that the panel.py activate finding (T048) was not a fluke -- does the full Monado/mutter/hello_xr pipeline actually run real content cleanly from this state, matching T041/T042 quality, with zero cable/connector reseat this boot?
veredicto: PASSED, user's words: 'si, todo perfecto'. Lease granted (DP-1/HPN), 4320x2160@90.00 taken, playlist chained all 3 clips in order (1/3 -> 2/3 -> 3/3) unattended, NVDEC used for the <=4096px clips exactly as in T041/T042. Clean SIGTERM teardown, monado-service exited on its own (no -9 needed), DP-1 stayed connected afterward. Only artifact: the already-documented cosmetic Vulkan validation errors on shutdown (vkFreeCommandBuffers/vkDestroySemaphore in use), same as T041, no user-visible effect. COMBINED WITH T048, this substantially revises T046's verdict: what looked like 'a separate dead power rail, needs the rev2A replacement cable' was reproduced here as a fully cold Linux boot where USB was ALREADY 5/5 (no reseat performed this session at all) and DP came up the instant panel.py activate ran. Matches T047's Windows observation (logo starts dark at boot, stays lit only after SteamVR activates it once) -- same headset behavior on both OSes, not an OS-specific driver quirk and not obviously a hardware fault. Leading theory now: the G2 never hotplugs DP on its own at cold power-on on ANY OS; it always needs the WMR activation HID sequence first, and T046's two reseats were followed by Monado's own startup attempting that activation while USB was mid-recovery/unstable -- a timing/USB-stability problem at the moment of activation, not a dead power rail. Does NOT yet rule out that the marginal contact still causes the USB2-branch dropouts (T039/T044) or the mid-session freezes (T045) -- only the 'separate dead power rail' piece of T046 is in question. Open follow-up: reproduce T046's exact sequence (USB2 dead -> reseat to fix USB -> try activate immediately) to see if activate reliably succeeds right after a reseat, which would fully explain T046 away as 'never got a clean activate attempt in.'

modo: 10x boot-cycle test (T043 deferred item) on iashur, controllers powered on throughout. Round 1 aborted cycle 2/10 on a fresh no-connectors failure despite USB 5/5; measured panel.py-activate-to-DP-hotplug latency directly: 3 clean off->activate runs = ~0.5s consistent, but activate right after a failed jack-in-wayland.sh attempt = ~6s twice, well past Monado internal WMR_DISPLAY_INIT_SLEEP_SECONDS=2. Hardened jack-in-wayland.sh (scripts/ + ~/vr/ synced): replaced blind panel.py off+sleep with an explicit activate-then-poll-sysfs-for-connected loop (up to 10s) BEFORE starting monado-service at all, so Monado only starts once the connector is already up instead of racing its own fixed internal wait. Re-ran the 10-cycle loop from scratch with the fix.
driver: Validate the fix removes the intermittent no-connectors failure, and complete the T043 controller-reconnect stress test that was deferred pending the rev2A cable (now downgraded per T048-T049).
veredicto: 10/10 cycles: USB reported 5/5 and a display mode was taken every time, zero no-connectors failures after the preflight fix -- the intermittent DP race appears solved. HOWEVER cycle 10 is a corrected false positive on closer log inspection: it logged 'Did not find HoloLens Sensors companion device' x2 and 'No builder was certain that it could create a head device', falling back to Monado's legacy 'Simulated HMD' builder -- which still leases DP-1 and logs 'found display mode' (since the connector was already up from the preflight activate), making it indistinguishable from a real success under the test script's grep-only check. This is a NEW false-positive trap: 'found display mode' alone does not prove the real WMR headset was used, only that some compositor backend got a connector. Real success requires also seeing 'Using builder wmr' (not 'Using builder legacy'/'Simulated HMD') in the log. So the corrected tally is 9/10 genuine WMR successes, 1/10 silent fallback to a simulated device -- root cause of that one miss not yet isolated (candidate: the fixed 2s gap between kill -9 and restart in the test harness may be too short for the companion's hidraw node to fully settle after teardown, unrelated to the DP/panel fix). All 10 cycles gave a clean SIGTERM teardown regardless.

modo: Same 10-cycle run as T050: controller registration checked per cycle via jack-in-wayland.log
driver: Complete the T043 controller-reconnect stress test: with both controllers powered on before every service start (the only condition that works per T043 -- hot-add does not exist), do both consistently register?
veredicto: NOT reproduced as expected: across all 9 genuine WMR cycles (see T050 for why cycle 10 is excluded), the LEFT controller registered every time ('left: HP Reverb G2 Left Controller') but the RIGHT controller NEVER did ('right: <none>'), despite the user confirming physically both controllers were powered on and showing synced/steady LEDs throughout (their words: 'yo los veo sincronizados en cuanto a la luz', 'ambos encendidos') -- ruling out a physical/pairing problem on the controller side. Root cause read directly from the log: Monado's device-builder prints its final 'Got devices' / role-assignment list EARLY in startup, and the right controller's own config read ('Reading configuration for controller serial a85k641053004dr... Reading right controller config') completes AFTER that list is already finalized -- it starts reading successfully, it is just consistently too slow to make the cutoff. Both controllers share one HID tunnel through the headset (docs/03), reads are sequential, and left appears to reliably win the race to be read first, every cycle. This is a race in the bounded startup wait (patch 0005, 3s window per docs/03), not a hardware or pairing fault -- distinct from T043's BT-layer flakiness anecdote (which was about occasional missed vibration acks, not a systematic loser). Candidate fix, not attempted: read/poll both controllers in parallel or round-robin instead of strictly sequential, or don't finalize the device list until both have responded or the window truly elapses. Left unfixed this session -- flagging for whoever next touches patches/monado's controller startup path.

modo: Real audio playback test: 440Hz test tones via paplay direct to alsa_output.usb-Generic_USB_Audio-00.analog-stereo, headset worn, 3s then 10s at 25% then 90% volume
driver: User flagged 2026-08-07 that audio 'activated' unexpectedly during the controller cycle test and asked for a thorough diagnosis plus an always-available way to lower volume -- audio playback quality had never actually been tested end-to-end in this project, only USB topology.
veredicto: False alarm, resolved fast: PipeWire/ALSA side was correct the whole time (paplay stream drained cleanly at 90% volume, zero underruns/glitches, sink connected, no errors) -- user simply had the G2's off-ear speakers folded up/away from the ears. Lowering them into listening position immediately fixed it, user: 'ahora si! de 10 che'. Also incidentally caught a REAL spontaneous fault while testing: the USB2 branch (hub+audio+companion) disconnected and re-enumerated entirely on its own mid-session (journalctl: 05:22:32-35, no panel/service cycling in progress at the time) -- confirms the marginal-contact recurrence (T039/T044) can happen at idle, not only during panel power transitions. Added ./scripts/hmd-audio.sh (mute/unmute/status/set, resolves the sink by name via wpctl so it survives PipeWire re-numbering the sink on every USB2 re-enumeration) for fast mute access, synced to ~/vr/. Still open: whether audio itself glitches/drops during an active USB2-branch dropout mid-playback (not tested -- this session's dropout happened between tests, not during one), and full mic-path testing (untested).

modo: Correction of T052 + live capture of an active USB2-branch reconnect storm on iashur, nothing running (no monado-service, no panel.py, no test loop)
driver: User corrected T052's verdict: the G2 has no proximity sensor near the off-ear speakers (confirmed: the only proximity sensor is WMR_CONTROL_MSG_IPD_VALUE, near the nose bridge for wear detection, per docs/12 -- unrelated to audio), and reported hearing it reconnecting roughly every 4s during the test, which is the actual explanation for the intermittent audio, not speaker position.
veredicto: T052's 'off-ear speaker position' explanation is WRONG and retracted -- coincidence, not causation (the position change happened to bracket a moment the branch was connected). Real mechanism, confirmed live via journalctl -k: the USB2 branch (hub 04b4:6506 + audio 0bda:4c15 + companion 03f0:0580) reconnected 66 times in the preceding 60 minutes, and while writing this entry it was actively cycling on its own with literally nothing running on the machine -- 05:27:19, :25, :36, :48 (roughly 6-12s apart), companion transiently missing from lsusb (4/5) mid-storm. This is a live, ongoing, unprompted degradation, denser than anything characterized in T039/T044/T046 -- those were single isolated events, this is a sustained rapid-cycling storm at idle. User declined a live touch-the-connector correlation test (wanted to keep moving), so cause within the connector vs. further down the cable is not discriminated this time. Practical effect on audio: PipeWire creates/destroys the ALSA sink on every cycle, so any in-progress or about-to-start playback has a real chance of hitting a disconnected window -- this fully explains the intermittent 'no escucho nada' before without needing any speaker-position theory. Revises the T048/T049 optimism: 'activate resolves the cold-boot dead panel' is still true and validated, but it does NOT mean the underlying marginal-contact fragility (USB2/audio/companion) is resolved or even calmed down -- if anything this storm is denser than prior sessions. Practical read: the rev2A cable recommendation should not be considered fully retired; treat it as still-open pending whether this storm is a one-off or the new baseline.

modo: hmd-watch.py standalone test (no Monado running), headset worn, USB2 branch mid-storm (T053)
driver: User asked whether the proximity sensor tooling (hmd-watch.py, docs/12 line 304) actually works -- it had only ever been listed as a tool in docs/12, never validated with a real test entry.
veredicto: Partially working, proximity half is not: the motion/gyro side (HoloLens Sensors 045e:0659, USB3 branch, unaffected by the USB2 storm) worked cleanly -- calibrated a rest baseline (~22) and read gyro energy with no errors across two runs. The proximity side (companion 03f0:0580 report 0x01) never produced data in any of 3 attempts (20s passive read, 20s passive read after re-finding the re-enumerated hidraw node, and 15s passive read immediately after a fresh panel.py activate()) -- 'proximity=no data' every time. A manual active HIDIOCGFEATURE(0x01) probe also failed with ETIMEDOUT (distinct from the -1/EIO seen in prior HID failures), suggesting report 0x01 either isn't retrievable via GFEATURE at all, or the companion only pushes it as a passive input report under conditions this standalone test isn't meeting. Leading theory, not confirmed: the companion needs Monado's own driver thread actively servicing the shared HID channel for this report to start flowing, not just the activate() sequence panel.py replicates -- panel.py's activate() is a subset of what wmr_hmd.c does, not the full picture. Confounded by T053's active USB2 storm happening at the same time (companion hidraw node changed number mid-test twice), so a clean retest once the branch is calm would be worth doing before concluding this is a real gap vs. a storm artifact. Not fixed or root-caused this session.

modo: Proximity/IPD validation with real Monado running (WMR_LOG=debug added, otherwise same env as jack-in-wayland.sh mode 1), user attempted a cover/uncover gesture on the sensor
driver: Follow-up to T054: does Monado itself receive proximity data when its own driver thread services the companion HID channel, unlike the standalone hmd-watch.py test which got nothing?
veredicto: Root cause found, and it is worse than 'only logs on change': control_read_packets() in wmr_hmd.c is continuously failing with os_hid_read returning -1 on the companion control channel, logged every poll cycle for the full ~35s window (including through the user's cover/uncover gesture) -- Monado never receives a single proximity/IPD packet to decode, let alone log a change. This is NOT a standalone-tool limitation (T054's hypothesis) -- the real WMR driver has the exact same problem live. Matches the 'enumerates but all HID I/O returns -1' failure mode first characterized in T043, confirming the marginal contact (T053's storm) is currently in a bad state for the companion's CONTROL endpoint specifically, even while lsusb still reports 5/5 devices present. Proximity sensor status: UNTESTED as working, not confirmed broken by design -- just currently unreachable due to the live cable/connector degradation. Worth retrying once/if the branch calms down. Killed the ad-hoc WMR_LOG=debug test service afterward.

modo: 3x 60s windows on iashur, counting usb 3-2 (USB2 branch) disconnects via journalctl -k: (1) idle, nothing running; (2) 440Hz test tone via paplay on the USB Audio sink; (3) full stack up (jack-in-wayland.sh mode 1) + play360.sh on the playlist-test directory
driver: User's request: does audio load affect USB2 disconnect frequency, and does video+audio together behave differently -- their recollection is 'never worked, always one or the other, never both'. Wanted a controlled comparison.
veredicto: Counts: idle=1, audio-tone-only=0, Monado+video session=5 disconnects in their respective 60s windows. IMPORTANT correction to the test's premise: play360.sh/hello_xr's video path is SILENT today (docs/02 line 248: 'Video audio (silent today; decode->PipeWire + A/V sync)' is listed as not-yet-implemented) -- so no configuration in this project can currently produce simultaneous video+audio-from-the-video through the player; the user's 'never worked, always one or the other' memory is consistent with that being a known, currently-unimplemented feature, not an intermittent bug. What was actually compared is idle vs. a standalone audio stream vs. a full Monado/OpenXR video session (silent). The correlation that emerges: running the full Monado pipeline (companion HID activation/keepalive, USB3 camera-less streaming, GPU load) correlates with more USB2-branch disconnects than either idle or a lightweight audio-only load -- consistent with the docs/06 'hub reset scales with panel/HID load' mechanism and T043's 'panel-activation power transitions trigger the third failure mode', not with audio specifically. Sample size is small (one 60s window per condition, single run) -- not a rigorous statistical result, just a first-pass signal pointing at Monado/panel activity as the aggravating factor over audio.

modo: 60s window, Monado+video session AND a simultaneous separate audio stream (paplay tone) both running at once, same USB2-disconnect counting method as T056
driver: Continue the T056 comparison with the realistic combined-load case: video session running while a desktop audio stream also plays through the headset speakers (a normal real-world usage pattern, e.g. music while watching silent VR video).
veredicto: 8 disconnects in 60s -- higher than video-alone (5, T056), audio-alone (0, T056), or idle (1, T056). Trend across all 4 conditions this session: idle=1 < audio-only=0 < video-only=5 < video+audio=8. Small sample (1 window per condition) so not statistically rigorous, but consistent and monotonic with 'more concurrent USB/HID load on the shared companion channel -> more disconnects' -- fits the existing docs/06 hub-reset-scales-with-load mechanism. User separately clarified (important cross-platform data point): audio never worked well on WINDOWS either with this unit, historically -- not a Linux/driver-specific complaint. Combined with T053's live spontaneous storm and T055's control-channel read failures, this continues to point at unit-specific physical-layer degradation rather than software. User's framing going forward: less about chasing a fix, more about cataloging every failure mode and its diagnostic procedure for future reference, given they suspect this is specific to their physical unit.

modo: Mic path test: 5s parecord from alsa_input.usb-Generic_USB_Audio-00.analog-stereo, then playback verification via two different paths (paplay to the sink, then VLC on the raw file)
driver: User wanted the mic tested -- never validated before in this project, USB2 branch was calmer (~1 disconnect/30s) but not fully idle.
veredicto: Mic capture WORKS: 5s recording captured real signal (ffmpeg volumedetect: -30.2dB mean, -15.2dB peak, clearly not silence), user's voice audible when finally played back. But getting there exposed a real trap: TWO separate paplay attempts targeting the USB Audio sink by name (once right after recording, once with --verbose showing a completely clean stream -- connected, 0 errors, drained normally) produced NO audible sound, confirmed by the user twice. Only playing the raw file in VLC (installed mid-session) actually produced sound. Leading theory: with the USB2 branch re-enumerating this often (T053), PipeWire recreates the sink object on every cycle: paplay/pactl/wpctl can report a live, healthy-looking connection to a sink name that is actually a stale node no longer backed by a real ALSA device at the moment audio is pushed -- 'stream drained cleanly' is not proof the physical device received it. Practical rule: on this unit, verify audio with an independent player (VLC) hitting the raw file, not paplay-reported success, whenever the USB2 branch has been reconnecting.

modo: Mic capture (10s parecord) WHILE a Monado video session is actively running (play360.sh playlist, same load as T056/T057 video condition)
driver: Does mic capture survive concurrent load on the shared USB2/HID channel, or does it glitch/corrupt like the companion control channel did (T055)?
veredicto: Clean: real signal captured (-35.6dB mean, -15.5dB peak, consistent with the T058 baseline's -30.2/-15.2dB, not silence or corrupted noise), saved to ~/mic-under-load.wav for independent VLC verification per the T058 lesson (do not trust paplay-reported success alone). One data point, not exhaustively verified for glitches/dropouts within the recording, only that overall signal was present and non-trivial.

modo: Full Basalt SLAM build from scratch (it had never actually been compiled in this ~/vr checkout -- CMakeCache existed but no build.ninja/no .so) + WMR_SLAM=1 monado-service + hello_xr with HELLO_XR_POSE_STATS=1, headset stationary on the table
driver: User recalled getting the SLAM cameras working before and asked whether it was still in the repo. Found it was never actually built here: missing deps (libbz2-dev liblz4-dev libssl-dev, then libepoxy-dev libyaml-cpp-dev libsqlite3-dev, none previously fully documented together), user installed them via sudo, configure+build succeeded (146/146 ninja targets, libbasalt.so.2.0.1 produced).
veredicto: SLAM tracker loads and starts cleanly: 'WMR HMD SLAM tracker successfully started', cam_count=4 (all four fisheye tracking cameras in use). hello_xr reports System Tracking Properties: OrientationTracking=True PositionTracking=True (real 6DoF, not the 3DoF-only IMU path used everywhere else in this project). 20s stationary-on-table measurement: inter-frame rotation mean 0.0013-0.0056 deg, max 0.04-0.14 deg, rock stable across the whole window, steady 90fps -- comparable to the historical 3DoF jitter floor and showing NONE of docs/06's documented '~3 deg mean error, det(Q1Jl)==0 divergence spam'. That entry is now stale/contradicted -- likely explanation: this is a fresh Basalt build (whatever upstream commit 'git clone --recursive' pulled today), not necessarily the same version whose divergence was measured originally, and this checkout's basalt had literally never been compiled before today (configure itself was failing on missing epoxy/yaml-cpp/sqlite3 deps, so no verified data existed in THIS repo/machine). NOT yet tested: real head movement / worn tracking quality, drift over a longer session, or whether this holds up under the marginal-USB2-contact instability documented all session (T053) since the tracking cameras are on the USB3 SuperSpeed branch, unaffected by that specific storm. docs/06's Basalt-diverges entry needs a stale-marker note pointing here.

modo: Wired 6DoF into the real supported path: jack-in-wayland.sh now takes a second arg (3dof default, 6dof) instead of hardcoding WMR_SLAM=0/WMR_CAMERAS=0, checks libbasalt.so exists before promising 6dof, and sets VIT_SYSTEM_LIBRARY_PATH automatically. Then a 25s hello_xr HELLO_XR_POSE_STATS run via ./jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof, headset WORN with real head movement (previous T060 was stationary-on-table only).
driver: Close the two gaps T060 left open: SLAM was only reachable by bypassing the supported script by hand, and only tested at rest. Confirm the real jack-in-wayland.sh path works with 6dof and that tracking holds up under actual head movement, not just idle jitter.
veredicto: Both confirmed. ./jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof brings up the full stack cleanly through the normal script (cam_count=4 logged, DP lease + 4320x2160@90 taken same as always). With the headset worn and moved for the ~25s window: inter-frame rotation mean 0.20-1.05 deg, peaks 0.5-1.86 deg during head turns, steady 90fps throughout, zero det(Q1Jl)==0 divergence lines in the whole log. Magnitude is comparable to the historical 3DoF-with-real-movement baseline (T045: mean up to 1.5 deg, peaks 2.9 deg) -- 6DoF SLAM is not obviously worse than 3DoF-only during motion, and shows none of docs/06's old divergence signature. Clean SIGTERM teardown. 6dof is now usable via the normal, documented entry point instead of a one-off manual monado-service invocation.

modo: monado-service crashed with SIGSEGV during earlier SLAM/6DoF testing (T060-T061), noticed only retroactively via coredumpctl
driver: Discovered while investigating an unrelated xrizer RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE error -- coredumpctl list showed a monado-service SIGSEGV coredump timestamped 06:29:07, which falls right in the middle of the T060/T061 SLAM work, previously unnoticed since a fresh jack-in-wayland.sh run afterward silently started a new working instance.
veredicto: A real, previously-unnoticed monado-service crash occurred during this session's SLAM testing window, distinct from the known USB2-storm-related failures. Not investigated in depth (session had moved on to other work by the time it was found) -- only established that it happened and roughly when. A second historical monado-service SIGSEGV coredump also exists from 2026-08-04 19:59:42, meaning this isn't the first time. Practical note for future sessions: run 'coredumpctl list' periodically or at session end, not just when something visibly breaks -- a silent Monado crash followed by a routine restart can hide real bugs.

modo: Full xrizer (OpenVR-on-OpenXR) setup and test attempt: installed Steam (user, via apt with i386 multiarch), fixed 3 rounds of missing i386 NVIDIA GLX packages, installed Rust via rustup, cloned+built xrizer (fixed 2 more missing deps: libclang-dev for bindgen, glslc for shader compilation), wrote openvrpaths.vrpath pointing at the built xrizer, then tried 2 Steam-installed OpenVR titles: NVIDIA VR Funhouse (Windows-only via Proton, blocked immediately by an unrelated GPU PhysX/CUDA error) and InCell VR (native Linux Unity build, reproducibly SIGABRT crashes inside VR_InitInternal).
driver: User wanted SteamVR/xrizer tested -- docs/06 had this marked 'not tested yet' since SteamVR's own vrmonitor is broken (missing libQt5Multimedia.so.5). xrizer bypasses vrmonitor entirely by reimplementing OpenVR on top of OpenXR/Monado directly.
veredicto: xrizer itself builds and mostly works -- real progress, not a dead end: (1) fixed and documented a genuine i386 NVIDIA package trap (glx-alternative-nvidia:i386 was missing; libgl1-nvidia-glvnd-glx:i386 is the WRONG package for the 595 driver series -- it only exists at 550, causing a version conflict; nvidia-driver-libs:i386 alone is correct). (2) fixed and documented that nothing on this system registers libopenxr_loader.so system-wide (no ldconfig entry) -- xrizer's dynamic Entry::load() can't find it without LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing at ~/vr/OpenXR-SDK-Source/build/src/loader, which is why the first InCell attempt logged 'InstanceCreationFailed(ERROR_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE)' in xrizer.txt despite monado-service running and healthy (verified: hello_xr connected fine to the exact same running service at the exact same time). NVIDIA VR Funhouse never reached the VR init step at all -- blocked earlier by a GPU PhysX/CUDA availability error inside its Proton prefix, unrelated to xrizer/VR and not investigated (out of scope, orthogonal to what's being tested). veredicto:
InMind VR: user confirmed physically what the crash analysis predicted (T064) -- a blank grey 2D window on the desktop monitor, backlight-only on the headset panel, no real content either place. Consistent, not a new finding.

SUPERHOT VR (Proton): shows in 2D on the desktop monitor, panel backlight-only in the headset -- same visual symptom, different root cause. xrizer's log showed a FRESH attempt (07:10:23, later 07:13:53) failing with the same ERROR_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE as the native titles, even after two real fixes: (1) adding LD_LIBRARY_PATH to the Steam launch options (identical result), (2) installing the system-wide libopenxr-loader1 package via apt so no LD_LIBRARY_PATH should even be needed (identical result again, confirmed loader registered via ldconfig). Root cause: Proton/Steam titles run inside Valve's Steam Linux Runtime container (pressure-vessel/bwrap), which sandboxes the process environment -- XR_RUNTIME_JSON set via Steam launch options is not reaching the sandboxed process at all, and there's no system-wide /etc/xdg/openxr/1/active_runtime.json to fall back on either. This is a DIFFERENT failure class from InCell/InMind's native-process crashes -- it's a container/sandboxing gap on our end, not an xrizer bug. xrizer's own README documents that Steam Linux Runtime needs special handling (PRESSURE_VESSEL_FILESYSTEMS_RW for filesystem paths) but doesn't cover this exact env-var-passthrough case; not resolved this session.

FINAL STATUS across the whole VR-games sweep (T063-T065): every title tried (Funhouse, InCell, InMind, SUPERHOT) failed to reach a real VR session, for THREE distinct reasons -- (a) Funhouse: unrelated Proton/PhysX/CUDA error before VR init; (b) InCell: reproducible xrizer VR_InitInternal/dlclose crash on a native process; (c) InMind: unrelated Mono runtime crash before touching VR; (d) SUPERHOT: Proton/pressure-vessel container not passing XR_RUNTIME_JSON through, so xrizer never finds Monado at all. None of these four failures share a single root cause -- fixing one would not fix the others. xrizer as a SteamVR replacement is NOT usable on this rig with any tested title tonight. What IS solidly reusable: the full toolchain (Steam, Rust, xrizer build, system libopenxr-loader1, openvrpaths.vrpath) for whoever debugs this further, plus three concretely diagnosed and documented failure modes instead of a vague 'doesn't work'.

modo: Real code fix for T051: the right-controller startup race in wmr_hmd.c, found by reading the source after the SUPERHOT/xrizer session exposed it as a blocker (no right-hand input = SUPERHOT never progresses past the intro)
driver: User wanted the right-controller registration bug (T051) actually fixed, not just documented, once it became a real blocker for the first working xrizer session (SUPERHOT VR).
veredicto: Root cause found and fixed. wmr_hmd.c ~line 2090, the bounded 3s controller-status wait used 'while (!have_left && !have_right && before_deadline)' -- De Morgan's law makes this exit the INSTANT EITHER flag becomes true (since !true=false breaks the AND chain), not when BOTH are true. So the loop always returned right after the first controller (observed: always left) answered, never giving the second one (right) a chance within its own bounded wait -- explains the 9/9 reproduction in T051. Fixed to 'while ((!have_left || !have_right) && before_deadline)' -- now waits for BOTH controllers (still bounded by the same 3s deadline, so a genuinely absent controller still doesn't hang startup). Rebuilt Monado clean (ninja, no errors). Verified twice: Monado's own device list now shows 'right: HP Reverb G2 Right Controller' (previously always <none>), and xrizer/SUPERHOT's log shows both hands with a real interaction profile (/interaction_profiles/oculus/touch_controller) instead of right being <null>. This is a genuine upstream-quality bug fix, not a workaround -- candidate for the Monado patch set (patches/monado) and worth upstreaming per docs/18.

modo: 10x jack-in-wayland.sh 1 3dof back-to-back (~10-15s apart: SIGTERM teardown + 3s + 4s cooldown between cycles), controllers left powered the whole time, scripted via scripts/stress-jack-in.sh (scratchpad)

veredicto: 1/10 auto-ok, 9/10 FAIL -- much worse than T068's 2/3. Every failing cycle showed USB rock solid at 5/5 (no companion/audio/hub dropout, rules out the T052-T053 USB2-storm pattern as the cause here) but DP-1/2/3 stayed disconnected past the script's 10s post-activation window every time, so compositor init failed with 'Found no connectors available for direct mode' and the script exited cleanly (no broken service left running, confirmed zero leftover monado processes and no stale IPC socket after the batch). A manual scripts/panel.py activate run immediately after the batch DID recover DP-1 -- but took 6s this time, vs 2s the first time it was tried in this session (T068 prelude). Working hypothesis, not confirmed: back-to-back cycling without enough idle time between attempts pushes the activate-to-hotplug latency close to or past the script's fixed 10s bound -- a real behavioral gap, not obviously the same visor-connector fault as T039/T052 (USB stayed clean throughout, which those storms never did). Important methodology caveat: this is NOT the same test as the user's Windows comparison -- that was ~4 full OS reboots minutes apart; this was 10 rapid same-boot service restarts seconds apart. Not yet apples-to-apples. Open next steps, not yet decided with the user: (a) widen the script's activation-wait window and inter-cycle cooldown and rerun, (b) a slower cycle (e.g. 60-120s apart) to separate 'needs recovery time' from 'genuinely unreliable', (c) actual reboot-based repetition to match the Windows methodology exactly.

veredicto: Spacing did NOT help: 1/8 auto-ok, 7/8 fail -- statistically indistinguishable from T069's 1/10. Rules out 'needs more idle time between cycles' as the explanation. New and more useful finding, found by chance while investigating: running scripts/panel.py activate BY HAND, standalone, immediately after one of the batch's failures reliably brought DP-1 up within 2-6s, 3/3 times across this session (T068 prelude + twice more here) -- and this is the exact same command (python3 panel.py activate) that jack-in-wayland.sh itself calls internally (jack-in-wayland.sh:83) with the same 10s/20x0.5s poll afterward (jack-in-wayland.sh:84-90). So the identical activation call is ~3/3 reliable when I run it manually right after a failure, but the scripted in-sequence call inside jack-in-wayland.sh is failing ~2/18 total across both stress batches. This points at something in the script's own sequencing around the call -- not the raw hardware responsiveness, which manual testing shows is fine -- most likely candidate: jack-in-wayland.sh:67 unconditionally SIGKILLs any still-detected monado-service and only sleeps 2s before calling activate (vs. this stress harness's own prior-cycle teardown already having done a clean SIGTERM+3s wait, so there normally shouldn't be a live process for that kill -9 to hit, but the interaction is unconfirmed). NOT root-caused yet -- flagging for next session: add timestamps around the kill -9/sleep 2/activate sequence in jack-in-wayland.sh and log exactly what's racing. Practical workaround available right now: run scripts/panel.py activate by hand before jack-in-wayland.sh instead of relying on its internal call.

modo: Root-caused via instrumented jack-in-wayland.sh (timestamps + captured panel.py stdout/stderr instead of discarding to /dev/null), then fixed at the source (scripts/jack-in-wayland.sh) and synced to the lab copy (~/vr/)
driver: User explicitly asked for a real fix, not a workaround -- repeated cable/connector touching shortens the life of a headset with no spare, and blocks other projects depending on this rig. Wanted the actual bug found even if it took more validation.
veredicto: ROOT CAUSE FOUND, not hardware: ~/vr/panel.py did not exist -- only patches/reverb-g2's scripts/panel.py did. jack-in-wayland.sh resolves PANEL_PY relative to its own location (dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"), which works in the repo (panel.py sits right next to it in scripts/) but NOT in the lab's flat ~/vr/ deployment, where panel.py was never copied over. Every single automated 'python3 $PANEL_PY activate' call in T069/T070 (and likely earlier, going back to whenever T050's pre-activation feature was deployed to the lab) was silently failing with 'can't open file ... No such file or directory' -- confirmed by capturing stdout/stderr instead of discarding them (previously '>/dev/null 2>&1' swallowed the error completely). The panel was NEVER actually told to activate on any of those runs; the one success in every batch was residual state from a manual activate moments earlier, not the script working. Zero relation to the visor-end cable/connector -- USB was clean throughout every failing cycle in T069/T070, consistent with this explanation and inconsistent with a connector fault. FIX: copied panel.py to ~/vr/panel.py, and hardened scripts/jack-in-wayland.sh (synced to ~/vr/) to surface any panel.py failure loudly instead of swallowing it, so this exact silent-failure class can't hide behind a fake 'DP never came up' hardware-looking symptom again. VERIFIED: 6/6 clean automatic DP hotplug + compositor start, 15s apart, right after the fix (vs. 1/10 and 1/8 before it). Controllers did NOT register on the last verification cycles (Got devices showed only the HMD, no controller config reads attempted at all) -- after ~1h+ of repeated cycling with zero physical controller interaction, almost certainly the controllers auto-slept from inactivity, not a regression; needs the user to wake/re-power them to confirm, separate from this fix.

This is a narrow, well-defined upstream gap (one missing version adapter), not a fundamental incompatibility -- Poly Runner VR is presumably an old (~2016-era) title built against exactly that version. Not fixed this session -- flagging as a candidate small patch to xrizer if the user wants one (the 012On014 shim right above it is a plausible template), otherwise just move to a different untested title. modo: War Robots VR: The Skirmish (672640), same pacing as T075-T077
driver: Continue the confirmed-good shortlist.
veredicto: BLOCKED, not just limited: game shows a persistent 'put on your VR helmet' prompt and never progresses, even with the headset actually worn -- user's words: 'venia bien' before that prompt. Read xrizer's source (~/vr/xrizer/src/system.rs): it does NOT implement HMD worn/presence detection at all -- ShouldApplicationPause() is hardcoded to return false and IsInputAvailable() hardcoded to return true, neither wired to any real signal. Monado's WMR driver DOES read the headset's real proximity sensor (wmr_hmd.c/.h, wh->proximity_sensor, exposed in the debug GUI) but that value never reaches xrizer/the game -- no presence-related symbol anywhere in xrizer's source. Likely explanation, not 100% proven (didn't instrument to confirm which exact OpenVR call War Robots polls): the game is waiting on a real presence/mounted signal that xrizer can only ever answer with a stub value, so it never sees a 'worn' transition. Distinct failure class from T072 (missing interface version) and T076's recenter question -- this is a missing FEATURE in xrizer (presence passthrough), not a missing interface shim or a calibration issue. Candidate fix, not attempted: wire xrizer's presence stubs to Monado's own XR_EXT_user_presence extension (already plumbed generically in oxr_session.c/oxr_event.c/oxr_system.c for other drivers) if wmr_hmd.c exposes proximity_sensor through it -- needs checking whether wmr's OpenXR-level user-presence wiring exists or only the raw HID field does. CLARIFIED by user right after logging: the game is not blocked from the start -- real 3D content DID show, and the user completed an in-game stick-driven calibration step successfully. The hang happens immediately AFTER that calibration finishes: headset drops to backlight-only and the un-skippable 'put on headset' prompt appears on the 2D mirror. Refines the theory: the trigger is a state transition right after calibration (likely the game re-checking presence/focus as part of that transition), not a stuck-from-frame-one presence check -- still consistent with xrizer's stubbed ShouldApplicationPause/IsInputAvailable never being able to report a real 'worn' signal once something puts the game into that waiting state.

veredicto: Two-part patch, both needed: (1) src/input.rs -- added Input<C>::system_recenter_hold/system_recenter_fired state and a call to a new legacy::check_system_recenter_hold() from frame_start_update's legacy-actions branch (runs once per frame for any game using the legacy GetControllerState API, confirmed VRSailing is one via absence of a 'loading action manifest' log line). (2) src/input/legacy.rs -- the actual hold-detection + firing logic, reading the existing app_menu action's state per-hand and calling self.openxr.reset_tracking_space(Standing) once 3s of continuous hold elapses (env override XRIZER_RECENTER_HOLD_SECS). FIRST ATTEMPT DIDN'T FIRE: app_menu on the oculus/touch_controller profile (what our WMR controllers present as) is bound to Y/B face buttons only (src/input/profiles/oculus_touch.rs) -- the REAL physical WMR menu button (Left<Menu,Click>, already a legal path on this profile, just never wired to app_menu) was never checked. Added it as a third app_menu binding source. Rebuilt (cargo build --release, clean, no warnings) and retested on VRSailing (T079's blocked-by-distance title): CONFIRMED WORKING -- user's words 'Resed works!' after holding the real menu button. Not yet fixed -- open question for the user whether to redo the game's height calibration post-recenter (works, just an extra step) or have the patch preserve Y/height and only reset X/Z + yaw (would need touching openxr_data.rs::reset_tracking_space itself, a shared function also used by the real ResetZeroPose/ResetSeatedZeroPose OpenVR calls, so a riskier change). This patch lives only in the local ~/vr/xrizer checkout -- not upstreamed, not on a named branch yet.

modo: About to write a patch for T072's 'missing IVRCompositor_013 shim' -- checked xrizer's vendored OpenVR headers (openvr/headers/) first, covering every SDK version Valve ever shipped, 0.9.12 through 2.15.6, before writing any code.
driver: Before touching xrizer's compositor interface dispatch, wanted to see the exact shape of the 012/014 gap the T072 diagnosis was built on, to know what a 013On014 shim should actually adapt between.
veredicto: T072's diagnosis was WRONG in its central claim. There is no IVRCompositor_013 -- confirmed exhaustively across every vendored header: 'IVRCompositor_Version' jumps directly from '_012' (openvr-0.9.17.h) to '_014' (openvr-0.9.20.h) in Valve's own SDK history, with no header in between ever defining 013. xrizer's 012On014 compatibility impl isn't a gap where a 013-specific shim is missing -- it's correctly named, because 012 and 014 really are adjacent real versions. Poly Runner VR requesting 'IVRCompositor_013' would fail against genuine Valve SteamVR too, on any version, forever -- it's asking for something that was never real. Near-certain explanation: this is routine version-probing (try v14, fall back to v13, fall back to v12...) that a well-behaved game does defensively, and failing on 013 specifically is expected/harmless, not the actual reason the session exits moments later in T072's log. CORRECTED: docs/pruebas.jsonl T072 stands as the historical record of the (wrong) diagnosis; patches/xrizer/README.md carries the correction going forward. Not fixed this session -- Poly Runner VR's REAL exit cause is still unknown and needs fresh log investigation from scratch, not an interface-version patch (there is nothing to patch against). Session's actual xrizer patch effort went to the global recenter feature instead (T080), which the user prioritized higher anyway.

modo: Root-caused why SUPERHOT's menu never opens, despite T082 confirming raw input is 100% healthy at the Monado level (debug GUI: trigger, squeeze, menu, bt_pairing, Y/B all register correctly on both hands).
driver: With hardware/driver ruled out by T082's debug GUI check, the remaining candidates were xrizer's translation layer or a binding mismatch -- needed to read the actual manifests, not guess.
veredicto: Found via SUPERHOT's own Unity log (output_log.txt): 'No active binding for SetupOpenAction (/actions/default/in/MENU)' spammed every frame. Traced the chain: SUPERHOT's actions.json defines a modern MENU action (not the legacy GetControllerState path); its default oculus_touch bindings (bindings_oculus_touch.json) offer exactly two sources for it -- a 'long' press on X, and a click on 'system' (/user/hand/*/input/system) -- and xrizer supports NEITHER: (1) 'long' as a button input mode doesn't exist anywhere in xrizer's action-manifest parser (ButtonInput in action_manifest/bindings.rs only has touch/click/double fields; serde silently drops unknown keys, no error), (2) 'system' was never a recognized subpath string in DynSubpath::from_openvr_str (src/input/profiles.rs) -- grepped all of src/input/, zero matches for 'system' as a path component anywhere. Both of SUPERHOT's MENU sources fail to resolve, hence the action stays permanently unbound. Not a WMR/G2-specific issue -- would affect any controller presented as oculus_touch.

modo: Wrote and tested a real patch to xrizer fixing the 'system' half of T083's finding: aliased the OpenVR-legacy 'system' path string to the already-legal Menu subpath in DynSubpath::from_openvr_str, one line, following the exact precedent already in that function (application_menu is already aliased to Menu a few lines above). modo: Live headset verification of the new digital-zoom patch (patches/hello_xr-player/0007), built and keyboard-smoke-tested earlier the same session. Played two clips through play360.sh with monado-service already up: stereo3d-pack/in/01pjni8u.mp4 (forced -p flat) and stereo3d-pack/out/03ehybrp_sbs.mp4 (forced -p flat -e sbs, per the known flat-SBS-misdetected-as-panoramic gap already documented in docs/02).
driver: Zoom (thumbstick Y) had only been verified against real hardware for OpenXR action *binding* (log line, no collision with Seek) and via a keyboard-only fake-pty test -- per this project's core rule, the actual in-headset visual result and the assumed +y=up=zoom-in sign still needed a human with the headset on before counting as done.
veredicto: Zoom itself: fully confirmed, first try, no sign flip needed. User, with the headset on, working the thumbstick live: 'zoom anda perfecto'. Stick up = zoom in, stick down = zoom out, matches the assumed OpenXR/gamepad convention exactly. docs/02 updated to VERIFIED LIVE. Separate, unrelated finding surfaced during the same session, reported by the user directly and NOT yet root-caused: 03ehybrp_sbs.mp4 loses pacing hard (real ~24fps content sustained at roughly 3x) right after its first automatic loop back to the start of the clip -- this is video360.cpp's own single-file DecodeLoop() EOF-restart path, not the playlist multi-file transition. User's working hypothesis: the seek/restart logic doesn't reset the pacing reference clock. Code read (not yet instrumented/reproduced with live numbers): that specific claim doesn't quite match the code as written -- AcquireCurrentSlot() deliberately does NOT reset clockStarted/playbackTime on an automatic loop (only a manual user Seek() does that, via seekPending), and the code comment explains this is intentional, to keep the wall clock monotonic across the loop seam. The more likely suspect given a read of DecodeLoop()/DrainDecoder() is the loopOffset recomputed at every EOF (`loopOffset = lastPts + frameDuration`, video360.cpp ~line 390): if `lastPts` at the exact EOF-flush drain doesn't land on the true final presentation timestamp (plausible if best_effort_timestamp reordering behaves oddly for the last few frames at flush), every post-loop frame gets queued under-offset, and AcquireCurrentSlot's stale-frame-skip loop (skip forward instead of playing slow motion once frames are already 'due') would visually read as a sustained speed-up rather than a one-time jump if the decoder also can't refill the queue fast enough to let it resettle. Worth checking whether it is specific to this file: 03ehybrp_sbs.mp4 already needed a software-decode fallback this same session (cuvidCreateDecoder CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE on NVDEC init), so it's untested whether hardware-decoded clips show the same loop bug. NOT reproduced with instrumented values yet -- next step is a live run with temporary logging of lastPts/loopOffset/elapsed right at the EOF/loop-restart transition (or HELLO_XR_VIDEO_STATS=1 watched closely across a loop boundary on both a hw- and a sw-decoded clip) before touching the fix.

modo: Root-causing and fixing the loop-restart pacing bug the user found and wrote up in stereo3d-pack/BUG_player_loop_speedup_2026-08-09.md -- much better evidenced than the T099 first pass the previous night (real measured upload-fps numbers across a loop boundary, a second reproduction clip with a new visual symptom, and a proposed one-line A/B-testable mitigation).
driver: T099's own guess (bad lastPts at the EOF-flush drain) was explicitly left unconfirmed, needing instrumented numbers before touching a fix -- the user's report supplied a different, better-evidenced hypothesis (their working theory: reset clockStarted on automatic loop, same as the manual-seek path already does) and a concrete repro (stereo3d-pack/out/media_sbs_lowres.mp4, 7.75s/30fps, loops many times per real minute).
veredicto: Applied the user's proposed clockStarted-reset mitigation first (video360.cpp, DecodeLoop()'s EOF path) and measured it live: NOT sufficient on its own -- the bug still reproduced almost identically (sustained ~70-84 fps upload rate vs the file's real 30fps, persisting across most loop boundaries in a 60s run). Added temporary DEBUG instrumentation (queue depth, loopOffset, queue.front().pts, playbackTime at every EOF/loop-restart, plus catch-up-skip counts in AcquireCurrentSlot) and re-ran -- this found the REAL bug: `loopOffset = lastPts + frameDuration` was a plain assignment, not an accumulation. Since `lastPts` is always the file's own raw 0-based last timestamp (naturally near-identical every loop, since the same file is re-read from position 0 each time), the assignment silently discarded every earlier loop's accumulated offset -- confirmed directly in the log: loopOffset stayed pinned at 7.567 (one loop-width) across every single loop-restart instead of growing to 15.13, 22.7, etc. From the second loop onward, every loop's frames were queued under the SAME pts window the previous loop had already caught up to by the time it ended, so they were stale the instant they were queued -- the render's stale-frame-skip logic discarded them in cascading bursts, triggering the next EOF/seek/flush cycle almost immediately, then the next one even faster (loop-restart log lines went from ~7.5s apart to sub-second apart within two loops). Fixed with `loopOffset += lastPts + frameDuration` (accumulate). Kept the clockStarted reset as a smaller complementary fix (handles wall-clock drift from the seek/flush itself, which the loopOffset fix doesn't address, though it's not the dominant effect). Removed all temporary DEBUG logging before committing. VERIFIED (log-based, not yet human-eyes-on-headset): 90s run of the same repro clip, ~12 loop crossings, 44 stat samples all in 29.8-30.4 fps (file is 30.0), decode steady at 30.1fps with 0 renderer starves the entire run -- zero samples outside a tight +-0.4fps band, versus the pre-fix run's sustained 70-84fps. Committed in ~/vr/OpenXR-SDK-Source (44b364b) and exported to patches/hello_xr-player/0008. NOT yet checked: the bug report's second symptom (a vertical 'rolling' visual artifact on a different clip, media.mp4) -- unconfirmed whether that was this same bug manifesting differently or a separate issue; needs a live look with the headset on, this fix was only verified via log stats so far.

veredicto: Speed fix: CONFIRMED with the headset on, playing stereo3d-pack/out/media_sbs_lowres.mp4 for 90s (~12 loops) -- no speedup at any loop boundary. Rolling artifact: user confirmed it is STILL present ('cuando se reinicia queda bien, enseguida arranca a bajar de a poco') -- a real, separate bug from the one just fixed. Investigated graphicsplugin_vulkan.cpp's video-to-skybox upload path first: found it's fully synchronous (UpdateVideoTexture() does Exec()+Wait(), blocking on the GPU every single frame before returning), which rules out a missing-fence/tearing race as the cause -- this pipeline was already correctly serialized. Tested whether TransferDirect (the NVDEC direct-to-staging path, which trusts av_hwframe_transfer_data to honor a tightly-packed linesize without repacking rows) was mishandling this clip's unusual per-eye height (852, not power-of-2-friendly): forced HELLO_XR_VIDEO_HW=0 (software decode, which explicitly repacks every row via NormalizeToNv12) and had the user re-check with the headset on -- rolling still there, identical, ruling out the NVDEC stride path specifically. Final, decisive test: played the exact same file in plain ffplay on the desktop monitor, completely outside OpenXR/Vulkan/this project's code entirely -- USER CONFIRMED the same rolling artifact appears there too. This conclusively proves the defect is baked into the file itself (a stereo3d-pack conversion artifact), not a bug in video360.cpp or graphicsplugin_vulkan.cpp -- an independent, unrelated player reproducing the identical symptom rules out anything on this side by construction. docs/02 updated to close this out and point back to the stereo3d-pack repo instead of tracking it here further.

modo: Root-causing why controller-driven quits ended the XR session (backlight-only) but the process never exited -- so play-with-legend.sh's content phase never started. Diagnosed with gdb attached to a live hang; two real bugs found and fixed; verified live.
driver: User reported repeatedly across several rounds: pressing a button (trigger, or Menu) made the legend image disappear but the video never appeared. Never reproducible via fake-pty keyboard tests (0.06-0.07s clean exits every time), only with the real controller -- which was the diagnostic tell. User explicitly chose to keep digging tonight rather than defer ('Seguir cavando ahora'), then stopped everything on the machine and asked for isolation ('Hay que aislarlo y resolverlo').
veredicto: ISOLATED DEFINITIVELY via gdb -p on the hung process, no bisection or rollback needed -- both thread stacks caught in the act. Thread 1 (main): exit() -> _IO_flush_all() -> __lll_lock_wait_private, waiting on stdin's stdio FILE lock. Thread 2 (our keyboard thread, from patch 0003): parked in getchar() -> read(), HOLDING that same lock, waiting for a keyboard byte that never comes when the quit came from the controller. Guaranteed deadlock inside exit() for every controller-driven quit. Latent since patch 0005 (Menu quit, 2026-08-06), masked by two accidental backstops: timeout --foreground's SIGTERM in interactive runs, and the old 'sleep N |' stdin pipe delivering EOF at N seconds (unblocking the thread LATE -- every prior 'Menu quit worked' was really 'the hang self-resolved before anyone measured it'). Tonight's controller-quit feature made the trigger common and the sleep-infinity stdin change removed the EOF backstop, surfacing it. FIX: keyboard thread reads via raw read(2) (ReadKeyByte() in main.cpp) instead of getchar() -- kernel reads hold no user-space locks, thread parks harmlessly at exit. SECOND BUG, same dig: ~OpenXrProgram() destroyed swapchain/session/instance with GPU work still in flight -- the true source of the vkFreeCommandBuffers/vkDestroySemaphore 'is in use' validation errors on EVERY quit (dismissed all session as harmless shutdown noise; T099 called it pre-existing, which was true, but not harmless). Fixed with IGraphicsPlugin::WaitForGpuIdle() (vkDeviceWaitIdle) first thing in the destructor. THIRD, enabling fix: the quit flag was only watched by the keyboard thread, so controller quits set it and nothing acted -- PollActions() now latches xrRequestExitSession() when QuitRequested() goes true. Also fixed play360.sh's non-interactive mode (pipe made the script block the full -t even after early exit; now timeout on hello_xr directly + sleep-infinity keepalive with explicit kill -- six orphaned keepalives had accumulated from the first version, confirmed cleaned). Verified: fake-pty keyboard tests still pass (keys work, 0.06s clean exit), and the full controller flow live with the headset on -- button press on legend -> content started immediately, user: 'ahora funcionó, el video arrancó al toque'. The successful run also exited cleanly on its own and left zero orphaned processes. Committed as 84bf12a in ~/vr/OpenXR-SDK-Source, exported as patches/hello_xr-player/0012 (bundled with previous-track/X, black theme default, and zoom/brightness no longer flashing the progress bar -- all from the same arc, each verified live except prev-track's backward playlist traversal, still pending a dedicated check).

USB EPISODE: the deliberate service restart (after ~8h uptime) killed the USB2 branch (classic 'Cannot enable... error -71' on usb3-port2, 2/5 devices). Recovery ladder results, all measured: PC-end replug NO; 12V power-cycle alone NO; visor-end reseat + power NO; full xhci controller rebind (software re-enumeration from scratch, confirmed real by Logitech re-enumerating) NO -- the most replug-resistant instance yet; what finally worked was power-cycle + MOVING THE USB TO A DIFFERENT PC PORT (5/5 immediately, devices now on 3-1.x/4-1.x instead of 3-2/4-2). Port-dependence echoes the original docs/06 bad-port saga; ALSO fits the marginal-cable theory (different port = different mechanical seating). Rev2A cable recommendation stays firm. SIMULATED-HMD TRAP, LIVE: with the companion missing, the first restart came up 'Using builder legacy' with 90Hz 'taken' and a granted lease -- exactly the documented indistinguishable-from-success trap; caught only because the check greps 'Using builder' as CLAUDE.md instructs. SLAM DIVERGENCE, NEW DATA: the fresh 6dof session (gravity anchored with headset still, 5/5 USB) diverged anyway -- Basalt spewing numerical-degeneracy cascades (det(Q1Jl)==0 backsubstitution skips, invalid d_res_d_xi/d_res_d_p jacobians), visible as violent position fly-away in Google Earth VR and Aircar plus re-tilting roll after every recenter; room light ON did not help; recenter did not help. T060's 'divergence fixed by clean build' verdict does NOT hold universally -- open hypotheses for next session: the NEW USB port delivering marginal SuperSpeed (camera frames feeding SLAM corrupt/dropped), nighttime room conditions, or calibration; untested. 3dof fallback session: rock solid, zero jitter, both controllers first try -- the pragmatic default for game sessions until the divergence is understood.
