modo: 6dof SLAM divergence, real hypothesis test (retomando T106/T110)
driver: con la rama USB2 ya asentada y estable, probar si la divergencia de Basalt correlaciona con luz nocturna, USB SuperSpeed marginal, o carga de CPU/GPU -- sesion 6dof real con contenido de complejidad creciente: foto estatica primero, luego video VR180 4K pesado
veredicto: HALLAZGO REAL, nueva hipotesis con datos a favor: la divergencia de Basalt escala fuertemente con la carga de decode+render, no con luz de sala ni con USB SuperSpeed marginal (ambas quedan efectivamente descartadas esta sesion: bus 4 -- camaras HoloLens Sensors -- confirmado estable a 5000M SuperSpeed durante toda la sesion; era de tarde/luz natural, no de noche). Progresion medida en el mismo log de una sola sesion 6dof continua: durante el test de foto estatica (test-equirect.jpg, sin decode de video), el warning 'det(Q1Jl) == 0, skipping backsubstitution' aparecia 4370 veces pero sobre solo 3 landmarks DISTINTOS -- loop benigno, no cascada real. Al pasar a reproducir tron_legacy_vr180_4k.mp4 (VR180 4K real, decode+render bajo carga), la cascada exploto: 48182 ocurrencias totales, 1321 landmarks DISTINTOS -- y partiendo el mismo log en tercios por lineas, la diversidad de landmarks fue 185 -> 55 -> 1154, una escalada brusca coincidente con el tramo final (video pesado corriendo). GPU/decoder no estaban saturados (29%/32% via nvidia-smi) pero el load average del sistema subia sostenido (2.99 -> 4.62 -> 8.64 en 15min). Hipotesis: Basalt (SLAM, corre en CPU) se queda sin tiempo de CPU cuando compite con el decode+render de video pesado, degenerando el tracking -- NO es GPU-bound, es contencion de CPU. Verificado fisicamente en vivo por el usuario mientras el video corria: 'esta girando el video constantemente en varias direcciones' -- confirmado que seguia girando incluso despues de preguntarle de nuevo. Bajada la sesion (kill -9 a hello_xr) para no seguir estresando. Pendiente para la proxima sesion: aislar la variable -- probar el MISMO video pesado en sesion 3dof (sin Basalt, sin competir por CPU) para confirmar que el video en si no tiene otro problema, y probar contenido liviano (foto o video chico) en 6dof bajo carga de CPU artificial (ej. stress-ng) para replicar la cascada sin necesitar un video real. Si se confirma, el fix candidato es afinar la prioridad/afinidad de CPU del hilo de Basalt (ya usa SCHED_FIFO segun el log -- 'Raised priority of thread Multi Client Module to policy SCHED_FIFO, priority 99' -- pero puede que el hilo de decode/render este compitiendo por los mismos cores o pisando esa prioridad).

modo: 3dof workaround confirmed for video playback (post-T112)
driver: verificar si el fallback a 3dof (sin Basalt/SLAM) evita la divergencia de T112 durante reproduccion de video real y pesado
veredicto: CONFIRMADO: el fallback a 3dof evita la divergencia de T112 durante reproduccion de video real. Sesion 6dof fresca (post-reseat+power-cycle, USB 5/5 estable) relanzada explicitamente en 3dof (jack-in-wayland.sh 1 3dof, Using builder wmr real, ambos controles registrados) y probada con tres videos VR180/SBS reales y pesados en secuencia: tron_legacy_vr180_4k.mp4 (VR180 4K h264, decode NVDEC 60/60fps estable) -- usuario: 'se ve estable, sin girar'; suicide_squad_midway_sbs.mp4 (plano 3D SBS, 1920x1080 por ojo, 24fps) -- 'se ve bien, sin girar'; blade_runner_skyline_vr180_4k.mp4 (VR180 4K, 1920x1920 por ojo, 60fps) -- 'se ve estable, sin girar'. Cero eventos de rotacion espontanea en los tres, bajo la misma carga de decode+render pesada que en T112 disparo la cascada de divergencia en 6dof. Confirma la hipotesis de T112 (contencion de CPU del hilo de Basalt) por eliminacion: sin Basalt corriendo, sin divergencia, pese a carga identica. Deja establecido el fallback pragmatico ya sugerido en T106 como plan concreto: 3dof para reproduccion de video hasta que se investigue el fix de afinidad/prioridad de CPU pendiente de T112. Nota aparte, no relacionada: en el camino se probo tambien LG QNED 8K MiniLED Shine 8K HDR (contenido HDR10 crudo sin tonemap, deliberadamente saltado el paso de conversion a pedido del usuario) -- el 'parpadeo' reportado ahi fue confirmado por el usuario como destellos de brillo del contenido HDR, no el bug de 60Hz del proyecto (90Hz real confirmado en el log durante esa prueba).

modo: preflight.sh diagnostic overhaul + physical bring-up after visor-end reseat
driver: el usuario pidio ajustar todo el diagnostico para no avisar falso positivo (logo HP prendido/apagado inconsistente en Linux y Windows, sin correlacionar con el panel real) -- usar todas las senales disponibles antes de declarar listo
veredicto: CONFIRMADO fisicamente por el usuario: panel encendido tras reseat en el extremo del visor (el reseat de PC+power solo no habia alcanzado). Hallazgo real durante el trabajo: la heuristica inicial 'EDID truncado a 128 bytes = señal de progreso parcial' era FALSA -- los monitores de escritorio reales de este equipo (conectores 130/134) tambien reportan 128 bytes con listas de modos completamente sanas, asi que el largo del blob EDID no es por si solo una señal de salud. La señal correcta, verificada con hexdump: el EDID real del G2 tiene una huella fija (mfg 0x220e 'HPN', product 0x36c1, capturada de forum-attachments/g2-edid.bin) -- cuando el conector del visor no trae esa huella, lo que hay en su lugar son puros ceros despues del header obligatorio, un placeholder sintetico del kernel, no EDID parcial real. drmprops.c ahora compara contra esa huella byte a byte e imprime hexdump de los primeros 16 bytes; preflight.sh usa esa coincidencia (no el tamaño) para el veredicto READY/NOT READY del paso 3, con logica portada a mawk (el awk por defecto de este sistema, no gawk -- match() de 3 argumentos no existe ahi). Verificado en vivo: el mismo chequeo correctamente ignoro los 128 bytes de los monitores reales (17 modos sanos cada uno) y solo marco NOT READY el conector con 1 solo modo de fallback 640x480@60 sin la huella. Sesion completa levantada despues: preflight.sh 3/3 READY, jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof con 'Using builder wmr' real, ambos controladores registrados por nombre, Basalt con 4 camaras, modo 4320x2160@90.00 encontrado, y el usuario confirmo panel encendido fisicamente.

modo: zero-touch stability sweep: system overload incident from overlapping game launches + background Steam downloads
driver: protocolo del usuario: cable/conector sin tocar desde el reseat exitoso, lanzar juegos de a uno validando cada paso, para separar 'se cae al moverlo' de 'se degrada solo'. Durante la ejecucion, se lanzo un segundo titulo (Emergence) sin confirmar que el primero (Back to Dinosaur Island) hubiera soltado el compositor, con Steam bajando de fondo varios GB (incl. SteamVR + steamvr_environments)
veredicto: INCIDENTE REAL, no relacionado al cable: se acumularon sesiones OpenXR sin cerrar (10 client_connected vs 8 client_disconnected en el log de Monado), el usuario vio visualmente 2-3 sesiones superpuestas en el casco, load average llego a 20.84 (normal: un digito), swap en uso activo, y el escritorio quedo tan colgado que el usuario tuvo que forzar el cierre de Steam a mano. monado-service aparecio muerto despues (crash o OOM-kill, no investigado mas a fondo). Limpieza aplicada: todos los procesos de juego/Proton/overlay matados, socket /run/user/1000/monado_comp_ipc stale eliminado, Steam cerrado completamente, load bajo a 3.04. PERO el companion USB (03f0:0580) NO se recupero solo al bajar la carga -- preflight.sh sigue reportando 2/5 dispositivos varios minutos despues, y journalctl -k de los ultimos 5 minutos no muestra NINGUN intento de re-enumeracion (ni siquiera un storm de error -71) -- esta simplemente ausente y quieto, un tercer estado distinto de 'tormenta activa' y de '5/5 sano', sin reintentos del kernel. No se toco el cable en ningun momento de todo el incidente. Documentado como trampa nueva en docs/23 ('overlapping VR game launches + background Steam downloads can hang the whole desktop') junto con el hallazgo positivo del mismo dia (variables de entorno globales en el proceso de Steam reemplazan la necesidad de Launch Options por juego). Pendiente: confirmar si el companion se recupera solo con mas tiempo en reposo, o si hace falta algun tipo de accion (sin tocar el cable/conector, protocolo del usuario) como prender/apagar los controladores o un replug puramente a nivel de puerto de la PC.

modo: zero-touch escalation ladder, planned with user (post-T115 overload incident)
driver: companion USB (03f0:0580) sigue en 2/5 tras 4 min de reposo puro (T115 continuacion) -- cero eventos de journalctl en toda la ventana, no es tormenta, esta quieto y ausente. Usuario propuso escalera explicita, en orden, cada paso aislando una variable distinta SIN tocar el cable del lado del visor: (1) reposo puro [COMPLETADO, T115, no alcanzo], (2) reinicios consecutivos del sistema, (3) reset de puerto USB por software (kernel-level, sin desenchufar nada), (4) desconexion/reconexion del cable USB SOLO en el extremo de la PC (separa PC-end de visor-end como variable), (5) power-cycle del propio casco (brick de 12V) -- el usuario recuerda casos anteriores donde esto solo ya habia recuperado el companion sin necesitar reseat del conector del visor. El usuario trata el cable/conector del visor con mucho cuidado deliberado ('es casi para museo ya esto', headset descontinuado sin fabricante activo) y no cree haberlo movido en este tramo de la sesion.
veredicto: Paso 3 de la escalera ejecutado (scripts/usb-bus-reset.sh, nuevo): uhubctl instalado pero 'No compatible devices detected' -- el root hub de este controlador no soporta power-switching por puerto (bit SMART hub ausente), asi que el camino uhubctl queda descartado para este hardware. Pivot a unbind/rebind del root hub completo via sysfs: el intento inicial contra el device path especifico '3-1' fallo con 'No such device' -- confirma que la rama esta totalmente ausente del arbol USB, no un dispositivo colgado con driver atascado (no hay NADA que unbindear a ese nivel). Corregido a targetear 'usb3' (el root hub en si) en vez de '3-1'. Resultado: 1/5 antes, 1/5 despues, SIN CAMBIOS -- confirmado que el reset de bus por software solo no alcanza. Dato colateral util: el mouse (tambien en bus 3) parpadeo un instante durante el unbind/bind, confirmando que el comando afecto al controlador correcto. Con esto, los pasos 2 (reboot, ya hecho: empeoro de 2/5 a 1/5) y 3 (reset de bus software) de la escalera de T116 quedan agotados sin recuperar el companion -- ambos software-only, cero contacto fisico con el cable. Siguen pendientes, en orden: (4) desconexion/reconexion del cable SOLO en el extremo de la PC, (5) power-cycle del casco (brick 12V). El usuario valido la direccion del trabajo: quiere estas herramientas de diagnostico (uhubctl, unbind/rebind, preflight.sh con fingerprint EDID de T114) pensadas como un kit reusable multi-SO -- utiles para cualquiera con este headset, no solo este lab Linux -- con el objetivo concreto de determinar que part number de cable/conector comprar como reemplazo. Idea guardada en memoria del agente para no perderla entre sesiones.

modo: usb-bus-reset.sh v2 with debugfs + trials, quick check
driver: confirmar que la version con soporte de N intentos y volcado de xhci debugfs funciona, y ver si el estado del companion cambio
veredicto: Version 2 del script (N intentos + volcado xhci debugfs) corrida por el usuario, 1 intento: sin cambios (1/5 -> 1/5), companion sigue ausente. El volcado de debugfs encontro /sys/kernel/debug/usb/xhci (SI esta montado y accesible como root -- dato nuevo, antes 'find' sin sudo no veia nada) pero no imprimio contenido de archivos dentro -- el bucle 'find maxdepth 1 -type f' no encontro archivos planos ahi, la estructura real de xhci debugfs es mas profunda (subdirectorios por bus/slot) de lo que el script asume. Pendiente de refinar si se retoma esta linea: inspeccionar a mano 'find /sys/kernel/debug/usb/xhci -type f' (con sudo) para mapear la estructura real antes de asumir un path. Cierre de sesion: la rama USB2 (companion 03f0:0580 + audio 0bda:4c15) sigue sin recuperarse via ningun paso software-only probado esta noche (reposo, reboot, bus-reset x1). Los pasos fisicos que quedan en la escalera (T116: replug solo en el extremo PC, power-cycle del brick 12V) no se ejecutaron -- decision explicita del usuario de cerrar la sesion evaluando el objetivo general en vez de seguir insistiendo con el hardware esta noche.

modo: reboot stability sweep, zero-touch (no cable movement)
driver: 3-4 reinicios consecutivos de la PC, cero contacto fisico con cualquier cable, chequeando USB (5 dispositivos) y DP/panel (fingerprint EDID real) en frio despues de cada uno -- controles deliberadamente ignorados (apagados a proposito). Objetivo: ver si el estado 5/5 actual (logrado via replug del lado PC) sobrevive reinicios repetidos sin intervencion fisica.
veredicto: 3 reinicios consecutivos (warm reboot), cero contacto fisico con cualquier cable. Resultado: 3/3 LIMPIOS -- USB 5/5 READY y DP READY (fingerprint EDID real confirmado) en cada ronda, sin ninguna excepcion. El usuario confirmo el logo HP prendido fisicamente en las rondas 2 y 3, coincidiendo en ambos casos con el veredicto de software (sin divergencia entre lo fisico y lo que reporta el DRM). Confirma que el estado 5/5 logrado esta noche via replug del lado PC (ver T117) es estable across reinicios repetidos, no un golpe de suerte de una sola vez. Controles deliberadamente ignorados (apagados a proposito, fuera de alcance de esta prueba).

modo: cold power-off/on cycle sweep, zero-touch (post T118)
driver: segunda ronda, esta vez apagado completo de la PC (no reboot tibio) con espera de 60s antes de encender, cero contacto fisico con cualquier cable -- mismo objetivo que T118 pero con power-cycle real en vez de warm reboot
veredicto: CONFIRMADO: power-cycle del brick 12V (no reboot de PC, aclarado por el usuario) -- 220V desconectado, esperado, reconectado. Secuencia medida con precision de milisegundo cruzando journalctl -k + polling del fingerprint EDID de drmprops.c: del reconecte del 220V (~19:47:00) al primer signo de vida USB paso ~17s (el casco tarda en bootear internamente antes de que el USB despierte). De ahi, los 5 dispositivos completaron en 3s: 19:47:17.0 hub USB2 (Cypress) + hub USB3 (WMR) simultaneos primero; 19:47:17-19 audio USB2 tardo 2s en terminar de enumerar; 19:47:19 camaras USB3 (HoloLens) justo despues; 19:47:20 companion USB2 (HID) ULTIMO, +3s desde el inicio -- coincide con que es la pieza mas marginal/sensible de toda la cadena, dato a favor de que el companion es el punto de falla mas probable en la degradacion del cable. DP/panel: fingerprint del G2 confirmado a las 19:48:26 (via preflight.sh disparando panel.py activate manualmente -- el DP NO sube solo, sigue necesitando activacion explicita). Investigado (WebSearch) si existe documentacion publica de esta secuencia de arranque -- NO existe, ni a nivel del chip hub (Cypress/Infineon CY4603, CYUSB331x) ni a nivel protocolo WMR en general: solo hay guias de setup genericas. Este timing medido es, hasta donde se pudo confirmar, dato original sin precedente publicado.

modo: brick power-cycle round 2, sequence timing
driver: segunda ronda del mismo test (T119) -- confirmar si el timing (17s+3s, companion ultimo) se repite o fue un dato de una sola vez
veredicto: REPETIDO: segunda ronda de power-cycle del brick, mismo patron que T119. Secuencia: 19:50:10.0 hub USB2 (Cypress)+hub USB3 (WMR) simultaneos primero; 19:50:11-13 audio USB2 tardo ~2s en enumerar (identico a la ronda 1); 19:50:13 camaras USB3 (HoloLens) junto con el audio; 19:50:14 companion USB2 (HID) OTRA VEZ ULTIMO, esta vez +4s desde el inicio de la secuencia (vs +3s en T119) -- mismo orden relativo, timing absoluto varia un poco entre rondas pero el companion consistentemente el ultimo en ambas. DP/panel: fingerprint del G2 confirmado de nuevo tras panel.py activate. 2/2 power-cycles del brick, ambos con recuperacion limpia 5/5 + DP READY y con el companion como ultimo eslabon en aparecer las dos veces -- refuerza la hipotesis de T119 de que el companion es el punto mas sensible/marginal de la cadena, no un evento aislado.

modo: brick power-cycle round 3, sequence timing
driver: tercera ronda, ronda chica de 3 establecida como estandar
veredicto: Tercera ronda del power-cycle del brick, completa la 'ronda chica de 3' establecida como estandar por el usuario. Resultado: 5/5 USB, DP READY -- exito otra vez, 3/3 power-cycles del brick con recuperacion limpia. PERO el timing NO repite el patron de T119/T120: esta vez companion (03f0:0580), camaras USB3 (045e:0659) y audio (0bda:4c15) llegaron los tres dentro del mismo segundo (19:53:11), sin que el companion fuera claramente el ultimo como en las dos rondas anteriores (+3s y +4s respectivamente). No se fuerza la hipotesis 'companion siempre ultimo' con este dato -- con solo 3 muestras y granularidad de segundo en el log crudo (el monitor detallado si tiene milisegundos pero esta lectura fue con journalctl directo), no hay suficiente resolucion para confirmar o descartar el patron con confianza. Lo que SI se sostiene 3/3: hub USB2 (Cypress) + hub USB3 (WMR) siempre simultaneos y siempre primeros. RESUMEN DE LA RONDA COMPLETA (T119-T121, 3 power-cycles del brick 12V): 3/3 recuperacion limpia (5/5 USB + DP READY), hub USB2+USB3 consistentemente primeros y simultaneos en las 3, companion consistentemente entre los ultimos mas no siempre estrictamente el ultimo aislado. Sin documentacion publica de esta secuencia (confirmado por busqueda), este es el primer mapeo real que existe de la secuencia de arranque de este headset especifico.

modo: PC-end USB cable replug, round of 3
driver: aislar el cable USB del lado PC como variable -- 3 desconecte/reconecte consecutivos, dejando el cable DP y el brick sin tocar
veredicto: 3/3 desconecte/reconecte del cable USB SOLO del lado PC (mismo puerto, el USB3 confirmado), sin tocar el brick ni el cable DP: las tres rondas recuperaron 5/5 limpio. Confirma que el asiento del cable USB del lado PC es un punto de falla real y reproducible -- no un evento aislado del principio de la noche (T117). RESUMEN ACUMULADO DE LA NOCHE (T118-T122, cable por cable, 3 veces cada uno, cero contacto con el conector del visor en todo el tramo): reinicios de PC 3/3 limpio, power-cycle del brick 3/3 limpio (secuencia de arranque documentada por primera vez, sin precedente publico), replug del cable USB en la PC 3/3 limpio. La rama USB2 que motivo toda esta escalera (T110-T116) esta hoy completamente estable bajo las tres intervenciones software/PC-side, sin haber tocado el conector del visor ni una vez desde el ultimo reseat exitoso.

modo: visor-end connector disconnect/reconnect -- the sensitive one
driver: ultimo paso de la escalera de reconexion, el mas delicado: el conector detras del gasket magnetico del visor. Todo lo anterior (T118-T122) evito tocarlo a proposito
veredicto: 3/3 desconecte/reconecte del conector del visor (detras del gasket magnetico) -- el paso mas delicado de la escalera, evitado toda la noche hasta ahora. Las tres rondas recuperaron 5/5 USB limpio. Durante la ronda 2 se observo un dato real: el logo HP se apago y volvio a prender SIN ningun desconecte de USB en journalctl -k y con lsusb en 5/5 estable todo el tiempo -- atribuido a que preflight.sh dispara panel.py activate en cada corrida, lo cual puede hacer parpadear el logo como parte del handshake de activacion sin que el DP/EDID subyacente se mueva. Se ajusto el protocolo a pedido del usuario: dejar de correr chequeos activos entre desconectes para no contaminar la observacion del logo con flapping inducido por el propio diagnostico -- leccion de metodo real, no solo de hardware. CIERRE DE LA ESCALERA COMPLETA DE ESTA NOCHE (T118-T123, cada pieza probada 3 veces, del menos invasivo al mas): reinicios de PC 3/3, power-cycle del brick 3/3, replug del USB en la PC 3/3, reconexion del conector del visor 3/3 -- TODOS limpios. La rama USB2 que motivo T110-T116 esta completamente estable bajo cada intervencion individual probada esta noche.

modo: breakout-box 12V barrel connector, round of 3 -- completing coverage
driver: conector de bajo voltaje (barril) entre el brick y la caja breakout, DISTINTO del lado 220V/mains ya probado en T119-T121. Para que la escalera de reconexion este completa, falta este conector especifico -- el usuario lo señalo explicitamente como gap de cobertura
veredicto: 3/3 desconecte/reconecte del conector de bajo voltaje (barril) entre el brick 12V y la caja breakout -- distinto al lado 220V/mains ya probado en T119-T121, completando la cobertura de conectores que el usuario señalo como gap. Las tres rondas: 0/5 al desconectar, 5/5 limpio al reconectar, sin excepcion. Nota de metodo: el sysfs de DP-1 mostro 'connected' incluso con USB en 0/5 durante el primer corte -- confirmado como lectura rezagada sin valor de senal aca (no hubo un hotplug real que forzara el refresh), el conteo de USB es la señal confiable para este conector especifico. CON ESTO, LA ESCALERA DE RECONEXION QUEDA REALMENTE COMPLETA (T118-T124): reinicios de PC, power-cycle del brick (lado 220V), replug USB en la PC, reconexion del conector del visor, Y AHORA el barril de bajo voltaje del brick -- CINCO puntos de contacto distintos, cada uno probado 3 veces, TODOS 3/3 limpios. Ningun conector de la cadena quedo sin probar.

modo: root port 4 (chipset-labeled by user, actually same CPU controller) -- USB2 fails, USB3 fine
driver: usuario probo un puerto que penso era del chipset (no-CPU) para completar cobertura de la topologia motherboard/CPU. Objetivo: documentar por que el VR nunca levanta en ese puerto
veredicto: HALLAZGO REAL, distinto al tema cable: cambio de puerto a root port 4 (ID_PATH pci-0000:07:00.3-usb-0:4) -- el usuario penso que era un puerto del chipset (no-CPU), pero es el MISMO controlador CPU 07:00.3 que el root port 1 ya usado toda la noche, solo un indice de puerto fisico distinto. Resultado medido en journalctl -k: la rama USB3 (bus4, puerto 4-4) enumero perfecto -- hub WMR (04b4:6504) y camaras HoloLens (045e:0659) ambos con 'New USB device found' limpio. La rama USB2 (bus3, puerto 3-4) FALLO por completo -- dos intentos de enumeracion (device 48, device 49) sin ningun 'New USB device found', el hub Cypress (04b4:6506) nunca llego a identificarse. Companion y audio, detras de ese hub, nunca aparecieron. EXPLICACION TECNICA (investigada, con fuente): el conector USB-A 3.0 tiene 9 pines fisicamente separados en dos grupos -- los 4 pines legacy de USB2 (D+, D-, VBUS, GND) en la posicion central identica a un USB2-A, mas 5 pines SuperSpeed agregados atras especificamente para mantener compatibilidad hacia atras. Son dos juegos de contactos independientes en el mismo conector fisico, lo cual explica mecanicamente por que USB3 puede enumerar sano mientras USB2 falla en el mismo puerto -- confirmado el hecho del pinout via busqueda, NO confirmada la causa especifica del desgaste diferencial (queda como hipotesis razonable, no dato verificado: los pines centrales legacy reciben uso de CUALQUIER dispositivo USB2 historico en ese puerto, no solo del headset, lo cual los expone a mas desgaste acumulado que los pines SuperSpeed mas nuevos). Usuario confirmo verbalmente antes de medir: 'en este el vr nunca levanta' -- consistente con el dato. No se intento levantar una sesion real de Monado en este puerto (ya se sabia que iba a fallar sin companion/HID, hubiera sido churn innecesario sobre una rama ya fragil). CONCLUSION: esto es un problema de TOPOLOGIA DE PUERTO/PLACA MADRE, no del cable ni del conector del visor -- variable completamente distinta a todo lo medido en T118-T124. El root port 1 (donde vivio el cable toda la noche) sigue siendo el puerto valido a usar; el root port 4 queda documentado como NO USAR para este headset especificamente.

modo: genuine chipset USB2 rear port -- everything enumerates, cameras bandwidth-crippled
driver: el ultimo puerto que faltaba: USB2 real del chipset (bus1, al lado del receptor Logitech, docs/00 ya lo identificaba). Completa el mapeo de puertos de la placa
veredicto: COMPLETA LA COBERTURA TOTAL DE PUERTOS: probado el puerto USB2 real del chipset A520 (bus1, root port 8 -- el mismo grupo fisico donde vive el receptor Logitech, ya identificado en docs/00). A diferencia del root port 4 (T125, USB2 completamente muerto): ACA los 4 dispositivos del headset enumeraron sin problema -- hub Cypress (04b4:6506) en 1-8, audio (0bda:4c15) en 1-8.2, companion (03f0:0580) en 1-8.3, y hasta las camaras HoloLens Sensors (045e:0659) en 1-8.1. PERO hallazgo real: las camaras negociaron a solo 480 Mbps (velocidad USB2/high-speed, confirmado via /sys/bus/usb/devices/1-8.1/speed) en vez de su velocidad nativa de 5000 Mbps (SuperSpeed) -- este puerto no tiene carriles SuperSpeed en absoluto (el chipset A520 solo expone USB3 por headers internos que este case no cablea, docs/00 ya lo establecia). Conclusion: 'enumera' no es lo mismo que 'funciona bien' -- por conteo esto casi parece 5/5 (falta solo el identificador del hub USB3 04b4:6504, que estructuralmente no puede existir en un puerto sin SuperSpeed), pero las camaras corriendo a 1/10 de su ancho de banda nativo casi seguro degradarian o rompen el streaming en tiempo real que necesita SLAM/WMR, aunque la enumeracion en si no falle. Un chequeo basado solo en conteo de dispositivos NO hubiera detectado este problema -- hace falta verificar tambien la velocidad negociada, no solo la presencia. CON ESTO QUEDA COMPLETO EL MAPEO DE TODOS LOS PUERTOS DE LA PLACA: root port 1 (CPU, bueno, el usado toda la noche), root port 4 (CPU, USB2 muerto, no usar), puerto USB2 del chipset (bus1, todo enumera pero camaras degradadas a 480M, no usar para sesiones reales con 6dof/SLAM).

modo: generic gamepad fallback identified for missing VR controllers
driver: explorando --skip=controllers de power-on.py: que dispositivo de respaldo hay disponible si los controles del G2 fallan/faltan
veredicto: Dato de contexto para el fallback de controles (power-on.py --skip=controllers): el usuario tiene DOS gamepads USB en la mesa -- un Xbox 360 oficial real y un generico PS3/PC marca SHANWAN (idVendor real 2563:0575) que emula compatibilidad Xbox 360. Ambos se anuncian identicos ante el sistema (045e:028e 'Xbox360 Controller', driver xpad de Linux los toma automaticamente), asi que lsusb por si solo no los distingue -- confirmado apagando el Xbox 360 real: lsusb bajo de 2 entradas '045e:028e' a 1 (quedo el SHANWAN, en bus 3). El SHANWAN llego solo por 'Bus 3-1', el mismo puerto raiz bueno (root port 1) donde vive el cable del headset toda la noche -- comparte controlador pero es un dispositivo totalmente independiente, no interfiere con la enumeracion del headset (confirmado, headset ya habia enumerado bien antes con el SHANWAN puesto). Limitacion real senalada por el usuario, no solo teorica: la emulacion Xbox 360 de gamepads genericos NO es garantia universal -- 'muchas veces andan en algunos' juegos, no en todos (algunos validan mas estricto que solo VID/PID). Conclusion para el mensaje de power-on.py: cuando faltan los controles VR reales, un gamepad USB generico es un fallback PARCIAL (sirve para navegar menus/juegos simples), no un reemplazo universal -- el mensaje no deberia prometer que 'cualquier joystick anda en cualquier juego'. Pendiente real, no arrancado: probar el SHANWAN contra juegos concretos de docs/23-game-compatibility.md y anotar ahi que funciona real (cuales si, cuales no), en vez de asumir por la emulacion.

modo: boot selector Phase 1 code + early-console blank-screen fix prep
driver: arreglados los bugs bloqueantes del selector de arranque encontrados por el review (handoff a graphical.target en fallos, exec removido, tty1/tty2 swap). Ademas se encontro y se va a resolver un problema preexistente: consola temprana en negro (LUKS a ciegas) por falta de nvidia-drm.modeset=1 + modulos NVIDIA en initramfs
veredicto: CONFIRMADO fisicamente por el usuario: consola temprana ahora visible en las 3 pantallas tras agregar nvidia-drm.modeset=1 al GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT y los modulos nvidia/nvidia_modeset/nvidia_drm al initramfs (verificado con lsinitramfs antes de reiniciar -- los .ko.xz reales estaban empaquetados, no solo la config). Login post-reinicio limpio, sin problemas. Resuelve el problema preexistente donde ni el prompt de desbloqueo de LUKS se veia (el usuario tipeaba la clave a ciegas) -- root-causado correctamente como ausencia de framebuffer temprano de NVIDIA, no como bug nuevo introducido por este proyecto. Con esto se destraba el prerequisito bloqueante que impedia probar el selector de arranque (Phase 1 del plan) en tty1, ya que antes esa consola hubiera estado tan en negro como el prompt de LUKS. Pendiente aun no confirmado: si el monitor horizontal (el '27') quedo efectivamente como primario/boot-primary, o si el vertical sigue siendo el que muestra la consola -- no se pregunto explicitamente en esta confirmacion. modo: boot selector Etapa 3-4: pruebas en vivo y default persistente

modo: T136: runuser mata monado-service/Steam al cerrar su sesion PAM -- reemplazado por systemd-run --scope
veredicto: Con T135 ya aplicado (XDG_SESSION_TYPE), el intento real via tty4 avanzo de verdad esta vez (23s, CPU/memoria reales en el journal, jack-in-wayland.log muestra swapchain 4320x2160 y BEGIN_SESSION real) pero igual termino en exit 1 -- monado-service se auto-apago limpio ('Server exiting: 0') en el MISMO segundo que la sesion PAM de runuser se cerro en el journal. Causa: runuser envuelve el comando en un scope de sesion de login que systemd/logind detiene explicitamente cuando el proceso lider (vr-launcher.py) termina, matando todo lo que quedaba en ese cgroup -- monado-service y Steam incluidos -- sin importar que setsid ya los desacoplara del control de terminal (setsid cambia la sesion de proceso a nivel kernel, no el cgroup de systemd que el logout de la sesion realmente usa para matar). Fix: reemplace runuser por 'systemd-run --scope --uid=iam' -- un scope transitorio propio no atado a ninguna sesion de login, que systemd mantiene vivo mientras el cgroup no este vacio (no se detiene solo porque el proceso original ya salio). CAVEAT IMPORTANTE: no tengo sudo desde esta sesion de Claude Code para probar el systemd-run con --uid= real (necesita root); el razonamiento se apoya en semantica documentada de systemd (scope units vs session scopes de logind), no en una repro controlada como T135. Pendiente validar con un reboot real.

Confirmado con getfacl que ese device es root:plugdev 0660 SIN acl uaccess dinamica (tag udev es ':seat:', no 'uaccess') -- el acceso depende 100% de membresia real en el grupo plugdev. modo: T142: idea parked 'mutter standalone' -- probada en vivo, resultado real: SI publica el lease al arrancar, NO lo refresca en un hotplug en vivo
veredicto: Se instalo una entrada de sesion SDDM adicional ('Mutter (bare, no shell)', /usr/share/wayland-sessions/mutter-bare.desktop + /usr/local/bin/mutter-bare-session.sh, sin tocar 'GNOME on Wayland') para probar la idea parked de 2026-08-10: si mutter solo (sin gnome-shell) sigue ofreciendo el DRM lease del G2. RESULTADO POSITIVO PARCIAL: con el conector 137/DP-2 ya CONECTADO al momento en que mutter arranca, mutter SI publica wp_drm_lease_device_v1 con el conector del casco (confirmado via wayland-info/check-lease.sh, log /tmp/mutter-bare-session-8892.log) -- la premisa tecnica (mutter implementa el lease el mismo, no via gnome-shell) es correcta. RESULTADO NEGATIVO, el bloqueante real: cuando el panel del G2 se activa DESPUES de que mutter ya esta corriendo (que es el caso real siempre -- el panel esta apagado hasta que Monado/panel.py mandan la activacion HID, eso pasa despues de que la sesion de escritorio ya existe), mutter-bare NO refresca su lista de conectores leaseables ante ese hotplug en vivo: con el conector 137 confirmado CONNECTED a nivel kernel/DRM (EDID de 384 bytes, huella real del G2) durante 6+ segundos seguidos, wayland-info contra el mutter-bare ya corriendo seguia mostrando wp_drm_lease_device_v1 CON CERO conectores. jack-in-wayland.sh fallo consistentemente con 'Found no connectors available for direct mode' en 3 intentos distintos (con su propio poll de 10s + 3 reintentos con settle de 3s, ya disenado para la raza ya documentada de 2026-08-09) -- mismo sintoma cada vez. GNOME completo (gnome-shell) maneja este hotplug en vivo correctamente (es el pipeline de produccion, verificado muchas veces); mutter bare aparentemente no. CONCLUSION: la idea 'escritorio liviano' con mutter standalone no es viable tal cual para este caso de uso especifico, salvo que se investigue por que mutter-bare no re-escanea conectores en vivo (posible: gnome-shell dispara algun refresh de outputs que mutter solo no hace por si mismo) -- no intentado, day cierra la investigacion por esta noche.

modo: T143: BUG REAL encontrado en el camino -- systemd-run --scope --uid=iam NO resuelve los grupos suplementarios de iam (falta plugdev)
veredicto: Mientras se debuggeaba T142, jack-in-wayland.sh fallaba con ERROR [p_open_hid_interface] Failed to open device '/dev/hidraw2' got '-13' (EACCES) al abrir el HID del headset (HoloLens Sensors, confirmado via udevadm). Diagnostico en vivo (scripts/diag-hidraw-scope.sh, ahora en el repo): 'systemd-run --scope --uid=iam -- id' devuelve groups=1000(iam),0(root) -- le falta plugdev (46) y el resto de los grupos reales de iam. Comparado con 'runuser -u iam -- id', que SI resuelve la lista completa y correcta (adm,cdrom,floppy,audio,dip,video,plugdev,users,netdev,systemd-journal). El pipeline de produccion (vr-launcher-console.sh, systemd-run --scope --uid=iam) nunca dependio realmente de esta resolucion de grupos siendo correcta -- funcionaba porque /dev/hidraw2 tiene ACL dinamica via logind (uaccess) para la sesion ACTIVA de seat0, independiente de grupos. Esa ACL se revoca en el instante en que la sesion deja de ser la activa (ej. el humano cambia de VT para hablar con el agente) -- eso es lo que rompio los primeros intentos de este test, incluso despues de un chvt de vuelta (la ventana se cerraba de nuevo apenas el humano volvia a reportar el resultado). FIX aplicado y verificado (scripts/jack-in-under-bare-mutter.sh): usar runuser SOLO para bajar el privilegio con los grupos reales, y de ahi saltar a 'systemd-run --user --scope' (el manager de systemd del propio usuario, no atado a la sesion de login de runuser) para que el proceso sobreviva igual que antes al teardown de la sesion PAM de runuser. Con este fix, el HID abrio bien y Monado creo el device del headset con XRT_SUCCESS -- el bug de permisos quedo resuelto independientemente del resultado de T142. NO APLICADO TODAVIA a la produccion real (vr-launcher-console.sh sigue usando el systemd-run --scope simple) porque nunca fallo alli -- ese pipeline jamas corre con el usuario cambiando de VT a mitad de un arranque. Vale la pena recordarlo si alguna vez se ve un EACCES ahi.

modo: T144: intento de mover el autologin Auto de GNOME a mutter-bare -- revertido, causa raiz no encontrada
veredicto: Idea del usuario, con buena logica: si power-on.py --pre-login YA activa el panel en su paso 4 (antes de que SDDM arranque), entonces el escenario que T142 confirmo que SI funciona (conector ya conectado cuando mutter arranca) deberia darse siempre en el boot real -- asi que apuntar el autologin de Auto a 'Mutter (bare, no shell)' en vez de GNOME deberia andar. La teoria en si NUNCA se pudo poner a prueba de verdad: lo que se rompio fue un nivel mas arriba, en como SDDM resuelve el autologin. Camino recorrido: (1) cambiar solo /etc/sddm.conf.d/98-vr-autologin.conf a mano + systemctl restart sddm -- SDDM siguio leyendo gnome-wayland.desktop, sin importar el contenido del archivo. (2) Encontrada la causa real de ESE sintoma especifico: scripts/vr-boot-selector.sh hardcodea 'Session=gnome-wayland.desktop' en su rama Auto (linea ~94 antes de esta correccion) y reescribe ese archivo en CADA boot -- cualquier edicion manual o restart de sddm sin tocar este script se pisa sola. Corregido el script para escribir mutter-bare.desktop ahi, con reboot limpio de verdad. (3) Con el script corregido y el panel pre-activado a mano antes del reboot (conector 137 confirmado CONNECTED, EDID de 384 bytes), el reboot completo SIGUIO autologueando a GNOME -- 'Reading from .../gnome-wayland.desktop' desde el primer log de sddm, sin un solo intento de mutter-bare. Descartado, cada uno confirmado en vivo con evidencia, no supuesto: el archivo en disco tenia el contenido correcto byte a byte (verificado con xxd, sin problema de encoding/espacios); vr-boot-selector.service corrio una sola vez ese boot (journalctl -u confirmado); ningun otro script del repo toca ese archivo (grep exhaustivo); no hay condicion de carrera entre la escritura (linea temprana del script) y el arranque de sddm (~19s de diferencia real, journalctl timestamps); AccountsService no tiene un perfil guardado para iam (/var/lib/AccountsService/users/iam no existe). Confirmado por separado, mismo dato importante: elegir 'Mutter (bare, no shell)' A MANO desde la lista grafica de sesiones de SDDM funciono bien (mas temprano la misma noche) -- el .desktop en si es valido y SDDM lo descubre normalmente en el selector interactivo. La sospecha mas fuerte, NO confirmada: el camino de autologin de SDDM puede resolver la sesion contra una lista distinta (escaneada/cacheada antes) que el selector interactivo, y no ve sesiones agregadas en el mismo boot -- no verificado, requeriria revisar el codigo fuente de SDDM o probar con el .desktop ya presente desde un boot ANTERIOR para distinguir 'autologin nunca ve sesiones nuevas' de 'autologin especificamente no funciona con mutter-bare'. REVERTIDO: vr-boot-selector.sh vuelve a escribir gnome-wayland.desktop (estado conocido-bueno). No repetir el mismo ciclo de escribir-y-reiniciar sin una idea nueva -- este camino ya esta agotado tal cual se lo probo.

modo: T145: unattended boot chain failed all 3 attempts with 'Found no connectors available for direct mode' -- NOT hardware; the compositor-side lease gate was missing and the evidence was being thrown away
veredicto: First entry written in English, per the standing rule that everything committed to this repo is in English (older entries deliberately left as they are -- they carry literal Spanish quotes from the user and rewriting them would risk distorting old verdicts). SYMPTOM: the 03:15 boot ran the whole unattended chain correctly -- vr-boot-selector -> Auto, power-on.py --pre-login reaching LISTO 5/5 at 03:15:39 (controllers_ok true, gamepad present), SDDM autologin into GNOME Wayland on VT3, vr-launcher-console on tty4 -- and then jack-in-wayland.sh failed three times in a row at 03:16 with 'Found no connectors available for direct mode'. vr-launcher.py exited 1 at 03:17:14, systemd restarted the service, and agetty took tty4: the 'hung cursor' the user reported is that login prompt, not a hang. NOT HARDWARE, measured immediately afterwards on the same boot with nothing restarted: panel.py activate brought DP-2 to connected with the healthy 384-byte EDID and connector 137 offering all three modes including 4320x2160@90, and check-lease.sh -- run against the mutter instance that had already been up for six minutes -- showed it offering connector 137 for lease. A theory drafted before that measurement ('mutter does not refresh its lease connector list on a live hotplug', carried over from the T144 mutter-bare investigation) was therefore WRONG and was discarded before being written down as a finding: mutter does pick up a live hotplug. What is left is the race jack-in-wayland.sh's own comments already describe -- comp_window_direct_wayland.c does one roundtrip and accepts the lease device's first 'done' event as final, so if mutter has not finished processing the hotplug at that instant Monado sees zero connectors and gives up. The blind 3-attempt retry added on 2026-08-09 lost all three times tonight. FIX 1 (jack-in-wayland.sh): after the existing drmprops non-desktop=1 gate, poll the COMPOSITOR side directly (same wayland-info query check-lease.sh uses, up to 15s) before starting Monado, instead of retrying blind. The kernel seeing the connector and mutter offering it for lease are two different events and only the second one is what Monado actually asks about. FIX 2 (vr-launcher.py): jack-in-wayland.sh's own output is now appended to ~/vr/logs/jack-in-launcher.log. Tonight the one piece of evidence that would have separated 'the panel never came up' from 'the connector was up but the compositor had not offered it' -- jack-in-wayland.sh's pre-flight lines -- went to tty4 and was overwritten by agetty, and /tmp/vr-launcher-console-debug.log stayed at 0 bytes precisely because capture_output=True swallows that stream before it can reach the redirect. Same class as the StandardOutput=tty trap from 2026-08-10. ALSO FOUND, not fixed: ~/.config/autostart/vr-launcher-autostart.desktop still points at scripts/vr-launcher-autostart.sh, which does not exist -- it fails harmlessly at every login (visible in the journal as an xdg-autostart-generator error) and is a leftover from the pre-tty4 approach. And ~/vr/play360.sh has drifted: it is a Spanish translation that was never committed, while scripts/play360.sh is still English.

modo: T146: 6DoF controllers, patch 0014 (constellation tracker created over the headset's cameras) -- built clean, not physically verified; plus the real floor/height mechanism read out of the source
veredicto: PATCH 0014 WRITTEN AND BUILT (zero warnings, monado-service links): WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS, default off, creates a t_constellation_tracker with one camera mosaic over the headset's tracking cameras and routes 0013's per-camera LED blobs into it. The design decision that separates this from the in-tree Rift reference: a Rift sensor sits still on a desk and gets a hardcoded fixed pose in the room, whereas the WMR cameras are bolted to the headset and move with it, so the mosaic is given a t_constellation_tracker_tracking_source that reports the headset's own tracked pose (whichever of SLAM/3dof is live, via the xrt_device entry point so the wh->offset correction is included) and each camera's pose_in_origin is its extrinsics relative to the middle of the eyes. The extrinsics needed two things taken from existing precedent in the same file rather than invented: the coordinate sandwich into OpenXR coordinates (config camera poses are raw WMR, the stored P_ht0_me is already OpenXR), and the HT2/HT3 swap quirk wmr_hmd_fill_slam_cams_calibration() already handles for the 4-camera G2. No devices are registered with the tracker yet (that is 0015), so nothing solves and no reported pose changes -- with the option off the behaviour is identical. NOT physically verified yet, deliberately: the user's standing rule against chaining monado-service restarts, so this waits for one clean run. VERBOSE TRACKING LOGS enabled in jack-in-wayland.sh (VR_VERBOSE=0 turns them off): XRT_LOG=debug (the global default is WARN, which is why the runtime looked so quiet), WMR_LOG, SLAM_LOG, CONSTELLATION_TRACKER_LOG, and -- the actually useful one -- SLAM_WRITE_CSVS=1 with SLAM_CSV_PATH pointed at a per-run ~/vr/logs/slam-<stamp>/ directory, so movement can be checked against a real series of poses instead of the presence of a log line. Left off on purpose: SLAM_UI (extra window, steals focus), CONSTELLATION_TRACKER_RERUN_ENABLE (wants an external rerun.io viewer), XRT_TRACING. HEIGHT/FLOOR CALIBRATION, researched in the source because the answer is not the SteamVR one: Monado has no floor calibration at all. Since the WMR driver does not set supported.stage, b_space_overseer_legacy_setup makes STAGE == root (the tracking origin, i.e. wherever the headset was when Basalt initialised), LOCAL == root + 1.6m in Y and LOCAL_FLOOR == root, with that 1.6 a literal constant in target_builder_helpers.c. So the floor is assumed to be exactly 1.6m below the headset's position at startup. The one knob that exists today is XRT_TRACKING_ORIGIN_OFFSET_{X,Y,Z}, applied unconditionally to every tracking origin at startup, giving XRT_TRACKING_ORIGIN_OFFSET_Y = (real headset height at startup) - 1.6. Two workable procedures with no code change: measure the headset height with a tape and set the difference (the headset must be at that height at the instant monado-service starts, because root is pinned there), or run XRT_DEBUG_GUI=1, rest the headset on the floor, read Y off the HMD's 'Tracked Pose' panel and use its negation -- wh->offset is exposed as an editable 'Pose Offset' in the same GUI, so it can be trimmed live before being fixed as an env var. Putting the CONTROLLERS on the floor cannot work yet: they have no position at all until 0017 fuses one. SIDE FINDING THAT EXPLAINS AN OLD SYMPTOM: the long-standing 'controllers appear offset, sometimes by several metres, and only rotate in place' is fully accounted for by u_builder_helpers.c, which gives untracked devices a fixed initial_offset -- (-0.2, 1.3, -0.5) and (0.2, 1.3, -0.5) for the controllers, (0, 1.6, 0) for head and eyes -- applied whenever tracking_origin->type is XRT_TRACKING_TYPE_NONE, and the only assignment of that field anywhere in the tree is the default NONE in u_device.c:341, so it is active on the WMR path even in 6DoF. The controllers are pinned relative to ROOT, not to the head, so with SLAM running the apparent error grows with how far the user has walked from the SLAM origin. CORRECTION to NEXT-STEP.md, which said the placeholder was a hardcoded y=1.2: the real values in this tree are 1.3 for controllers and gamepad and 1.6 for head and eyes. LIVE RESULT, same night, two clean runs (one restart between them, not a chain of them): BOTH came up on attempt 1/3 with 'Compositor offers the connector for lease', 4320x2160@90, 'Using builder wmr' and both controllers registered -- so the T145 compositor-side gate is confirmed working against the exact failure that made this night start. BASELINE (option off): 30.1 Hz pose rate, 19.4 m of trajectory, max step 3.0 cm, no step above 4 cm, user verdict 'todo perfecto, parece que trackea bien'. Earlier in the same run, 59 s of deliberate movement gave 4.04 m of path, 0.95 m max displacement, 17.6 cm of vertical span and 111 deg of rotation, against 2-4 cm of drift with the headset resting on the table -- real 6DoF, measured against a resting baseline rather than asserted. WITH WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS=1: tracker created over 4 tracking cameras, 1 mosaic, no devices registered, and 30.0 Hz pose rate -- i.e. NO regression, which is the question that mattered, since the blobwatch chain now feeding the tracker runs inside the same realtime USB callback as the SLAM path. The 45 steps above 4 cm in that run are consecutive samples at a normal 33 ms interval (a fast real movement), not a discontinuity. REAL BUG IN 0014 FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE ANYTHING CONSUMED IT: the printed per-camera positions were geometrically impossible -- all four cameras within ~8 cm of each other and effectively coplanar in Z -- while the headset's own calibration puts HT1 10.8 cm from HT0 and HT2 13.7 cm from HT0. A rigid transform preserves those distances, so the composition had to be wrong, and it was: P_A_B is the placement of B in A's frame, so both tcams[i]->pose (P_ci_c0) and the stored P_ht0_me point the opposite way to what pose_in_origin wants, and both needed inverting -- P_me_ci = P_me_ht0 * P_ht0_ci. Rebuilt clean. Nothing consumed the extrinsics yet (no devices are registered until 0015), so no measurement above is invalidated, but this would have silently biased every solved position in 0016-0017. ACCEPTANCE CHECK for the next run, no hardware judgement needed: the distances between the printed camera positions must match the config, |pos0-pos1| ~= 0.108 m and |pos0-pos2| ~= 0.137 m. ALSO WORTH KEEPING: 859 and 630 'det(Q1Jl) == 0' warnings from Basalt across the two runs with ZERO divergence in either. Previous sessions treated that message as the signature of the known SLAM divergence issue -- it is not, on its own. It is the optimizer skipping degenerate landmarks. Check the trajectory for real discontinuities before calling SLAM broken because of it. EXTRINSICS FIX CONFIRMED on the following run, and the acceptance check above needed correcting: the four cameras now come out symmetric, slightly below eye level and at NEGATIVE Z (in front of the eyes, since OpenXR -Z is forward), with |pos0-pos1| = 0.1082 m against the 0.1082 in the headset's own calibration and |pos0-pos3| = 0.1369 m against 0.1371 -- before the fix all four sat within ~8 mm of each other and behind the head. The check as first written (|pos0-pos2| ~= 0.137) reads as a FAILURE when everything is right, because this code deliberately applies the same HT2/HT3 swap the SLAM path applies: compare pos0<->pos3 against HT2 and pos0<->pos2 against HT3, not index for index. PLAYER VERIFIED END TO END the same night, user-confirmed twice ('imagen de ejemplo, bien. controles ok' and 'perfecto, andando de 10'): the 360 player reached XR_SESSION_STATE_FOCUSED against tonight's build with both controllers bound to oculus/touch_controller and every action resolved. NEW INSTRUMENT, and it made the placeholder finding undeniable: hello_xr now logs head plus both controller poses once a second, ON BY DEFAULT (HELLO_XR_POSE_LOG=0 to opt out), explicitly so controller tracking can be watched WITHOUT anyone wearing the headset -- on this hardware every put-on/take-off means moving a cable with a documented history of marginal contact, so a check that needs a human's head has a real hardware cost. Live output: the head moves (+-3 cm of drift resting on a table) while BOTH controllers report byte-identical positions line after line, flagged 'pos:OK trk:--'. That is exactly the u_builder_helpers.c placeholder predicted earlier from reading the source: y = -0.255 in app space is the placeholder's 1.3 minus the 1.6 the space overseer puts between STAGE and LOCAL, and x is -+0.2. The flags are the point -- an untracked controller reports a completely plausible position, so a bare XYZ triplet cannot be told apart from a real one; only TRACKED distinguishes them. At 0017 that field flips to OK and the numbers start moving, which is a binary criterion needing no human judgement. DEAD END, recorded so it is not retried: XRT_WINDOW_PEEK (the SDL2 mirror window, asked for so the session could be watched on the desktop) creates its window and then dies in comp_window_peek_blit with VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED, taking monado-service down with it. Consistent with the compositor being in direct mode with the connector leased. XRT_DEBUG_GUI=1 is the mirror that works. New doc: docs/28-log-map.md -- where every log lives, what question each answers, what is still not captured (the player's POSE output when launched from tty4, xrizer's own output, per-title engine logs), and the traps already paid for.

modo: T147: SLAM runs away with the headset static (measured, unexplained); controller-tracking camera frames are black and the reference implementation's exposure fix never ran; cubes restored to the player
veredicto: SLAM RUNAWAY, MEASURED AND UNEXPLAINED. With the headset motionless the tracked pose leaves 25 cm of the origin somewhere between 2.2 s and 50.8 s depending on the run, and then grows super-quadratically -- 785 m at 99 s in one run, 16 km at 211 s in another. New tool scripts/pose-measure.py reports this from the SLAM pose CSV with a stable/runaway verdict, the crossing time, the dominant axis and the growth exponent. Exponents measured between 2.4 and 3.5: an exponent near 2 is a constant unmodelled acceleration (double integration of a bias), above 2 means the attitude error is growing too, so gravity leaks in progressively. At 211 s the displacement implied about 7 percent of g uncompensated, i.e. roughly 4 degrees of attitude error with nothing bounding it. WHAT WAS RULED OUT, each by measurement rather than argument: ambient light (user confirmed lights on with plenty of visual reference, and the 'SLAM Tracking Streams' debug panel looked perfect); frames not arriving (timing.csv has 4802 rows at exactly 30.0/s, the camera frame rate); and the constellation patches -- though the last one only after a real methodological error, described below. METHODOLOGICAL ERROR WORTH KEEPING. An A/B was run with WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS off to test whether patch 0013's per-frame work inside img_xfer_cb was degrading SLAM. It proved nothing: the flag only gated the tracker in wmr_hmd.c, while 0013's blobwatch chain in wmr_source.c ran unconditionally, so the 'off' arm still paid for all of it. Fixed by gating the whole chain (patch 0015). A second error followed immediately: with the chain genuinely out, one run crossed 25 cm at 26.3 s versus 2.2 s with it in, and that was briefly written up as a 12x effect. Running the same metric over all six runs of the night killed it -- times with the chain active ranged from 2.2 s to 50.8 s, so the spread WITHIN the group is larger than the difference between groups, and 26.3 s sits in the middle of it. Two of those runs also had the headset moving on a table rather than static on the floor, so they are not comparable at all. Conclusion: the data is too confounded to attribute anything, and one sample is not a finding. CONTROLLER-TRACKING FRAMES ARE BLACK, and this is the night's real discovery. 'Controller Tracking Streams' -- an upstream debug panel that predates all of our patches -- is absolutely black while 'SLAM Tracking Streams' is perfect, with the controllers' LED rings plainly lit and clearly visible in the SLAM view. So every 'Controller Blob Cam' panel from 0013 is black downstream of that, and patch 0015's planned LED model would have fed a solver black images. Chain of elimination, each step checked rather than assumed: (1) WMR controller tracking LEDs are VISIBLE light, not infrared -- an earlier claim in this session that they were IR was wrong and was corrected; the user confirmed the ring glows to the naked eye. (2) The LEDs are not off: the controllers sleep on their own when left still (autonomous, not host-driven), but a service start walks them asleep -> fast blink -> solid on, observed live. (3) There is NO LED-enable command anywhere in the WMR driver; only four commands are ever sent (reinit, quiesce/restart, status ON, IMU ON) and wmr_led_config leds[] is parsed and discarded. (4) The real gap is exposure: thaytan's dev-constellation-controller-tracking branch has DEFAULT_CTRL_EXPOSURE 0x0190 and DEFAULT_CTRL_GAIN 0x0001 -- a 15x shorter exposure at minimum gain, so the camera sees only the LEDs and nothing else. That design also explains two known WMR behaviours from the outside: controller tracking works in a dark room, and using these headsets in direct sunlight is advised against because the sun swamps the LEDs. (5) OUR TREE HAS NO SUCH FUNCTION AT ALL, and thaytan's calls it from `for (int i = cam->tcam_count; i < cam->tcam_count; i++)`, a loop that never executes -- so the reference mapping has almost certainly never run on any hardware either. PATCH 0015 (opt-in, NOT VALIDATED): adds the controller exposure/gain command and gates the whole constellation path behind WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS. thaytan's slot mapping is a hardcoded camera_id + 2, correct for a two-camera headset but landing on real SLAM cameras on the four-camera G2, so it was generalised to + tcam_count. The controller stream stayed black, so either that mapping is wrong or the frames are not arriving. Left opt-in precisely because it is unproven. NEXT STEP is to make it measurable instead of guessing one restart at a time: a one-shot per-frametype frame counter to settle whether controller frames arrive at all, and a live u_var control for the controller exposure slot so the mapping can be swept without restarting. ALSO: t_led_sync_refinement.c in the constellation module exists to refine the latency offset between LED BLINK times and camera exposure -- the constellation LEDs strobe rather than being continuously lit, so a correct short exposure that lands outside the pulse still captures darkness. That is a third candidate explanation for the black frames and it is not excluded. OPERATIONAL NOTE for any future controller-tracking test: the controllers fall asleep on their own when left still, and their LEDs go out with them. Any optical test needs them held or moving. hello_xr patch 0015 restores the per-pose cubes the 360 player dropped when it replaced the geometry pipeline with the fullscreen-triangle path; second pipeline, own shaders, shares the existing layout.

modo: T148: player cubes verified on hardware (two real render bugs fixed first); then the USB2 branch dropped at 04:59 and three 'failed' sessions were actually the Simulated HMD
veredicto: CUBES VERIFIED ON REAL HARDWARE, user-confirmed ('los veo!', and on rotation 'giran, todo bien'): the per-pose cubes are drawn, stay fixed in world space while the head rotates around them, and sit at the untracked-controller placeholder positions as expected. That closes the render path -- pipeline, depth, view matrix, and the pose vector arriving from the runtime -- and gives the 6DoF work its in-headset instrument: the same cubes will start following the controllers once 0017 fuses a real position. TWO REAL BUGS had to be fixed before anything was visible, neither of which any log would have shown. (1) The 360 background wrote gl_Position.z = 0.0, the NEAREST depth, with depth writes on. It filled the depth buffer with the minimum value and every cube drawn afterwards failed the LESS test and was discarded silently. Fixed to 0.9999 -- not 1.0, because the buffer is cleared to 1.0 and LESS would then reject the background itself. (2) hello_xr also draws a 25 cm cube per reference space, and in a 3dof session the head sits exactly at the Local origin, so that cube lands centred on the viewer's face; with cullMode NONE its inner faces render too and the viewer is sealed inside an opaque box hiding everything else. User's report was literally 'estoy dentro de un cubo de colores, no veo los controles'. Now off by default behind HELLO_XR_SPACE_CUBES=1. ONE OBSERVATION THAT LOOKED LIKE A BUG AND IS NOT: with only 3dof the user reported the cubes seemed anchored to the headset because they could not walk around them. In 3dof the head has no position at all -- the pose log reads (0,0,0) for the whole session -- so translating the body cannot move anything and world-anchoring simply cannot be tested in that mode. Rotation, which IS reported, behaved correctly. USB2 BRANCH DROPPED AT 04:59, and this is the part worth remembering. journalctl -k shows the first 'usb 3-1: device not accepting address 2, error -71' at 04:59:08 with repeated failures after. lsusb then had only the SuperSpeed side (04b4:6504, 045e:0659); the whole USB2 branch (04b4:6506 hub, 03f0:0580 companion, 0bda:4c15 audio) was gone. THE KNOWN TRIGGER FOR THIS IS REPEATED monado-service RESTARTS (T039/T044/T052), and this session ran about ten of them. We caused it. The consequence is worse than losing the headset: every session started after that came up on the legacy builder's SIMULATED HMD, which still leases the connector, still logs 'found display mode' and still prints 'Socket ready'. Three restarts were spent diagnosing what looked like the T051 controller startup race -- 'left: <none>, right: <none>' -- when the real cause was that there was no WMR headset in the session at all. `grep 'Using builder'` is what distinguishes these and it should be the FIRST check when controllers come up as <none>, not the last. Everything measured before 04:59 ran on the real headset and stands, including the cube verification (its service started around 04:53). hello_xr patch 0016 replaces the controller cube with a three-axis gizmo so orientation is unambiguous; built but NOT seen, since the hardware went down before it could be shown.

modo: T149: everyday-system session #2 with a new USB-C adapter -- 0015's controller exposure fix corrected (slot mapping + values), real LED blob tracking confirmed live, clock-domain fix for constellation timestamps only partially closes the loop
veredicto: NEW USB-C-TO-USB-A ADAPTER HOLDS UP CLEAN. Swapped after the prior session's degrading-link pattern (reqCmd 23 + non-desktop:0). Full session: 5/5 USB enumeration throughout, zero reqCmd 23, zero USB2 branch drops -- the adapter is not the remaining bottleneck. Bringup itself was noisier than usual (3 of the first 4 launches hit vkAcquireXlibDisplayEXT: VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN or a slow wake_panel() probe timing out at 25s with no error; one failed run left a zombie monado-service that blocked the next launch's service_pids guard) -- all recovered with a clean stop+retry, reads as the ordinary display-acquire race the project already documents, not a repeat of last session's hardware wear. 0015 CORRECTED, TWO SEPARATE WRONG GUESSES FOUND AND FIXED. First, captured the WMR_LOG=trace measurement the previous session (T147/T148) left as the concrete next step: paired each frame's frame-type trace line with its exposure trace line over ~2400 samples -- frametype 2 (controller) read exposure=0 in 99.5% of frames, frametype 0 (SLAM) read exposure=450 in 100%, settling that the black controller stream is a real exposure=0 condition, not just absent blobs (also ruled out ambient light and controller positioning as confounds: 0 blobs across 30s of active controller movement, 0 across 30s with the room light off). Then applied 0015's own camera.c hunk (not yet committed on this branch) and confirmed via the same trace method that the +tcam_count slot mapping sends its exposure/gain command successfully (no USB error) but the frame's own embedded exposure readback stays 0 regardless -- ruling OUT '0015 just needs the frames to start arriving' and ruling IN 'the slot mapping itself is wrong', settling the question 0015's own commit message left open. Switched to a flat +2 (thaytan's original constant; this hardware's real camera location IDs are 0,1,4,5, not contiguous 0-3, so +tcam_count and +2 land on genuinely different slots) -- readback immediately went nonzero: 400 requested -> 20 read back, then 6000 requested -> 300 read back, both exactly /20, a clean and repeatable linear relationship confirming +2 addresses a real, controllable register. Readback nonzero alone wasn't enough: at thaytan's reference values (400 exposure / 1 gain) the debug panel was still fully black. Raised to 6000/100 and got real images -- 'Controller Blob Cam 0/1' went from solid black to showing LED blob clusters that moved live with the controller, user-confirmed repeatedly ('si! los veo!', 'ahi estan claros muchos de los puntos', 'veo que trackean!'). CONSTELLATION_TRACKER_LOG=trace then showed RANSAC-PnP actually recovering device poses, not just blob detection: 'Fast processing for device 0 succeeded with blob recovery' / 'RANSAC-PnP recovered pose for device 0 from 6 blobs' repeating continuously while the controller was held steady and visible, and constellation_sample_store's own periodic log showed a stable solve -- sample #2070, pos=(-0.039,-0.012,-0.130), matched_blobs=5, visible_leds=9, reprojection error 0.04-0.10px held across 2000+ consecutive samples. SEPARATE FINDING: blob visibility is intermittent right after power-on -- user observed the controllers' white LEDs light immediately but the red blob overlay sometimes takes a moment to catch up; not root-caused, flagged as possibly related to the LED strobe/camera-exposure sync t_led_sync_refinement.c exists to handle (see T147), not excluded. CLOCK-DOMAIN FIX, PARTIALLY CLOSED. With blobs and pose solving confirmed working, get_tracked_pose still reported position_tracked=no (placeholder) with a constant ~44.5 million ms (~12.4 hour) delta between at_timestamp_ns and the constellation sample's timestamp. Traced to a real, previously-unknown gap: the SLAM cam_sinks path (receive_cam0..3 in wmr_source.c) has always applied 'xf->timestamp += ws->cam_hw2mono' to convert the WMR hardware's raw device clock into Monado's host monotonic clock, but the controller-tracking frame path never had the same correction, so constellation sample timestamps stayed in the raw hardware clock the whole time -- unrelated to d6b84cda1's freshness-check abs() fix from the previous session, which was already correctly rejecting the resulting always-huge, always-stale delta. Added receive_ctrl_cam, mirroring the SLAM correction, wired in front of the controller-tracking blobwatch chain. Confirmed via temporary per-call tracing that the correction reaches CameraSample's constructor and Camera::pushPose's sample.timestamp_ns correctly -- but found a SECOND, NOT-understood bug in the same run: at that exact push_sample call site, the timestamp is consistently corrected for one device_id and consistently raw for the other, deterministically, across the whole session, despite both devices reaching that identical code path from the identical camera_sample.timestamp_ns field. Not a race, not transient, not explained by the wiring (checked: the per-camera sink loop is symmetric across all 4 cameras). get_tracked_pose still reports position_tracked=no for at least one controller as a result -- the exposure and blob-detection fixes are real and confirmed, but full positional 6DoF is not yet reaching the app-facing pose. ALSO FOUND, INCIDENTALLY: wmr_controller_base_get_tracked_pose's own diagnostic log (added 9c78bc346, previous session) used a function-local 'static' throttle counter shared across BOTH controllers, so it only ever logged whichever device's calls happened to land on the modulo-90 boundary -- silently hiding the other controller's output the entire session and very nearly hiding the device-specific bug above. Fixed to gate on the device's own sample_count instead. SYNC GAP FOUND: this session's 'git log' on the lab machine's actual g2-constellation-x11kde branch showed real committed history well past what patches/monado/ exports -- a 'Fuse constellation position into the controller's output pose' commit (332a57f27, referred to as work toward '0017' in later commit messages) and several logging/freshness-check commits already exist there, none exported as .patch files yet. Flagged in patches/monado/README.md so future sessions check git log directly rather than assuming the exported patch numbers are current. Patch 0016 (supersedes 0015, includes both the exposure/slot fix and the clock-domain fix, code comments document the unresolved device-specific bug in place) committed locally on the everyday-system monado checkout, not yet pushed anywhere (no fork remote configured there). LIGHT-LEVEL CALIBRATION STARTED, not concluded: user began raising room light gradually from dark, tracking blobs remained visible with a small amount of light added, even through a controller standby cycle -- session ended before finding the failure threshold to compare against the known-good Windows light level.

modo: T150: light-level calibration, dark -> normal living-room light, comparing against the known-good Windows level
veredicto: Raised room light gradually from dark (T149's state) up to normal full living-room brightness (not dim), watching Controller Blob Cam tracking the whole way, aiming to bracket the light level that's known to work fine on Windows. Tracking survived a controller standby->wake cycle even at full light. At full light, real false-positive blobs started appearing near bright ambient sources (lamps) -- distinct from the actual controller LED blobs, plausible given the short-exposure/low-gain design (T149) isolates LEDs by exposure alone, so any other sufficiently bright point can cross the same pixel_threshold. Deliberately NOT tuned this session -- noted as a known tradeoff, not chased, since without a working tracked pose (see T149's unresolved device-specific clock bug) there's no way to judge whether a given threshold change actually reduces false tracking versus just reducing the debug panel's dot count. Revisit pixel_threshold/blob_required_threshold (RIFT_BLOBWATCH_PIXEL_THRESHOLD_CV1 and friends in wmr_source.c) once T149 is resolved.

modo: T151: root-causing and fixing the device-specific clock-domain bug left open by T149
veredicto: The 'device-specific' timestamp bug from T149 was never device-specific -- it was a container_of misuse. receive_ctrl_cam (wmr_source.c) recovered `struct wmr_source *ws` via container_of(sink, struct wmr_source, ctrl_ts_fix_sinks), where `sink` was &ws->ctrl_ts_fix_sinks[i] for camera index i. container_of only computes the right enclosing pointer when the passed pointer is the START of the named field. For i==0 that happens to hold (array's own address == its first element's address), so camera 0 always got a correct `ws` and a correctly hw2mono-corrected timestamp. For i>0, the recovered `ws` silently pointed i*sizeof(xrt_frame_sink) bytes into the real struct, reading garbage for cam_hw2mono, AND cam_id computed from the same broken math resolved to exactly 0 regardless of i by construction -- confirmed with a temporary per-call trace: 12947/12948 calls to receive_ctrl_cam logged cam_id=0, literally never any other value, across all 4 physical cameras. Since the two controllers are seen predominantly by different physical cameras, this looked exactly like a 'works for one device, not the other' bug in T149's trace. Fixed by wrapping each camera's sink in its own `struct wmr_ctrl_ts_fix_sink` (sink as first member, explicit `ws`/`downstream` pointers set once at wiring time) so container_of recovers the correct instance regardless of array index -- no dependency on the caller's pointer happening to equal the array's base address. Also found and fixed a separate operational gap while investigating: WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS is NOT exported by jack-in.sh, so a bare relaunch silently runs with the entire controller-tracking path off (must be exported manually, e.g. `WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS=1 ./jack-in.sh`) -- worth wiring into the script itself later. Verified live twice (including a full clean rebuild + relaunch to rule out stale state): pushPose's cam_sample_ts now lands 5-40ms behind os_monotonic_get_ns() for every device/camera combination sampled (device 0 via cameras 0 and 2, device 1 via cameras 1 and 3), all comfortably inside the 200ms freshness window. Ran hello_xr to drive real get_tracked_pose calls: both controllers report position_tracked=yes consistently, with distinct, stable positions per device (e.g. device A settling around (0.11, 0.08, 0.17), device B around (-0.16, -0.02, -0.24)), not intermittently and not for only one controller. This closes the last open item from T149/patch 0016 -- constellation-based 6DoF controller positional tracking is now fully working end to end on this hardware, from raw exposure/blob detection through to a fresh, correctly-clocked pose reaching get_tracked_pose. See patch 0017 in patches/monado/.

modo: T152: build xrizer from scratch on the everyday system, attempt to run Aircar (OpenVR) through it
veredicto:
Aircar (851MB, owned, not previously installed on this machine) was chosen as the 'simple game' to test after tonight's constellation-tracking fixes, since it's the project's own best-verified OpenVR title on the lab machine ('first game I'd call 99%'). xrizer was never set up on this machine before -- built from scratch: rustup (stable 1.97.1), then cargo build --release needed three missing apt packages not previously documented as needed here (glslc, libclang-dev, libxcb-glx0-dev -- the xcb/glx.h header specifically). Build succeeded clean at xrizer's current upstream HEAD (dd0da05); the project's own pinned SHA (6c3e45f) no longer exists in the repo's history (rewritten/rebased upstream), and the two local patches (0001 global-recenter, 0002 system-path alias) fail to apply against current HEAD (missing files like meta_touch_plus.rs, vive_focus3.rs -- real upstream restructuring, not just line drift). Proceeded WITHOUT those two patches (they're interaction polish, not blocking) -- flagged as a real gap for whoever picks this up: xrizer needs re-patching or the patches need rebasing against current upstream. i386 NVIDIA libs (nvidia-driver-libs:i386) and libopenxr-loader1 were already present system-wide from a prior session, so neither of the two traps docs/06 documented for the lab's original xrizer bring-up applied here. 

Configured openvrpaths.vrpath to point at the xrizer build. First launch attempt used per-game Steam Launch Options with VR_OVERRIDE + IPC_IGNORE_VERSION omitted (a mistake, not copying the project's own documented canonical launch options from docs/23) -- game ran fine in flat 2D via gamepad, zero xrizer log ever created, zero Monado IPC client connection. Corrected to the project's canonical launch options (XR_RUNTIME_JSON + IPC_IGNORE_VERSION=1 + PRESSURE_VESSEL_FILESYSTEMS_RW, no VR_OVERRIDE) -- still flat 2D, still zero xrizer log. Discovered along the way: Steam silently RE-ADDS the SteamVR entry to ~/.config/openvr/openvrpaths.vrpath's runtime array on every Steam client startup (not documented anywhere in this project before) -- has to be fixed AFTER Steam is already running, and stays fixed only until the next Steam restart. Also found a Proton-prefix-local copy of openvrpaths.vrpath (compatdata/<appid>/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/AppData/Local/openvr/openvrpaths.vrpath) that Proton regenerates into a fixed 'C:\vrclient' entry on every launch, seemingly independent of which path the Linux-side file lists -- this is Proton's own openvr-to-native bridge mechanism, not a config bug, but wasn't documented here before either. 

Tried the project's OWN documented 'export the 3 vars before starting Steam itself' technique (docs/23, validated working for VersaillesVR on 2026-08-09) -- confirmed via /proc/<pid>/environ that all 3 vars correctly reached the actual Windows game process this time. Still flat 2D, still zero xrizer log. Added VR_OVERRIDE as a 4th exported var (xrizer's own upstream README recommends it specifically for the Steam Linux Runtime/Proton case) -- confirmed present on the Steam client process itself, but consistently STRIPPED before reaching the actual game binary (reproduced twice) -- Proton or pressure-vessel appears to consume/filter this specific var name, likely to build the C:\vrclient bridge internally rather than passing it through raw. Tried appending a '-vr' launch argument (common UE4 pattern to force VR mode past an auto-detect heuristic) -- confirmed present in the real process's command line, zero effect, identical flat main-menu flythrough screen both with and without it. User manually checked the in-game menu for a VR toggle -- none found. 

Final diagnostic before stopping: enabled PROTON_LOG=1/PROTON_LOG_DIR and relaunched -- the resulting Wine trace log (~1MB) is the first real evidence the whole session: the game's own bundled openvr_api.dll (OpenVRv1_0_16) DOES load, and DOES load C:\vrclient\bin\vrclient_x64.dll (xrizer's actual Proton bridge) -- 4 load/unload cycles logged in quick succession, meaning the OpenVR init handshake is being attempted and is failing/retrying repeatedly, not being skipped entirely as every earlier symptom (zero xrizer log) suggested. The game process then exited on its own after ~9 seconds (new behavior -- every prior attempt ran indefinitely in flat 2D instead). No exception or clear error visible in the trace tail (ends mid-normal .NET/Mono DllMain startup sequence, looks like an ordinary process handoff, not an obvious crash line) -- would need a narrower WINEDEBUG channel (e.g. +ntdll+seh, or hooking the specific vrclient_x64.dll entry points) to isolate why the handshake fails, genuinely deeper Wine/Proton debugging than tonight's scope. 

STOPPED HERE, by explicit user choice, in favor of validating 6DoF visually via hello_xr instead for tonight -- this is a real, partially-characterized, NOT-fixed gap, not a dead end: the bridge DLL loading proves xrizer is reachable from this game on this machine, so the remaining problem is inside the OpenVR init handshake itself (either xrizer's own VR_InitInternal, or something about how this specific game's older OpenVR SDK version 1.0.16 calls it), not the launch plumbing that consumed most of tonight's time. Concrete next step for whoever resumes this: re-run with PROTON_LOG=1 and grep the full ~1MB trace (not just the vrclient lines) for anything between the last vrclient_x64.dll load and the process exit ~9s later -- or add WINEDEBUG=+seh to catch the actual exception, if any. Also worth trying a DIFFERENT already-validated Proton title (SUPERHOT, Propagation VR) to check whether this is Aircar-specific (e.g. its older OpenVR SDK version) or a general xrizer-on-this-machine regression.

modo: T153: head-tracking jitter check after tonight's constellation-tracking work, quantified with HELLO_XR_POSE_STATS=1
veredicto:
User reported noticeable head-tracking jitter while viewing the static-image player tonight, worse than the historical baseline (docs/22 T045: mean 0.0003-0.0016 deg/frame, max 0.056 deg at rest). First measurement (service still running with WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS=1, ~18 background Steam/Proton/Wine processes still alive from the earlier xrizer/Aircar investigation, system load average 13.75 on a 6-core/12-thread machine): mean 0.006-0.060 deg/frame, max up to 1.00 deg -- roughly 4-40x the documented baseline. Killed Steam entirely (18 -> 4 background processes) -- user's subjective read: 'still quite noticeable, but maybe 50% better.' 

Hypothesis tested: constellation controller tracking (4 extra blobwatch/RANSAC-PnP threads per camera, running continuously whenever WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS=1) competing for CPU with Basalt's own SLAM optimization threads, since the historical baseline was measured before constellation tracking existed on this branch. Restarted monado-service WITHOUT WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS (confirmed unset via /proc/<pid>/environ) and re-measured. Result: NOT confirmed as the sole cause. With controllers fully powered off and the user explicitly not touching anything, most 2-second windows land at or near the documented baseline (max exactly 0.056 deg several times, matching the historical measurement byte-for-byte) -- but real, isolated spikes still appear interspersed (max 0.42, 1.38, 1.57, 2.14 deg across a ~20s clean-rest window), with neither constellation tracking nor controller power transitions active to explain them. A separate, noisier window (taken while the user was describing what they were observing, so possibly correlated with real controller state changes at the time, not isolated) showed much larger spikes (max 3.66, 9.38, 14.18, 5.68 deg) -- consistent with the user's own report that controller standby-wake specifically triggers a visible 'ajuste' (adjustment snap), but not proven in isolation since that window wasn't a clean single-variable test.
