Net read: two separate things are probably both real and NOT yet fully separated: (1) a residual, low-amplitude jitter spike pattern that persists even in the cleanest possible condition (no controllers, no constellation tracking, motionless) -- cause unknown, candidates include Basalt's own periodic keyframe marginalization/bundle-adjustment bursts, or general system scheduling noise from remaining background processes (Firefox with many tabs was still running throughout); (2) a much larger, controller-standby-wake-correlated spike the user directly observed and described, not yet isolated with a clean before/after measurement pinned to the exact moment of standby-wake. NOT root-caused tonight -- stopped here given how much of the session was already spent on the xrizer/Aircar investigation. Concrete next step: a controlled test with a fixed timestamp log of exactly when a controller wakes from standby, cross-referenced against the pose-stats windows at that exact moment, done with WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS unset (as here) to isolate the standby-wake effect from the constellation-tracking-CPU-contention effect, which this session's evidence suggests is a real but separate, smaller contributor.

modo: T154: test a SECOND already-lab-verified title (Aliens Attack VR, 932190) on the everyday system/KDE, to determine whether Aircar (T152) failing to connect to xrizer here is title-specific or a general regression
driver: User wanted to contribute real test coverage for the KDE/X11 environment specifically, since almost every 'Working' row in docs/23-game-compatibility.md was only ever validated on the lab machine (GNOME/Wayland/90Hz). Chose Aliens Attack VR because it already has a clean confirmed working row there (one harmless IVRChaperoneSetup_005 warning aside), making it a clean idea/procedure/diagnostic test: same title, same xrizer version family, only the OS/desktop/compositor/refresh-rate axis changes.
veredicto: IDEA: reuse Aircar bring-up (T152) infra -- openvrpaths.vrpath already points at this machine's xrizer build, canonical launch options already known -- and just swap in a different, already-lab-verified title to isolate title-specific vs. environment-wide failure. PROCEDURE: installed Aliens Attack VR (851MB) fresh via Steam; since Steam was already running (mid-install, could not restart without losing progress), set launch options through the per-game Steam UI (Properties -> Launch Options) rather than the pre-Steam-start env-export trick, per the documented trap in docs/23 ("editing launch options on disk while Steam runs does nothing"). Exact launch options used: XR_RUNTIME_JSON=/home/brunduk/Documents/linux_vr_base/monado/build/openxr_monado-dev.json IPC_IGNORE_VERSION=1 PRESSURE_VESSEL_FILESYSTEMS_RW=/run/user/1000/monado_comp_ipc %command%. Confirmed live socket present (/run/user/1000/monado_comp_ipc) and monado-service running before launch. DIAGNOSTIC: launched -- game ran fine in flat 2D on the desktop monitor (gamepad-controllable, matching Aircar's first-launch shape), headset panel stayed powered on but showed nothing. Checked three independent signals, all confirming the same non-connection: (1) jack-in.log shows zero new client_connected/client_disconnected pair for this launch -- the only such pair in the entire 714k-line log is stale, from an earlier hello_xr session, not this one; (2) ~/.local/state/xrizer/xrizer.txt does not exist anywhere on the filesystem (searched from /), meaning xrizer never even opened its own log file; (3) confirmed the Proton-side plumbing itself is NOT the problem -- compatdata/932190/pfx/drive_c/vrclient/bin/vrclient_x64.dll and vrclient.dll are present (built during this same bring-up), and the prefix-local openvrpaths.vrpath correctly lists C:\vrclient as the runtime, matching the working Aircar setup exactly. This is the SAME symptom shape Aircar showed before PROTON_LOG revealed the DLL was at least being loaded/unloaded 4 times -- so the working hypothesis going in was that Aliens Attack VR would show the identical load/unload-then-exit pattern once traced, which would be strong confirmation this is a general xrizer-on-this-machine regression, not anything specific to Aircar's older OpenVR SDK version. PROCESS-HYGIENE NOTE: the game process was cleanly closed by the assistant directly (SIGTERM to the game .exe PID, then its orphaned gameoverlayui companion process, both verified gone via pgrep before relaunching with PROTON_LOG=1 added) instead of asking the user to close it via the Steam UI -- explicit user instruction this session to reduce user-facing friction on this kind of step going forward. NEXT STEP: PROTON_LOG=1 + PROTON_LOG_DIR added to launch options, relaunched; trace analysis and final verdict to follow in a subsequent entry. PLAN IF THE RELAUNCH STILL SHOWS ZERO CONNECTION (stated explicitly, per user instruction, before the result was known): stop chasing this on the everyday/KDE machine and resume validation on the dev/lab machine (GNOME/Wayland/90Hz/patched), where the full game sweep is already confirmed working -- this environment/title pairing is not worth more diagnostic time than Aircar already cost if a second title reproduces the identical failure.

modo: T155: relaunched Aliens Attack VR with PROTON_LOG=1 to compare against Aircar's T152 trace; when that relaunch also came back empty, researched whether the everyday-system xrizer non-connection is a known external NVIDIA/Proton/OpenXR bug class rather than a project-specific one
driver: Wanted the PROTON_LOG confirmation to close out T154's open question (does Aliens Attack VR show the same load/unload-then-exit vrclient_x64.dll pattern Aircar did), and wanted to check public sources for anyone else hitting silent OpenXR-in-Proton non-connection on NVIDIA before assuming this project's own xrizer build or patches are at fault.
veredicto:
FIRST RELAUNCH ATTEMPT FAILED TO ACTUALLY TEST ANYTHING: verified via /proc/<pid>/environ on the live Proton process that PROTON_LOG and PROTON_LOG_DIR were NOT present -- only the 3 usual vars (XR_RUNTIME_JSON, IPC_IGNORE_VERSION, PRESSURE_VESSEL_FILESYSTEMS_RW) made it through, meaning the Launch Options edit didn't fully save/apply that round. Process was cleanly killed by the assistant directly (SIGTERM to the game .exe, then its orphaned gameoverlayui companion, verified gone via pgrep) -- second instance of the new process-hygiene habit from T154 (assistant closes Steam-launched game processes on request instead of asking the user to do it by hand, to cut UI friction). User re-set the launch options; second relaunch is pending re-verification of PROTON_LOG reaching the process this time -- not yet confirmed live in this entry, deferred to a follow-up T-entry once the trace is actually captured.

EXTERNAL RESEARCH (WebSearch + WebFetch, not project-specific): checked whether NVIDIA + Proton + OpenXR (the exact combination underlying every xrizer/Monado bring-up on this machine and the lab machine) has known, unresolved bugs independent of this project's own code. Found three real, currently-open reports: (1) ValveSoftware/steam-runtime issue #782 -- pressure-vessel's graphics-drivers-openxr-1.c reprocesses the active OpenXR runtime json when PRESSURE_VESSEL_IMPORT_OPENXR_1_RUNTIMES=1 is set, and the reporter's own example shows a Monado-specific vendor field (MND_libmonado_path) silently disappearing after that reprocessing. This project does NOT set that env var, so this exact code path is probably not firing for us -- but it's concrete precedent that pressure-vessel is known to silently mangle custom/vendor OpenXR runtime json fields for Monado specifically in other configurations, which is at least directionally consistent with a silent, log-free non-connection like ours. No fix, no workaround documented, issue open. (2) ValveSoftware/Proton issue #7228 -- 'VR applications fail to load OpenXR library with stack overflow in Proton 8.0+', NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti / driver 535.113.01, stack overflow inside libopenxr_loader.so.1. Different failure SHAPE than ours (this one hangs visibly, stuck as 'Next Up' in SteamVR with repeated 'VR state wait timeout' warnings -- we don't use SteamVR at all, xrizer replaces it, and our processes exit cleanly with zero warnings logged anywhere) but same underlying trigger category (Proton probing/loading the OpenXR loader on NVIDIA). Open, unresolved, no fix. (3) NVIDIA Developer Forums thread (RTX 3060, driver 550.76 -- one version-family away from this rig's own 550.163.01) -- 'entire graphics stack crashes' launching Proton titles that target OpenXR (Beat Saber, Ancient Dungeon), reproduced with BOTH SteamVR and Monado as the runtime, confirmed absent on AMD hardware. Reporter's own words: 'if I can't get any traction on this issue I'll be switching to AMD hardware.' Open, unresolved, no workaround found.

CONCLUSION, stated explicitly: none of the three is a symptom-for-symptom match (all three describe a visible crash/hang; ours is a silent, log-free non-connection with a clean process exit) -- so this is corroborating context, not a root-cause find. But it meaningfully shifts the prior toward 'general NVIDIA+Proton+OpenXR fragility on this specific machine/driver combination', independent of anything in this project's own xrizer patches or Monado build, and away from 'something we broke'. Doesn't change the plan already agreed with the user: if Aliens Attack VR's PROTON_LOG trace (once actually captured) matches Aircar's load/unload-then-exit pattern, stop chasing this on the everyday/KDE machine and resume on the dev/lab machine where the full sweep already works. CONCRETE FOLLOW-UP if this is picked up again: inspect the OpenXR runtime json as the process actually sees it INSIDE the pressure-vessel sandbox (not the original file on disk) to check whether any fields are silently stripped even without PRESSURE_VESSEL_IMPORT_OPENXR_1_RUNTIMES set -- not yet done this session.

modo: T156: LAB MACHINE -- 'nothing graphical starts' after an automatic boot was a lost VT, not a broken session; plus a measured breakdown of boot-to-desktop time (the 25s stall is a upower D-Bus activation race, not GNOME). Also: this session opened on a checkout 15 commits behind origin -- see the last paragraph, it is the most important part of this entry
veredicto: SYMPTOM: after a fully automatic boot the user reported no graphical session at all. NOTHING WAS BROKEN. GNOME had autologged in correctly and was running the entire time: sddm-helper logged 'Starting Wayland user session: /etc/sddm/wayland-session /usr/bin/gnome-session' and 'Session started true' at 00:30:51, loginctl showed session 1 on tty3 with Type=wayland, and gnome-session-binary (1341), gnome-shell (1463) and Xwayland (1912) were all alive. The only thing wrong was WHICH VT was on screen: /sys/class/tty/tty0/active read tty2, and session 1 (tty3) had Active=no. Ctrl+Alt+F3 restored the desktop instantly, user-confirmed ('confirmado, corriendo' / 'si, volvio bien'). THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SETTLES THIS CLASS OF REPORT IN ONE COMMAND: cat /sys/class/tty/tty0/active, compared against loginctl's TTY column for the wayland session. If they differ, the desktop is fine and only the console focus is wrong -- do not debug sddm, GNOME or the driver. HOW THE FOCUS GOT LOST: the pipeline chvt's to tty4 for the picker. vr-launcher-console.service ran its picker from 00:30:54 (runuser session opened) to 00:32:36, then exited status=1/FAILURE; systemd restarted the unit and tty4 is now a bare agetty. So a picker crash leaves the visible VT on a console with no path back to the graphical session on tty3 -- which is exactly how a picker bug presents itself to the user as 'nothing graphical boots'. TWO OPEN ITEMS FROM THIS: (a) why the picker exited 1 is unknown, because /tmp/vr-launcher-console-debug.log is EMPTY and StandardOutput=tty swallowed the rest -- the same debuggability hole T108-T141 already paid for once; (b) nothing returns the VT to the graphical session when the picker dies. A chvt back to the GNOME VT on the picker's exit path would turn this failure from 'the machine did not boot' into 'the picker did not come up'. WHY BOOT-TO-DESKTOP FEELS SLOW -- three independent components, measured, only one of which is real: (1) systemd-analyze reports 'Startup finished in 24.331s (kernel) + 2.280s (userspace)'. The 24.3s is NOT time Linux spent booting: the first kernel line in journalctl -k (the 'Linux version' banner) already carries monotonic [24.885810], and an awk scan for gaps >0.8s across the whole kernel log found NONE. So that figure is a constant baseline offset sitting before the kernel's first message -- most likely firmware/POST time included via the TSC-derived clock on this Ryzen board, which is a known effect there. NOT PROVEN (raw dmesg needs root and returned nothing), but the 'no gaps anywhere in the kernel log' measurement rules out Linux itself being slow either way. Real userspace boot to multi-user.target is 2.26s. (2) vr-boot-selector.service ran 19.804s -- its own 10s countdown plus the power-on hardware gate. Expected, by design. (3) THE ONE THAT MATTERS: a 25-second stall inside the user session. systemd-analyze --user blame puts xdg-desktop-portal.service at 25.166s and org.gnome.SettingsDaemon.MediaKeys.service at 25.127s, and gsd-media-keys logs the cause verbatim: "Error calling StartServiceByName for org.freedesktop.UPower: Failed to activate service 'org.freedesktop.UPower': timed out (service_start_timeout=25000ms)". This is what held gnome-session.target back from 00:30:54 to 00:31:19. ROOT CAUSE OF THE STALL, and it is a RACE, not a misconfiguration: upower.service is started, logs 'Deactivated successfully' 0.66s later (idle exit), and is then re-activated -- but on this boot the re-activation did not land until 00:31:19.052, exactly one 25s D-Bus activation timeout after the client asked. Checked across boots -1, -2 and -3: the identical start -> deactivate -> restart cycle happens EVERY boot, but there the restart lands 100-200ms after the exit and the whole thing costs ~1.4s. So the same code path is either ~1.4s or ~25s depending on timing. It is intermittent and it is not GNOME's fault. Not fixed; the obvious lever if it recurs is to stop upowerd from idle-exiting during session startup, but that has not been tried or measured. USER REPORT, PARKED, NOT INVESTIGATED: the automatic-mode shortcut never works from console sessions -- 'en sesiones de consola nunca puedo prender el modo automatico, falla el atajo'. Deferred by the user to a later session. The boot in question was NOT touched by hand ('no toque nada, todo automatico'), so everything above describes the unattended path as it actually behaves. ENVIRONMENT NOTE, because the repo now spans two machines: everything above was measured on the LAB SSD (patched 595-open, GNOME on Wayland, the boot-selector/autologin/tty4 pipeline), NOT the everyday system that T149-T155 were run on. AND THE REAL LESSON OF THIS SESSION, which outweighs the findings above: this checkout was 15 commits BEHIND origin/main for the whole session and nobody noticed until the user asked whether the repo was synced. T149-T155 had been run and pushed from the everyday system. Reading CLAUDE.md, NEXT-STEP.md and pruebas.jsonl from this disk therefore produced a stale picture of the project, and two concrete failures followed: (1) the USB-C adapter swap was re-documented from scratch as if unrecorded, when origin already had it in docs/22 with exact part numbers (HP L56522-002 -> Nisuta NSADU30UC, commit e25f0c0) and its own fault-signature row for the reqCmd23/non-desktop:0 cluster -- the local write-up actively asserted 'not recorded' about recorded facts; (2) the IDs T149 and T150 were allocated locally while both already existed upstream meaning entirely different tests. Both were caught before any commit; the redundant adapter entry was discarded and this one renumbered. ROOT CAUSE, and it is mechanical, not a lapse of attention: scripts/testlog.py allocates the next ID by counting rows in the LOCAL docs/pruebas.jsonl (`"id": f"T{n:03d}"`, line 46). With two machines pushing to one repo, a checkout that is behind will silently hand out an ID that already exists. Nothing in the tooling or the docs told anyone to fetch first. STANDING RULE ADDED FROM THIS: `git fetch` and check behind/ahead BEFORE reading any project doc as current state, and never trust a test ID allocated on a checkout that is behind origin.

modo: T157: LAB MACHINE -- rebuilding Monado from patches/ exposed that the tracked series cannot build the lab binary: 0016/0017 do not apply, and the 90 Hz patch had been silently missing from every clean rebuild since 2026-08-08
veredicto: WHY THIS WAS DONE: patches 0016/0017 were developed on the everyday system and pushed; this machine's ~/vr/monado was still at 0015, so any controller-tracking measurement here would have measured the wrong code -- the T068 drift trap. The rebuild was meant to be routine. It found two separate real problems. PROBLEM 1 -- THE 90 Hz PATCH WAS MISSING FROM THE LAB BINARY, AND HAD BEEN FOR FOUR DAYS. The branch actually built and run since 2026-08-08 (`lab-verified`, 15 commits from the pinned SHA 735e29e4e = a clean git am of 0001-0015) does NOT contain bf3a2e4b9 'd/wmr: Set 90 Hz nominal frame interval on WMR HMD screens'. The older, drifted `lab` branch DOES. Mechanism: that patch is third-party (Project-VR, authored by Ashish Kumar Singh) and was never exported into patches/monado/ -- it lived only as a prose footnote at the bottom of patches/monado/README.md ('Still needed on top for 90 Hz testing'). So when T068 rebuilt clean from patches/ to escape the drift, the clean rebuild silently dropped it, and every lab binary built from patches/ between 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-12 ran without it. What the patch does: sets screens[0].nominal_frame_interval_ns = 1e9/90, which u_extents_2d_split_side_by_side() leaves at 0, so a downstream consumer computes refresh = 1/0 = infinite and falls back to 60 Hz. SCOPE CAVEAT, stated because it is not measured: the commit message names the SteamVR driver bridge as that consumer, NOT the native OpenXR path -- whether its absence was visible through jack-in-wayland.sh/hello_xr or xrizer was never tested, so no claim is made that this fixed anything observable. FIXED PROPERLY: exported as patches/monado/0018-d-wmr-Set-90-Hz-nominal-frame-interval-on-WMR-HMD-sc.patch, given its own table row, and the README footnote struck through with the reason. A patch the build needs belongs in the series, not in a sentence. PROBLEM 2 -- patches/monado 0016 AND 0017 DO NOT APPLY, AND THE README SAID THEY DID. The README claimed 'All seventeen apply with plain git am onto the pinned SHA and build with zero warnings.' Measured from scratch onto 735e29e4e: 0001-0015 apply clean, then 0016 fails on three files at once (wmr_camera.c:37, wmr_controller_base.c:576, wmr_source.c:74). Three independent confirmations that this is divergent history, not a context conflict to hand-resolve: (a) two of 0016's own pre-image blobs do not exist in this repository at all (0eaa8be3e for wmr_controller_base.c, a0f87946f for wmr_source.c) -- they were generated against commits that were never exported; (b) DECISIVE: 0016 tries to ADD lines to wmr_camera.c that the exported 0015 ALREADY CONTAINS (DEBUG_GET_ONCE_BOOL_OPTION(wmr_constellation_controllers, ...)), so 0016 was generated against a different 0015 than the one exported; (c) consistent with both, the exported 0015 still carries exactly the values 0016 is documented to correct (DEFAULT_CTRL_EXPOSURE 0x0190 = 400, DEFAULT_CTRL_GAIN 0x0001 = 1, slot offset `camera_id + cam->tcam_count`), and ctrl_ts_fix_sinks -- the struct 0017 fixes -- does not exist in this tree's wmr_source.c at all. The README's own 'known sync gap' note was therefore not a footnote: it makes the series unbuildable. patches/monado/ currently cannot reproduce the lab build, which is the only reason that directory exists. Same failure class as T068. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: hand-applying 0016/0017's intent onto this series. That is precisely what caused T068 and a week of controller tests against the wrong binary. The fix is a consistent re-export from the checkout where 0016/0017 were developed -- work for that machine, not something to fake here. RESULT: branch lab-90hz-0017 = 0001-0015 + 0018 (16 commits), ninja exit 0, ZERO warnings, nominal_frame_interval_ns confirmed present at wmr_hmd.c:2101. Verified the launcher uses exactly this binary (jack-in-wayland.sh:34 points at $VR/monado/build/...; no /usr/local/bin or /usr/bin copy exists to shadow it) rather than assuming it. Consequence for planning: controller constellation tracking (0016/0017) cannot be validated on this machine until the series is re-exported.

modo: T158: LAB MACHINE, long hardware session -- 90Hz/3dof/audio/Aircar all verified live; and a Proton-VR framerate collapse (13-18 fps in EVERY title) narrowed by elimination to the 2026-08-09 kernel+NVIDIA rebuild, with the previous kernel still installed for a clean A/B
veredicto: ALL OF THE FOLLOWING WERE PHYSICALLY VERIFIED BY THE USER WEARING THE HEADSET, per the project's core rule. (1) 90 Hz, NO FLICKER, on the freshly rebuilt binary (0001-0015 + 0018): 'no parpadea nada, 90hz clavados'. The project's central goal, re-confirmed. (2) 3dof session fully good: world stable, in-headset camera correct, and the CONTROLLER AXIS GIZMOS SEEN FOR THE FIRST TIME -- hello_xr patch 0016's three-axis gizmo was recorded in T148 as 'built but NOT seen'; it is now seen and rotating correctly. (3) HEADSET AUDIO WORKS AND ITS CHANNELS ARE CORRECT: hard-panned tones, low tone left / high tone right, user confirmed 'solo un tono por oido, mas grave a la izquierda, mas agudo a la derecha'. Test material was verified by measurement first (ffmpeg astats: -21 dB on the live channel, -inf on the silent one) so a channel-swap could not be blamed on the file. (4) AIRCAR RUNS ON THIS MACHINE -- 3D, head tracking and audio, 'si, perfecto'. (5) The VR-controller stick drift was fixed by WMR_STICK_DEADZONE=0.15, user: 'nada de drift o MUY poco'. AIRCAR CLOSES AN OPEN QUESTION FROM NEXT-STEP. The standing plan said that if Aliens Attack reproduced Aircar's non-connection on the everyday/KDE machine, the work should move to the lab machine 'where the full game sweep is already confirmed working'. Aircar reached client_connected + BEGIN_SESSION here on the first try, where T152 saw ZERO client_connected. So the Aircar/xrizer failure is specific to the everyday system, NOT a general xrizer or Monado bug. Stop chasing it there. USER-DIAGNOSED, AGENT WAS WRONG: the drift. The agent measured the Xbox pad's evdev axes (resting offsets 1809-2697 against a declared deadzone `Flat` of only 128, i.e. 14-21x) and concluded the pad was the cause. The user pointed out the game uses the VR controllers AND the pad simultaneously and that the VR sticks were the likely source. He was right, and patch 0008's own comment corroborates it: 'WMR controller configs carry NO stick centre calibration'. WMR_STICK_DEADZONE=0.15 fixed it -- the FIRST live hardware validation of patch 0008 for this purpose. The pad's own offset is real and still unaddressed, but it was not what he was feeling. THE MAIN UNSOLVED PROBLEM: EVERY Proton VR title runs at 13-18 fps. Aircar 13, International Space Station Tour VR 16-18. Signature: the DXVK submit thread pegged at 85-92% of ONE core while the GPU sits at 4-45% utilisation. RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT, each one a separate experiment with no effect on framerate: display mode (4320x2160 vs 2880x1440); render scale (3024x3024 -> 2160x2160 per eye, half the pixels); GPU clocks (870 -> 1770 MHz via PowerMizer); background load (Firefox closed, ~41% CPU freed -- dxvk-submit went UP, not down); Monado's verbose logging (49 KB/s of [control_read_packets] from the realtime USB callback, taken to 0 bytes/s -- the user's audio crackle every 2-3 s made this look promising and it was not it); Proton version (experimental-11.0-20260805, unchanged since 2026-08-08, the day the games worked, and only one version installed); title-specific causes (two unrelated titles, same numbers). xrizer's own log is clean: reaches FOCUSED, both hands on oculus/touch_controller, no errors and no fallback path. THE CONTRAST THAT LOCATES THE FAULT: hello_xr -- a NATIVE OpenXR client, no Proton, no DXVK, no xrizer -- ran perfectly at 90 Hz in this same session, and did so at 140% supersampling (3024x3024 per eye, 18 MP/frame) WITH the verbose logging still on. The VR stack, the compositor, the driver's display path and the machine are therefore all fine. The fault is entirely inside Proton -> DXVK -> xrizer -> OpenXR. LEADING HYPOTHESIS, from timeline elimination rather than from a mechanism: the games last worked 2026-08-08 05:25 (four titles, T068-T081). On 2026-08-09 17:30 the system took kernel 6.12.101 and NVIDIA 595.71.05 was rebuilt by DKMS for it (T109). T108/T109 then verified only the NATIVE player after that update -- it was perfect, and it is still perfect today. NO Proton title has been run between that update and today. So the kernel+driver rebuild is the ONLY untested change across the boundary, and it is exactly the kind of change that would hit DXVK/Vulkan while leaving the native path untouched. Corroborating detail noticed before the timeline was: Aircar's DXVK_state_cache directory is EMPTY and dated 2026-08-09 04:37 -- consistent with a driver change invalidating the shader cache. THE A/B IS AVAILABLE AND CLEAN: /boot/vmlinuz-6.12.100+deb13-amd64 is still installed and /lib/modules/6.12.100+deb13-amd64/updates/dkms/nvidia.ko.xz is already built for it. Reboot, pick 6.12.100 in GRUB, launch any Proton VR title. If the framerate returns, the cause is the update; if not, the whole kernel/driver line is eliminated and the remaining suspect is the DXVK->OpenXR texture handoff itself. NOT YET RUN. SIDE FINDINGS WORTH THEIR OWN LINES. (a) RECONFIGURING THE MONITORS SILENTLY RESETS POWERMIZER TO ADAPTIVE. Forced to maximum performance the SM clock sits at 1770-1995 MHz; after the user changed the primary display it was back at 555 MHz -- 26% of the card's 2115 MHz maximum -- with nothing reporting it. Any 'it used to run better' report should check clocks.sm before anything else. (b) nvidia-settings LIES about it: after a successful 'assigned value 1' the query still returns GPUPowerMizerMode=0 and nvidia-smi still reports pstate P3 while the SM clock has plainly doubled. Trust clocks.sm, not the attribute and not the pstate. (c) MONADO SUPERSAMPLES 140% BY DEFAULT: comp_settings.c:34, XRT_COMPOSITOR_SCALE_PERCENTAGE default 140, which is where 2160x2160 native becomes 3024x3024 per eye. It is driven by the device's native panel, NOT by the display mode, which is why lowering the video mode changes nothing about render cost. (d) MONADO HAS NO FOV-CROP OPTION. Checked all 240 of its DEBUG_GET_ONCE options and the runtime source: the only levers are XRT_COMPOSITOR_SCALE_PERCENTAGE and OXR_VIEWPORT_SCALE_PERCENTAGE, both uniform scalers. SteamVR's tangent-multiplier style peripheral crop -- trimming the edges the lenses barely show, which the user reports is free performance up to a point -- does not exist here. The FOV is assembled at wmr_hmd.c:2114, so there is a clear place for a patch. Real gap, not yet filed. (e) TRAP, COST REAL TIME TONIGHT: `pw-play --target <id|name>` accepts the target, exits 0, and routes NOWHERE -- the sink never leaves SUSPENDED. `paplay --device=<name>` works and the sink goes to IDLE/RUNNING. Three 'successful' silent playbacks were blamed on the hardware before this was found. Always confirm the sink state changed, never trust exit 0. (f) The pgrep self-match trap in CLAUDE.md bit twice, both times because the agent's own echo string contained the literal process name -- `pgrep -f "monado[-]service"` is not enough if the same command echoes "monado-service" in plain text. (g) PipeWire's stream-restore remembers a per-application sink: after moving Aircar's stream to the headset once, it returned there by itself across a Monado restart. ADAPTER/NISUTA WATCH (the T150/docs22 open item): this session ran FOUR full monado-service restart cycles plus several Steam/Proton launches -- the restart-heavy pattern that used to trigger the USB2 branch. Result: ZERO 'error -71', ZERO 'Cannot enable', ZERO USB2 drops across the entire boot, and reqCmd 23 appeared exactly ONCE, on the very first service start, never again. docs/22 characterises the fault as reqCmd 23 RECURRING, so a single isolated occurrence does not meet its own falsification criterion. This is the first restart-heavy session since the swap and it is evidence FOR the Nisuta fix, still not enough to close it.

modo: T159: ROOT CAUSE of the whole night's performance collapse -- Xwayland started in SOFTWARE rendering because the render node's uaccess ACL is only granted to the ACTIVE session, and at boot the GNOME session was not the active VT. Same mechanism as T143, and a direct consequence of T156's lost VT
veredicto: THE EVIDENCE, straight from this boot's journal, three consecutive lines at 00:30:54: 'wayland-egl: could not open /dev/dri/renderD128 (Permission denied)' -> 'EGL setup failed, disabling glamor' -> 'Failed to initialize glamor, falling back to sw'. Xwayland (pid 1912) therefore ran the ENTIRE session in software rendering, and an Xwayland instance does not re-initialise glamor later -- the fallback is permanent for its lifetime. Everything that presents through X11 was being composited on the CPU: every Proton title, Quake II RTX in both its RTX and OpenGL modes, everything. THE CAUSAL CHAIN, each link verified rather than assumed: (1) the user is NOT in the `render` group -- `id` listed adm, cdrom, floppy, audio, dip, video, plugdev, users, netdev, systemd-journal and no render; (2) with no group membership, the only access path to /dev/dri/renderD128 is the `uaccess` ACL that systemd-logind grants to the ACTIVE session of seat0; (3) at 00:30:54 the GNOME session was on tty3 while the VISIBLE VT was tty2 -- i.e. GNOME was not the active session, which is exactly the lost-VT condition diagnosed at the very start of this same session in T156; (4) no active session -> no ACL -> permission denied -> glamor off. getfacl confirms the ACL (`user:iam:rw-`) IS present NOW, because pressing Ctrl+Alt+F3 made the session active -- but hours too late for the Xwayland that had already fallen back. THIS IS THE SAME MECHANISM AS T143, which documented logind revoking /dev/hidraw's uaccess ACL the moment the session stops being active. Same ACL, different device node. T143 recorded it as a nuisance that broke a test; here it silently destroyed 3D performance for an entire session without a single error surfacing to the user. IT EXPLAINS EVERY MEASUREMENT OF THE NIGHT, INCLUDING THE ONE THAT DID NOT FIT. All Proton VR titles 13-18 fps; Quake II RTX ~15 fps in RTX mode and 70-90 fps in OpenGL mode where a 3060 Ti should produce thousands; the DXVK submit thread pegged at 85-92% of one core while the GPU sat at 4-45% utilisation and clocks idled -- all of that is the signature of CPU-side compositing, not of a GPU limit. And the anomaly that made no sense under every other hypothesis is explained too: hello_xr ran PERFECTLY at 90 Hz with 3024x3024 per eye, 18 MP/frame, because it reaches the headset through Monado's direct DRM lease and NEVER TOUCHES XWAYLAND. The one path that bypassed Xwayland was the one path that was fast. WHAT THIS RETROACTIVELY CORRECTS, and it matters because the session spent hours on them: the leading hypothesis in T158 -- that the 2026-08-09 kernel 6.12.101 + NVIDIA DKMS rebuild caused the collapse -- is WRONG and is withdrawn. It was built on timeline elimination (that update was the only untested change across the boundary) and the reasoning was sound given what was known, but this evidence is direct, timestamped and mechanistic, and it wins. The planned A/B reboot into the still-installed 6.12.100 is CANCELLED as unnecessary. Also withdrawn as causes, though each was independently worth measuring: display mode, render scale, PowerMizer clocks, background load, Monado's verbose logging, Proton version, xrizer, and any per-title explanation. THE FIX, applied by the user this session: `sudo usermod -aG render iam`. Validated: `getent group render` now reads `render:x:992:iam` and `id iam` lists 992(render). Group membership grants access to the render node REGARDLESS of which VT is active, so the boot ordering stops mattering. Confirmed in the same check that the running session does not yet carry the group -- it takes effect on the next login, which is why a reboot is the confirmation step. NOT YET CONFIRMED WORKING: the reboot and a re-measurement of Quake II RTX (native, no headset needed, and the cheapest instrument available for this) are the acceptance test. THE STANDING LESSON, larger than this bug: on this machine a graphical session that is not the ACTIVE VT loses uaccess ACLs, and the failures that follow are SILENT and non-obvious -- software rendering here, EACCES on hidraw in T143. The boot pipeline deliberately moves the visible VT around (chvt 4 for the picker), so this condition is not exotic on this system, it is designed in. Anything the VR stack needs from a uaccess-controlled device node should be secured by GROUP MEMBERSHIP, not left to depend on which console happens to be in front of the user. Worth auditing the other nodes the stack touches on the same basis. CREDIT WHERE IT BELONGS: this was found only because the user reported that Quake II RTX -- a NATIVE Vulkan application with no Proton, no DXVK and no VR anywhere in it -- was also slow, and that its OpenGL mode was giving 70-90 fps where it should give thousands. Up to that point the entire investigation was scoped to the Proton/VR path and would not have found this. A single measurement from outside the assumed scope collapsed a whole night of hypotheses.

modo: T160: acceptance test for T159's render-group fix -- CONFIRMED, Xwayland on the GPU and Quake II RTX OpenGL from 70-90 fps to the engine's 1000 fps ceiling
veredicto: T159 closed with the fix applied but explicitly NOT confirmed working. This entry closes that. After the reboot, three checks, two negative and one POSITIVE -- the positive one is the point, because absence of an error message is not proof of acceleration. (1) The session now carries the group: `id -nG` lists `render`, which it did not before the reboot (group changes only take effect on a new login). (2) ZERO occurrences of 'could not open /dev/dri/renderD128', 'EGL setup failed' or 'falling back to sw' anywhere in this boot's journal, against three such lines at 00:30:54 in the previous boot. (3) THE POSITIVE CONFIRMATION, which is what actually settles it: an X11 client through Xwayland now reports `OpenGL vendor string: NVIDIA Corporation` and `OpenGL renderer string: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti/PCIe/SSE2`. Under the previous boot's software fallback this would have read llvmpipe. Xwayland is on the GPU. NOTABLE, and it does NOT weaken the fix -- it strengthens the reasoning behind it: this boot happened to come up with the visible VT already on tty3, the same VT as the graphical session, so the uaccess ACL would have been granted anyway. The group membership is what makes that irrelevant rather than lucky. The underlying VT problem from T156 is untouched and still open (the tty4 picker exits status=1 leaving no trace, and nothing returns focus to the graphical session) -- the point of the fix is that it no longer costs 3D performance when it happens. A future boot that lands on the wrong VT is the real proof, and it will arrive on its own. CONFIRMED BY THE END-USER MEASUREMENT, which is what actually closes this: Quake II RTX in OpenGL mode went from 70-90 fps before the fix to 1000 fps after it -- roughly a 12x improvement on the same hardware, same driver, same kernel, with nothing changed but the group membership. The user immediately noted the number looked capped, and he is right, which makes the result STRONGER rather than weaker: id Tech 2 measures frame time in whole milliseconds, so 1 ms is the shortest representable frame and 1000 fps is the engine's own arithmetic ceiling. The measurement is therefore not 'the GPU delivers 1000' but 'the GPU is no longer the limiting factor at all' -- before the fix the limit was the CPU compositing in software at 70-90, after it the limit is the game's inability to count faster. Corroborating instrument reading, unforced: the GPU now sits at pstate P0 (maximum performance) at 1665 MHz and 68 W under load, without PowerMizer being forced this boot, against the P3 it was stuck in during the software-rendering session. The earlier P3 lock now reads as a SYMPTOM of the GPU being starved of real work, not as an independent problem -- which retroactively explains why forcing PowerMizer earlier improved things slightly and then decayed again. System state at the time of writing: monado-service up on `Using builder wmr`, USB 5/5, zero `error -71` / `Cannot enable` in the kernel log for the whole boot. SECOND MEASUREMENT, the RTX path: Quake II RTX in its ray-traced mode went from ~15 fps before the fix to 80 fps after it, a 5.3x improvement. This one is a genuine hardware ceiling rather than an engine one -- sampled over 20 s while the user played, the GPU averaged 100% utilisation, 1896 MHz and 239.2 W against a 240 W limit at 69 C, in pstate P0. There is no headroom left in clocks, power or thermals, so 80 fps is what this 3060 Ti does with real-time path tracing and not a configuration problem. Contrast with the broken state measured hours earlier on the same hardware: 4-45% utilisation, 32-60 W, P3, 210-870 MHz -- the card was very nearly idle while a single CPU thread did its work in software.

modo: T161: LAB MACHINE -- half the Steam library could never reach the runtime (no launch options); fixed, then a full human-verified round of every previously-untested title. Five new working titles, four distinct failure classes named, three xrizer gaps located
veredicto: THE BLOCKER FOUND FIRST, and it invalidated part of the existing record: 23 of the 46 installed titles had NO Steam launch options at all, and one more (NVIDIA VR Funhouse) had them incomplete. Without XR_RUNTIME_JSON + IPC_IGNORE_VERSION + PRESSURE_VESSEL_FILESYSTEMS_RW a title cannot see Monado's socket from inside pressure-vessel and dies with ERROR_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE or a 'VR HMD not found' popup -- which reads exactly like a compatibility verdict and is not one. Found because fpsVR failed that way. All 37 real VR titles now carry the base recipe; the 9 that do not are native/non-VR titles and Steam's own tools. Verified there is no Steam API to set this externally (only steam://launch exists; 'LaunchOptions' appears in steamclient.so as a VDF key, not a command), so editing localconfig.vdf with Steam closed is the only reliable route. ALSO VERIFIED, and worth knowing: `steam -applaunch <id> <args>` does NOT forward extra arguments -- the game's cmdline ends at the .exe. A per-title flag has to go in the launch options as `%command% -flag`. FIVE NEW TITLES CONFIRMED WORKING, every one seen by the user with the headset on, per the project's core rule. Blast the Past: hands in 3DoF and responding, ZERO late frames in 30 s (0.00-0.09%) -- the cleanest result of the night. Emergence: playable with the VR sticks, 0.41% late frames. VersaillesVR: sound, both sticks visible and registering movement, 0.37%. Interkosmos: 3DoF hands, video perfect. Audio Factory: works. Steam 360 Video Player reaches VR with controllers visible but renders black for lack of content -- structurally fine, verification incomplete rather than failed. TWO OBSERVATIONS ON AUDIO FACTORY THAT ARE NOT ITS FAULT and were recorded as such: the user was positioned too high (Monado assumes the floor is a flat 1.6 m below the headset at startup, T146, project-wide) and one controller showed 3DoF only (the paused controller position tracking, docs/03). FOUR DISTINCT FAILURE CLASSES, named because they were previously all lumped together as 'does not work'. (1) NEVER REACHES THE RUNTIME -- the launch-options gap above; fpsVR was the example. (2) OPENS AN XR SESSION AND IMMEDIATELY ABANDONS IT, then runs fine in 2D: Dagon, Back to Dinosaur Island 1 and Amoreon NightClub, all with the identical signature SYNCHRONIZED -> STOPPING -> IDLE -> EXITING inside the same millisecond while the process stays alive. This is NOT a crash and NOT a plumbing failure -- the title talks to OpenVR, gets a session, and drops it. Likely needs a per-title launch flag; testable in one batch next session with `%command% -vr`. (3) CRASHES OUTRIGHT: Back to Dinosaur Island 2, where the user saw CryEngine's 'crash handler not found' followed by 'bug submission failed' -- the reporter failing after the game had already died. (4) BLOCKED BY A NAMED GAP IN OUR OWN STACK, see below. THREE XRIZER GAPS LOCATED, each with file and line, each blocking a specific title. (a) OVERLAYS ARE NOT SUPPORTED AT ALL: fpsVR gets 'Unsupported application type: Overlay' from xrizer::clientcore, so no OpenVR overlay app can work -- not fpsVR, not OVR Toolkit, none. A missing feature, not a misconfiguration. (b) CHAPERONE IS A STUB: Microsoft Maquette's readiness checklist fails on 'controllers on' and 'controllers tracking', and its log shows GetPlayAreaSize and GetPlayAreaRect unimplemented at src/chaperone.rs:65 and :58. The failing checklist reads like a controller-tracking problem and is very likely the room-setup query instead. (c) Maquette also has several right-hand bindings rejected -- /user/hand/right/input/x/click, /y/click, /trigger/value -- because X/Y are LEFT-hand only on the oculus/touch_controller profile (the right hand has A/B). Same class as SUPERHOT's Menu button, already documented. (d) Separately, Monado has NO FOV-crop option at all: all 240 of its DEBUG_GET_ONCE options were checked and only the two uniform scalers exist, so SteamVR's tangent-multiplier style peripheral crop has no equivalent. The FOV is assembled at wmr_hmd.c:2114 -- a clear place for a patch, and strictly better than lowering global render scale because it removes cost from where the lenses barely show anything. THE OVRPLUGIN STUB, written and working this session (tools/ovrplugin-stub/). InCell VR and InMind VR are NATIVE Linux Unity builds -- not Proton, so none of the launch-options reasoning applied to them, and an earlier claim in this session that all three 'unrelated failures' shared the launch-options cause was WRONG for these two and is corrected here. Their real cause: both call Oculus's OVRPlugin before anything else (OVRSwitcher.GetVRActiveDevice / OVRManager.Update), and libOVRPlugin.so has never existed on Linux -- Oculus abandoned the platform in 2015. Mono throws DllNotFoundException and the process aborts in under a second. That abort is what CLAUDE.md recorded as 'an unrelated Mono crash': a symptom, not a cause. The user's note that both titles ran on a DK2 made a genuine performance failure implausible and pointed the search the right way. FIX: a 78-symbol stub .so that answers 'no HMD, not initialised' to everything, generated from the symbol list extracted from the games' own Assembly-CSharp.dll rather than guessed. It must go in <Game>_Data/Plugins/x86_64/ -- Unity's native-plugin directory -- NOT in Mono/x86_64/, which is only the fallback path the log advertises; installing it there did nothing. RESULT, and it worked exactly as designed: the stub's own trace shows ovrp_GetString and ovrp_GetStatus being called, and the stack then continues through OVRSwitcher into SteamVR.CreateInstance -> OpenVR.Init -> OpenVRInterop.InitInternal. The Oculus block is gone and the title now dies inside VR_InitInternal -- which is precisely the failure CLAUDE.md attributed to InCell in the first place. So that verdict was right about WHERE and wrong about the path: nobody could have reached it, because an earlier blocker stopped the game a full stage sooner. Next suspect for the remaining crash: the game bundles its own libopenvr_api.so from the OpenVR 1.0.x era in Plugins/x86_64/, and an ABI mismatch between that and xrizer would explain a crash this early -- xrizer never even opens its log. Not investigated. WARM-UP CONFIRMED AS A GENERAL RULE, on three independent titles now, not one: Aircar 3.44% -> 0.13%, Emergence 2.56% -> 0.41%, and VersaillesVR from a user-reported 2 fps to perfect -- in every case with the render scale and everything else unchanged, purely DXVK finishing its shader compilation. The first minute of a Proton title measures warm-up, not steady state. This is now written into scripts/frame-pacing.sh so the next person does not draw the conclusion this session nearly drew. PERCEPTION SCALE, calibrated against the only instrument that counts. The user's own reports line up with the measurements: 0.13% imperceptible ('casi perfecto'), 2.56% noticeable but playable ('se nota que un poquito apenas se pierde, pero bien igual'), 3.44% noticeable and mildly nauseating. The script's 1% threshold is therefore reasonable, and that number comes from this user's direct perception on this hardware, not from an industry rule. ONE AGENT FAILURE WORTH RECORDING: the user had explicitly asked that pacing be measured on every title. The tool was built and then not run for the first three titles of the round until he asked again. Measuring is not optional instrumentation here -- it is the deliverable he asked for.

modo: T162: LAB MACHINE -- 6DoF SLAM root-caused and fixed, then taken into a real game. The runaway was a starved visual front-end; the jitter is rotational and comes from Basalt, not from the output stage. Five patches, two measured dead ends, one self-inflicted design cost
driver: monado lab-90hz-0017 (0001-0015+0018, then +0019/0020/0021 written this session), basalt df6e970 +0001, jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof
veredicto: SIX-DOF NOW WORKS AND WAS USER-VERIFIED WITH THE HEADSET ON ('parece estar todo bien, firme siguiendome'), after a full session of measurement. THE CHAIN, each link measured rather than argued. (1) THE SESSION OPENED ON A DIFFERENT FAILURE: the unattended boot reached the picker and hung at 'subiendo monado'. panel.py activate worked and connector 137 (DP-2, non-desktop=1, 384-byte EDID, 4320x2160@90) came up in the kernel, but mutter offered ZERO connectors for lease for 15s and all 3 monado attempts failed; by then the panel had gone back to sleep, because jack-in-wayland.sh activates the panel ONCE outside its retry loop (line ~82), so retries 2 and 3 were doomed. Relaunching by hand with GNOME in the foreground on tty3 worked first try. Prime suspect is the picker's chvt 4 making the GNOME session inactive so logind revokes mutter's DRM master -- same mechanism class as T143/T159 -- but it is NOT confirmed: chvt needs a password from the agent's shell, so the decisive A/B was never run. Do not record it as cause. (2) THE 6DOF RUNAWAY REPRODUCED HERE, so it is not specific to the everyday system (T147): motionless headset, RUNAWAY at 25cm in 2.66s, 1963.7 m at 79.5s, exponent t^3.8. AND A CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: T060/T061's 'SLAM works well here' (2026-08-07) measured ONLY rotation jitter -- pose-measure.py did not exist until T147 -- so position was very likely running away then too and nobody looked. In a 360 photo viewer the sphere is at infinity, so a position leaving for kilometres is invisible. Treat this as never-worked, not a regression. (3) TWO HYPOTHESES KILLED BY MEASUREMENT, both mine. 'It is the 4-camera config': with WMR_MAX_SLAM_CAMS=2 it still ran away (12165 m). 'It degenerates only at rest, for lack of parallax': worn and moving it ran away from the first second (2.5 m at 5s, 1839 m at 70s). Motion did cut det(Q1Jl)==0 spam 10x (119/s static vs 11/s moving) but changed nothing about the divergence, so the degeneracy was a symptom. (4) THE INSTRUMENT THAT CRACKED IT. Two pieces of SLAM telemetry existed but were reachable only through the debug GUI. Exported as env knobs (patch 0019): EUROC_RECORD=1/EUROC_RECORD_PATH, and SLAM_FEATURES_ENABLE=1 which makes t_slam write features.csv. THAT was the measurement: Basalt was holding a mean of 0.0-0.9 landmarks per camera. A healthy VIO holds 50-150. Everything else was fine and verified: per-camera ROI images visually perfect in the GUI (screenshotted directly with `import -window`, no need for the user to describe them), camera timing 30.04 Hz with dt stdev 0.2 ms and zero gaps over 385 s, raw IMU |accel| = 9.8118 +/- 0.0124 m/s^2 with gyro noise 0.001 rad/s, calibration delivered with no parse warnings. Also ruled out by reading code, each one checked not assumed: stride handling (Basalt does cv::Mat{h,w,type,data,stride}), the wmr/rt8 distortion struct layouts (identical in the first 8 fields, the memcpy does not scramble them), intrinsics denormalisation (fx = 0.4232*640 = 270.9), and rpmax semantics (evaluated in NORMALISED coordinates, so 2.79 is permissive -- an early guess that it was a 3-pixel clip was wrong). (5) A DEAD END WORTH RECORDING: SLAM_UI=1 is a silent no-op on this Basalt. The `cmake --preset library` build (T060) has no Pangolin -- `nm -D libbasalt.so | grep -c pangolin` = 0, no window ever appears. And monocular is impossible: 'Basalt doesn't support running with 1 cameras', hard assert. The EuRoC known-good control was never run either: robotics.ethz.ch is down (curl rc=28, connect timeout), no mirror found. (6) THE FIX. SLAM_CONFIG was all-or-nothing -- passing a file makes Monado stop sending the driver calibration -- so tuning one pipeline parameter meant hand-writing the whole G2 calibration in Basalt's format first. Two small patches remove that: monado 0020 (SLAM_CONFIG_PIPELINE_ONLY=1) and basalt 0001 (--cam-calib no longer required). With sweeping unlocked the answer came in three runs: Basalt's DEFAULT DETECTION SETTINGS ARE TOO SPARSE FOR THE G2's FISHEYE CAMERAS. Note data/default_config.json and data/euroc/euroc_config.json are byte-for-byte identical, so the defaults ARE the EuRoC settings, tuned for 752x480 pinhole at 20 Hz, not 640x480 fisheye at 30 Hz. With grid_size 30 / num_points_cell 3 / min_threshold 3 the static drift went from thousands of metres to 0.72 m at 60 s, reproduced twice (0.08 m @10s, 0.39 @30s, 0.72 @60s). It is a THRESHOLD, not one wrong knob: measured at 60 s, only-num_points_cell 4613 m, only-min_threshold 1791 m, only-grid_size 865 m -- no single one of the three is enough. Worn and walking, the real condition: features went to a mean of 20.4/21.0 per camera (max 261/285), det(Q1Jl) to 0.12/s from 119/s, and the distance to origin RETURNED (0.99 m at 180-200 s, 0.51 m at 200-220 s). A runaway never comes back; that is tracking. Wired into scripts/jack-in-wayland.sh as the default for 6dof via scripts/basalt-g2-config.json (SLAM_G2_CONFIG=0 for an A/B). (7) A SEPARATE CRASH BUG, FOUND AND FIXED (patch 0021). t_slam detected camera frames whose timestamp was not greater than the last, warned, AND PUSHED THEM ANYWAY. Basalt aborts on those (sqrt_keypoint_vio.cpp:311, 'frame timestamps not monotonically increasing?!') and it killed monado-service THREE times this session with three unrelated triggers: disk I/O from the EuRoC recorder, CPU from denser detection, and a CamerasDmaReset/DMA CMT ERR burst from the headset itself. Now the whole bundle is dropped (all cameras in a bundle must share a timestamp, so dropping only cam0 trades one assert for another). MEASURED AFTER THE FIX, and this is the interesting part: the guard fires ~195 times per session, 157 of them dropping a single bundle, max 5, with backwards jumps of 10-106 ms. The G2's camera clock hiccups constantly and every one of those out-of-order frames used to reach the tracker. (8) ALSO FIXED IN BASALT (patch 0001, second half): monado_out_state_queue.set_capacity(32) only ran when a unified config file was given. pop_state() implements push-newest-drop-oldest as `while (!try_push(x)) pop(_)`, which is a no-op on an unbounded queue, so the caller-driven path -- the one Monado uses by default -- let that queue grow without bound instead of dropping stale states. STILL OPEN: 0.72 m of static drift in 60 s is ordinary VIO drift, not zero; pushing detection harder (grid 20, 4 pts/cell) made the process crash before the frame-drop guard existed and has not been retried since; the boot-time lease failure in (1) has no confirmed cause and nothing returns the VT to the graphical session when the picker dies (still open from T156). ||| AFTERNOON, IN-GAME (Aircar 1073390, user wearing the headset throughout). USER-VERIFIED WORKING but not comfortable: 'funciona, bastante jittering', spawned 0.5-2 m outside the cockpit, and after ~3 minutes 'se salto para cualquier lado afuera'. Measured behind that report: the pose held 0.8 m for 600 s and then jumped to 2211 m in one step and FROZE -- identical to the centimetre for the next 90 s. That is not a runaway, that is the tracker losing it and not coming back, with the wearer stranded 2.5 km away and no recovery short of killing the service. PATCH 0023 ADDS A DIVERGENCE AUTO-RESET for exactly that: implied speed between consecutive poses over 10 m/s (a head peaks at 2-3 m/s) calls tracker_reset. Verified by forcing it -- threshold lowered until it fired 22 times in a row, service alive and re-localising each time -- which is also how two real bugs in it surfaced: dt needs a 5 ms floor (two of the first three real resets fired on dt=0.000 s, where 5 mm reads as 21 m/s) and SLAM_AUTO_RESET_MAX_SPEED goes through DEBUG_GET_ONCE_NUM_OPTION which parses INTEGERS ONLY, so 0.05 silently becomes 0 and everything 'diverges'. In the real session it worked: 9 resets, position back to 0.19-0.26 m after peaking at 45 m. KNOWN COST, SELF-INFLICTED, NOT FIXED: a reset re-anchors the tracker at the origin and the application is never told, so the world anchor moves to wherever the wearer was standing -- in-game that reads as being teleported. The user's 'estoy lejos de la nave' happened with the tracker reporting a healthy 0.19 m. It trades a permanent freeze for repeated teleports; the real fix is to carry the reset offset through to the output pose. THE JITTER IS ROTATIONAL, AND I SPENT AN HOUR MEASURING THE WRONG AXIS. Position steps looked bad (p99 152 mm, max 582 mm) so the first two attempts went at the output stage: the one euro filter (SLAM_FILTER knob, patch 0023) and then SLAM_PREDICTION_TYPE=2 (gyro-only) on the theory that linear dead reckoning over a gappy IMU stream was the source. User verdict on the first: 'el jittering no cambio casi, la posicion mas bien'. On the second: 'igual mucho jitter'. Measuring ROTATION between consecutive poses settled it instantly -- raw Basalt p50 0.0396 deg, p90 2.78, p99 12.03, max 32.35 (that is 970 deg/s, impossible for a head), against p99 1.13 / max 5.54 after the filter. So the one euro filter, which I had nearly written off as useless, is doing the single biggest thing in the output path -- for rotation -- and the jitter itself is Basalt's, upstream of everything I was tuning. It is now the default for 6dof in jack-in-wayland.sh. DENSER DETECTION RETRIED, now that patch 0021 stops the crash it used to cause: detect_plus (grid 20, 4 pts/cell, thr 3) survives, features went from a mean of 1.0-2.6 to 46.2 on cam0 (peak 524), static drift to 0.012 m at 60 s and rotation at rest to p99 0.89 deg. User in-game: 'cambio el comportamiento, es mas suave el jitter o menos frecuente'. BUT IT FEEDS BACK: 24150 IMU samples dropped against ~6000 with the lighter config, because the extra CPU perturbs sample arrival, which moves the clock fit, which is what produces the drops and feeds the divergences. CPU <-> clock <-> tracking is one loop and past this point every lever pushes the problem around it. NOT MEASURED, STATED AS NOT MEASURED: the user reports pronounced left/CCW roll drift (docs/23 already records this for Aircar on long SLAM sessions). The attempt to quantify it hit gimbal lock -- the Euler decomposition gave a constant pitch of -88 deg, meaning the axis convention assumed was wrong, and near +-90 deg roll and yaw trade off and the numbers are meaningless. Measuring roll drift while the wearer moves is confounded anyway. It needs the headset static on a flat surface for 2-3 minutes with the gravity direction tracked. No number is claimed. RECOMMENDED CONFIG AT SESSION END, wired as the default: basalt-g2-config.json (grid 30) + SLAM_FILTER=one_euro + SLAM_AUTO_RESET. detect_plus is better on every static metric but drops 4x the IMU samples in a real game.

modo: T163: LAB MACHINE -- 6DoF CONTROLLER tracking (constellation) works for the first time in this project, user-verified. Three real bugs found and fixed after that; the remaining error is characterised as pose ambiguity and the obvious next fix is measured and rejected with a number
driver: monado lab-full 2a6e64d6e (= g2-constellation-x11kde 7cb73701b + 90Hz + 0019-0023 cherry-picked, then patches 0024-0027 written this session), jack-in-wayland.sh 1 ctrl
veredicto: USER-VERIFIED WITH THE HEADSET ON, twice, per the project's core rule: first 'confirmado que los dos funcionan, veo que los ejes no parecen correctos, pero se van desplazando en los 3 ejes', then after the axis fix 'los ejes parecen estar bien, si hago un movimiento de 3-6cm, todo bien'. This is the FIRST time 6DoF controller position has ever reached an application in this project. ||| THE STARTING POINT WAS NOT A BUG, IT WAS A MISSING BINARY. The lab's built branch (lab-90hz-0017) does not contain the constellation fusion at all -- wmr_controller_base.c has no constellation code on it; that lives only on g2-constellation-x11kde. No amount of testing on the built binary could ever have shown controller position. Fixed by branching lab-full from the constellation branch and cherry-picking the six head/SLAM commits (90 Hz + 0019-0023) onto it; all six applied clean. Note the direction: constellation as the base, SLAM on top -- the reverse (the tracked 0001-0023 series as base) is the one that does not apply, per T157. ||| BUG 1 (patch 0024), found by reading rather than by symptom: WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS is declared TWICE with DIFFERENT defaults -- true in wmr_hmd.c, false in wmr_camera.c. Left unset, the HMD creates a constellation tracker while the camera path never assigns the controller exposure slots that feed it. That is a starved tracker, not a disabled one, and it presents exactly as 'constellation does not work'. ||| FIRST MEASUREMENT, AND A TRAP AVOIDED: 125 log lines all reading pos=(0.046, 0.022, -0.014) with matched_blobs=6 constant looked like a degenerate solver stuck on one value. It was not. Asking the user to move the controllers showed TWO separate sample streams with independent counters: one was a controller sitting still (constant position = correct), and the other had produced ZERO samples until picked up, its counter starting from 15. The 'frozen' reading was one controller reporting, not two controllers at the same point. ||| BUG 2 (patch 0025) -- THE WRONG AXES, root-caused in the tracker's own source. The camera mosaic was created without a tracking_origin, so CameraMosaic::getTrackingOriginPose (t_constellation_tracker.cpp:791) fell through to XRT_POSE_IDENTITY: the tracker assumed the headset never moves and never turns, and placed its cameras in a frame bolted to the IMU's initial orientation. The header documents that field as existing precisely for cameras mounted on a headset. Wiring the HMD's own pose in fixed the axes -- user-verified. Detail that mattered: the tracker discards the observation unless the origin reports BOTH position and orientation valid, and a 3dof head has no valid position, so a naive source would have broken what already worked; (0,0,0) is the honest answer there because in 3dof the headset IS the fixed origin. Orientation is deliberately not forced. ||| BUG 3 (patch 0026), UPSTREAM, NOT OURS. Both callers of Camera::pushPose gate on POSE_MATCH_GOOD, but that is the score BEFORE the RANSAC-PnP refinement inside pushPose; the refined score is recomputed right after and was only ever used to fill in the sample metrics. Poses the tracker's own criterion had just rejected were published anyway, including matched_blob_count == 0 -- a pose supported by no observation at all, 3 of 876 samples, one of them a 1.43 m jump. Only the publication is suppressed; found_pose, marked blobs and the rest of the per-frame bookkeeping are untouched, so the tracker's search is unchanged. ||| BUG 4 (patch 0027): the driver invented its own output scheme -- last stored sample if under 200 ms old, else a fixed placeholder pose -- where both reference drivers (rift, pssense) push into an m_relation_history and read it back interpolated at the requested timestamp. It also left t_constellation_tracker_device_params.tracking_source NULL; that field is the tracker's PRIOR, what it uses to throw out pose hypotheses before committing. Both now go through one m_relation_history. Before wiring it, the clock-domain worry written into the code (samples once seen SECONDS ahead of at_timestamp_ns) was re-measured on this build and is gone: the delta is a steady 30-37 ms, i.e. the ordinary age of the last 30 Hz camera frame. Patch 0016's clock alignment had already fixed it. That measurement needed its own fix first -- the diagnostic log gated on sample_count % 30, so it was silent exactly when samples stopped arriving. ||| THE NUMBERS, all from a controller lying MOTIONLESS on a desk, so every step is error by definition. Step between consecutive samples, controller A / controller B: baseline p99 0.435 / 0.413 m, max 1.607 / 0.937 m. After 0026: p99 0.435 / 0.413 unchanged but max 0.560 / 0.432, and matched_blobs=0 samples to zero. After 0027: p99 0.194 / 0.007 m, max 0.202 / 0.007 m. Controller B is essentially solved -- 7 mm. Poses rejected by the tracker's own quality check fell 271 -> 27 in a comparable window, which is the prior doing its job: helping it find the right pose instead of discarding the wrong one afterwards. ||| WHAT IS STILL OPEN, CHARACTERISED RATHER THAN GUESSED. Controller A keeps a BISTABLE flip: clustering its positions gives two groups 0.189 m apart, both with ~8 matched blobs and ~8-9 visible LEDs, i.e. both are good fits. That is pose ambiguity, and no threshold on the tracker's quality metrics can separate them -- several of the bad solves have a LOWER reprojection error than the good ones (0.06 px at 45 cm away), because with few visible LEDs a wrong pose can fit a handful of blobs almost perfectly. Only outside information breaks it. The obvious candidate is the controller's own IMU orientation, and IT WAS MEASURED BEFORE BEING WIRED, which is why it was not wired: the angle between the constellation solve's orientation and the IMU fusion's is 138-178 deg, and the GRAVITY DIRECTION ALONE disagrees by 104-161 deg -- bimodally, matching the two clusters. If this were only the fusion's arbitrary yaw the gravity axis would agree. It does not, so the LED model frame and the IMU frame are genuinely different frames (the LED model is in the controller's calibration frame; the IMU has its own pose inside that model). An IMU-backed prior needs that fixed transform derived from the factory calibration first. NOT a drop-in, and feeding it in blind would reject the true pose. ||| ALSO CONFIRMED IN PASSING: the T051 controller startup race can lose BOTH controllers, not just the right one. Two consecutive starts came up left: <none> / right: <none> with b_system_devices_static_finalize at log line 121 and the two controller configs only finishing at lines 470 and 643, preceded by 'Controller fw read timed out after 261 ms'. Waking both controllers with a button press before starting the service fixed it and gave zero fw timeouts on every start afterwards. The user's own read (that they were out of the cameras' view) explains missing constellation samples but cannot explain the role list -- that path is the HID/BT tunnel, not vision. ||| TOOLING: jack-in-wayland.sh gains a third tracking mode, 'ctrl' -- head 3dof but cameras ON and constellation enabled -- so controller position can be measured without Basalt's CPU load in the way, which matters because T162 established that CPU load perturbs IMU sample arrival and moves the clock fit that constellation samples are stamped against. It always passes WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS explicitly, never relying on the default, because of bug 1. ||| AIRCAR, LATER THE SAME SESSION (6dof head + constellation controllers together, the real target config). IT EXPOSED A BUG IN PATCH 0025 THAT COST THE WHOLE FIRST ATTEMPT, and the chain is worth keeping because two of my own diagnoses along the way were wrong. Both controllers came back (nan, nan, nan) indefinitely. FIRST WRONG READ: I said the SLAM head pose was NaN and that an auto-reset had fired -- both from sloppy greps, 'nan' was matching 'maintenance' in the Vulkan extension list and the 'auto-reset' hit was the startup line saying the feature is enabled. The head pose was healthy in the CSV. SECOND WRONG READ: with the head pose confirmed NaN at the constellation boundary (logged with values: pos=(-nan, nan, -nan), quat all NaN, flags=0x33, xret=0 -- i.e. Monado reporting NaN while claiming POSITION_VALID and SUCCESS), I diagnosed a thread race, because patch 0025 added a second thread calling wmr_hmd_get_tracked_pose and the one euro filter is stateful. Added a mutex. IT DID NOT FIX IT, and that is the useful part: the problem is the ORDERING, not the race. The compositor asks about a PREDICTED DISPLAY TIME (future, advancing); the constellation tracker asks at CAMERA FRAME timestamps (past). m_filter_one_euro.c:243 divides by dt = when_ns - its own last timestamp with no guard, and that timestamp is unsigned, so interleaving the two makes dt go negative and the NaN is STORED IN THE FILTER for good. Confirmed by the cleanest possible A/B: SLAM_FILTER=none was completely clean in the identical configuration, SLAM_FILTER=one_euro was not. ||| THEN THE FIX ITSELF REGRESSED SOMETHING, and only instrumentation caught it. A plain 'must be newer than the last one' latch is poisoned permanently by ONE bad timestamp: a caller passed when_ns = 5216735132270448003 (~165 years, against normal values around 7e12) exactly once, and from then on every pose was 'in the past' and skipped -- applied 16 against skipped 7984. The one euro filter had switched itself OFF for the whole session with nothing in the log saying so, and the user felt it directly ('hay jittering todavia') at a point where T162's numbers say it should not have been there. Now bounded against os_monotonic_get_ns(), which no single value can move, and near-simultaneous repeat queries (measured: pairs 17-19 us apart, the second always slightly earlier -- these predate today's work) are answered with the last FILTERED pose rather than the raw one, so two views of one frame cannot disagree by the full jitter amplitude. After: applied 30000, skipped 27160 of which 9512 answered from the last filtered pose, 329 implausible. A standing count now lives in the log precisely because this failed silently once. ||| PROCESS FAILURE, MINE, WORTH NOT REPEATING: I restarted monado-service repeatedly while the user had Aircar open, without telling them. That is what produced the two 'LowLevelFatalError: GameThread timed out waiting for RenderThread after 120.00 secs' and at least the later xrizer panics -- compositor.rs:1162 is .expect("Failed to acquire swapchain image"), which is what a client gets when the runtime goes away underneath it. Steam's own log settles it: the game's processes were added at 21:00:59 and only removed at 21:21:21, i.e. the hung instance survived the entire window in which I was cycling the service. I also initially offered 'the NaN caused the panic' as though it were established when it was a hypothesis. ||| FINAL IN-GAME RESULT, USER-VERIFIED: 'me parece que mejoro. Durante el intro, muy poco movimiento. Luego dentro del juego al menos por lo general estoy dentro de la nave', and 'sin errores' -- no xrizer panic once the NaN was gone and I stopped restarting the service, which answers whether that panic was an independent bug: it was not. Measured alongside: ZERO divergence auto-resets (grep for the exact string the code emits, 'Tracker diverged'), against NINE in T162's Aircar session, each of which re-anchors the world and is what produced 'estoy lejos de la nave'. STATED PLAINLY: the zero-resets result is NOT attributable to today's patches -- the divergence path was not touched, and this may be session variance. The jitter improvement IS attributable, because there is a measured before and after on the filter being applied at all. ||| WHAT AIRCAR CANNOT TELL US, from the user: this title does not render the controllers, so none of today's controller work is visible in it. Validating 6DoF controllers needs a title where the hands are drawn -- VRSailing or SUPERHOT VR from docs/23.

modo: T164: LAB MACHINE -- 6DoF controllers taken into four real titles, and the orientation drift this project blamed on SLAM for weeks turns out to be a gyro-bias estimator that nothing ever calls. Also: the 6dof performance cost measured and attributed, and three tools written after getting process state wrong three times
driver: monado lab-full cfa90eb84 (0024-0031), basalt df6e970+0001, hello_xr with a pointing-direction readout, jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof with SLAM_THREADS=2
veredicto: THE HEADLINE: THE ORIENTATION DRIFT IS NOT A SLAM PROBLEM AND NEVER WAS. m_imu_3dof has carried a gyro-bias estimator all along; gyro_biasing() returns immediately unless gyro_bias.manually_fire is set, and the ONLY thing that sets it is a checkbox in the debug GUI, which no real session ever opens. So the residual bias is integrated forever. MEASURED with both controllers lying untouched on a desk, two independent windows agreeing within 1%: LEFT 72 deg/min (93% of steps monotonic), RIGHT 20 deg/min (63%). Repeated with the controllers in a completely different resting orientation: 71.7 and 20.0 deg/min -- ORIENTATION-INDEPENDENT, which rules out accelerometer misalignment and scale error and leaves plain gyro bias. Gravity correction cannot help: the accelerometer fixes vertical so pitch and roll are pulled back, but YAW has no absolute reference and runs unbounded -- exactly the axis the user kept reporting. This single cause covers everything previously logged as separate: the left controller 'pointing at me', the constant leftward yaw, the roll drift in 3dof, AND the fact that it reproduces with Basalt not running at all. docs/23 and T162 both attributed it to long 6DoF sessions; that attribution was WRONG. ||| THE FIX AND ITS HONEST LIMIT (patch 0031). M_IMU_3DOF_USE_GYRO_BIAS_AUTO fires the existing estimator after a continuous second of stillness (raw gyro < 0.10 rad/s, |accel| within 0.5 of gravity), re-estimating every 2 s. Confirmed firing -- 39 times in 25 s across three devices -- and the biases it measures (34.5, 63.9, 47.9 deg/min) are the same magnitude as the drift observed, which corroborates the diagnosis independently of whether the fix works. RESULT, measured frame-independently as the angle BETWEEN the two controllers (no rotation of the reference frame can affect it): 18.8 -> 8.9 deg/min, a 53% reduction. NOT a cure, and the reason is in the estimator's own log: successive estimates of the same motionless device vary almost twofold, because it averages 300 ms and then REPLACES the bias wholesale. Smoothing instead of replacing is the next step. ||| A MEASUREMENT TRAP WORTH KEEPING: the first 'after' measurement looked like a failure (63 and 98 deg/min) until the trajectories showed both controllers rising TOGETHER -- that is the reference frame rotating, not the controllers drifting, because in 6dof the SLAM head pose moves and carries both. Absolute per-controller angles are confounded by it; the inter-controller angle is not. That is what made the result readable. ||| CONTROLLER PATH, FOUR BUGS (patch 0030), each found from a user report and closed with a number. (1) HANDS AT FLOOR LEVEL: the controllers adopted the constellation tracker's own tracking origin, initial_offset = XRT_POSE_IDENTITY, where u_builder_setup_tracking_origins gives NONE-type origins y = 1.3 m; the head-to-controller offset read a clean -1.59 m. Adopting that origin was correct while the mosaic had no origin of its own -- once patch 0025 gave it the headset's pose, the solve already lands in the head's frame and a second origin just misplaces it. USER-VERIFIED after the fix: 'estan acordes a la altura real'. (2) HANDS FLYING AWAY: a sample at (-3432890, -7235085, -15194503) metres with 7 matched blobs -- finite, so the NaN guard never saw it, and it would have entered the relation history and hence the tracker's own prior. Range check added; NOTE it compares against the ORIGIN when a controller is an arm's length from the HEAD, which can itself be metres away, so the threshold is loose and head-relative is the right check. (3) POSITION NEVER REACHING THE APPLICATION: 128 placeholder against 1 tracked while the tracker solved happily at 6-10 matched blobs -- the 200 ms freshness gate was shorter than the ~250 ms real per-controller sample interval. Now WMR_CONSTELLATION_MAX_AGE_MS, default 500. The user's description was diagnostic on its own: hands anchored as if 3DoF, and when they jump they jump to the NEW position, not the initial one. THE REAL FIX IS SAMPLE RATE: 4/s per controller against 30 Hz cameras. (4) P_imu_me, the IMU-to-device rotation, is computed by the controllers and used only by the HMD. Measured from this headset's own calibration: left axis (-0.449, +0.778, -0.440) angle 105.3 deg, right (-0.449, -0.782, +0.432) angle 105.5 -- same angle, mirrored axes, the signature of two physically mirrored devices. Applied now, behind WMR_CONTROLLER_IMU_TO_DEVICE. STATED PLAINLY: this did NOT fix the 'left points at me' symptom it was written for -- that was the gyro drift. It is a real gap, just not that one. ||| TITLES, ALL USER-VERIFIED WITH THE HEADSET ON. Interkosmos: first validation in a title that DRAWS the controllers -- 'tecnicamente funciona'. Aircar: 'por lo general estoy dentro de la nave', zero divergence auto-resets against nine in T162 (NOT claimed as caused by these patches -- the divergence path was untouched). Blast the Past: exposed bug (3). SafeZoneVR: opened a session and abandoned it, twice. Blade Runner 9732: docs/23 said no copy existed -- there is one at ~/vr/nonsteam/BR9732. It runs in 2D and never enters VR, traced to libxrizer.so never being dlopened (checked in /proc/<pid>/maps) while the game's own openvr_api.dll and Proton's vrclient_x64.so both load: the launch METHOD, not the title. Needs a non-Steam Steam shortcut. AND: SteamVR (250820) and Windows Mixed Reality for SteamVR (719950) are installed but are NOT games -- the first is the runtime this project replaces, the second is Microsoft's Windows-only driver plugin for it. Recorded in docs/23 so the question has an answer. ||| PERFORMANCE, MEASURED AND ATTRIBUTED. The user reported 50-70 fps in 6dof against 80-90 in 3dof. It is the SLAM's CPU cost, not the controller work: Basalt pins one whole core at 99.4% of six physical while the machine sits at 26% overall, and the GPU is only at 62-64% (198 W of 250) -- so lowering render scale would not help. Two obvious answers were WRONG and both were measured before being believed: constellation tracking is not the cost (with it off, the same config gave 3.44% and 7.22% late frames in back-to-back windows -- the run-to-run variance is wider than the effect), and MORE Basalt threads make pacing worse. THE THREAD COUNT NEEDED BOTH SIDES MEASURED, and the first pass got it wrong by looking at only one: threads cost frame pacing and BUY tracking. 1 thread: 9.8 Hz pose rate, rotation p99 11.4-23.6 deg, max 159.8 deg, 3.7% late. 2: 13.8 Hz, p99 7.52, max 30.0, 8.2% late. 3: 19.9 Hz, p99 7.18, max 25.1, 10.8-11.6% late. A 159.8-degree step between consecutive poses is not a head movement, it is the tracker losing it. The user pushed back on the premature revert to 1 ('venia andando bien... con multihilo') and the pose CSVs, which were on disk the whole time, showed they were right. 2 is now the default; user verdict 'mejoro MUCHO'. Also measured and surprising: num-threads does NOT cap Basalt's total threads -- at both 2 and 3 there are four monado threads at 94-99%; only at 1 is there a single saturated one. ||| WHAT THE PERFORMANCE WORK RULED OUT: deprioritising Basalt's threads to nice 19 changed nothing (9.33% and 12.41% against 8.22%), so the game is not losing frames to CPU starvation; and WMR: USB-HMD and VBlank Events already run SCHED_FIFO 99 while everything else, compositor included, is SCHED_OTHER 0. With GPU and CPU both having headroom, the remaining hypothesis is the compositor BLOCKING on the SLAM pose query. Not measured. ||| EYE HEIGHT / FLOOR. Monado never measures the floor: b_space_overseer_legacy_setup places STAGE a hardcoded 1.6 m below LOCAL (target_builder_helpers.c), so every session assumes the wearer's eyes are exactly there -- seated, that is out by around half a metre. XRT_TRACKING_ORIGIN_OFFSET_Y already exists and u_builder_helpers.c applies it to every origin regardless of type, so offset = eye_height - 1.6 fixes it with no code. Wired into jack-in-wayland.sh via a profile file so the unattended boot never has to ask. The user's design critique is recorded and correct: standing/seated are two presets and someone playing almost lying down on a bean bag is neither, and nobody knows their eye height in that posture -- so MEASURING it (a controller placed on the floor, now possible for the first time) is the real answer, not a typed number. Blocked on controller position being trustworthy: the bistable 0.189 m flip from T163 would poison a single sample. ||| TOOLING, ALL OF IT WRITTEN AFTER GETTING SOMETHING WRONG. scripts/vr-state.sh: an authoritative 'what is running' snapshot, written after misreading process state twice and then FIXED TWICE MORE because its first two implementations fell into the very trap they existed to remove -- matching `ps -eo args` finds the caller's own shell, since the shell's command line contains the strings being searched for. Three shells died to exit 144 in one session.
