It now matches on comm, and the args-based fallback was deleted outright rather than repaired: the authoritative signal is the OpenXR client count from the runtime's own log. scripts/machine-specs.sh: hardware profile, so tuning derives from the machine instead of being hardcoded to this one -- prompted by the user pointing out that num-threads=1 on a 6-core box is an unexamined assumption on an 8-thread one. scripts/vr-power-setup.sh: report/apply/restore full-performance settings; applied live (CPU governor and EPP powersave -> performance, PCIe ASPM -> performance, GPU 240 -> 250 W) and NOT yet measured against a baseline. scripts/controller-watch.sh plus a hello_xr change: a flat-monitor readout of which way each controller points, which is what made the frame-independent drift measurement possible. ||| PROCESS, MINE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT COST THE USER TWO CRASHES: restarting monado-service under a live title kills it (Unreal: 'GameThread timed out waiting for RenderThread after 120.00 secs'; xrizer panics at compositor.rs:1162, which is .expect("Failed to acquire swapchain image") -- what a client gets when the runtime goes away). Steam's own log settled it: the game's processes were added at 21:00:59 and removed only at 21:21:21, so the hung instance survived the whole window in which the service was being cycled. The user's rule from this: the agent opens and closes the titles, so process state stays tracked. Also learned: after closing a title Steam may be waiting on a confirmation dialog, and further applaunch calls silently do nothing until it is answered.

modo: T165: LAB MACHINE -- the resting-controller orientation drift closed for real: it was the firmware zeroing the IMU fields ~30 s after rest while our calibration pipeline manufactured a fake constant rotation out of the zeros. Found only after building a fixed measurement protocol, two failed fixes, and a controlled wake experiment with the user
driver: monado lab-full 2286029f8 (0024-0035), jack-in-wayland.sh 1 3dof, scripts/drift-measure.py
veredicto: THE RESULT FIRST: a resting controller now measures +0.00 deg/min, residual RMS 0.00 deg, on the fixed protocol (settle 60 s, capture 120 s, least-squares slope over ~120 samples) -- against 31-72 deg/min across every earlier measurement. Verified per-link in the same log before the final number: 12 bias estimates per controller during the awake window, then 'idle (zeroed) IMU packet -- fusion paused' from each, then frozen output. ||| THE MECHANISM, WHICH NONE OF THE NIGHT'S HYPOTHESES HAD RIGHT: ~30 s after a G2 controller stops moving, its firmware KEEPS the 44-byte packet stream alive -- buttons, battery, timestamps all valid, zero parse errors -- but ZEROES the six raw IMU count fields. wmr_controller_hp.c's calibration then fabricates data from nothing: 0 * mix_matrix + bias_offsets = the device's factory bias vector, a small CONSTANT. Fingerprint that settled it, sitting in the stillness diagnostics: |accel| frozen at EXACTLY 0.171 m/s^2 on one controller and 0.121 on the other across every idle packet -- impossible for a real resting accelerometer (must read ~9.81) and precisely each device's own offsets -- plus a fake constant gyro of 0.006-0.021 rad/s = 20-70 deg/min, THE ENTIRE RANGE of 'drift' chased across two sessions, always at R^2=1.000 because it was arithmetic, not measurement. Rates changed between wake cycles because what integrates is factory_offset MINUS whatever the bias estimator had converged on that session -- which is also, exactly, why consecutive measurements of the same resting controller disagreed by up to 5x (9.4 / 51.5 / 71.7 deg/min) and why the whole topic looked unmeasurable. ||| HOW IT WAS FOUND, kept because the path is the lesson. (1) Measurements would not reproduce, so iteration stopped and scripts/drift-measure.py got built: fixed settle, fixed capture, lsq slope, R^2, movement self-validation, estimator fires per fusion instance recorded per window, everything appended to ~/vr/logs/drift-measure.jsonl with the environment. Its first two back-to-back windows disagreed (inter-controller -1.58 vs -11.62 deg/min) -- 'system not stationary' was itself the finding. (2) Its fires-per-instance field showed BOTH controller estimators stopped at fire #16 = ~32 s after coming to rest, every time -- the first hard evidence of a ~30 s motion gate. (3) CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT, user executing: wake ONE controller with a button press, leave the other as control. The woken one resumed estimating with counter continuity (#16 -> #17), re-slept, and its extrapolation rate CHANGED (30.5 -> 46.6 deg/min) while the untouched one held 32.7-34.1 across three windows. Sleep hypothesis confirmed -- but only half right about the mechanism. (4) FIX 1, prediction-horizon cap (patch 0034, 100 ms cap, zero velocities past 1 s stale): VERIFICATION FAILED -- both controllers still turned at 46-50 deg/min, R^2=1.00. Stated plainly at the time: prediction was the wrong sole mechanism. (5) The stillness diagnostic (added to answer 'is the gate even reached') held the real answer: controllers WERE streaming during 'idle', with |accel| ~ 0.15 -- physically impossible, constant per device, and equal to each device's factory offsets. Zeroed-IMU packets, calibration re-adding offsets. (6) FIX 2 (patch 0035): detect six exact raw zeros -- no live sensor produces that -- skip fusion, deliberately do NOT advance last_imu_timestamp_ns so 0034's cap engages. All three fixes are needed: the estimator cannot fire during idle (its gate wants |accel|~g), the cap never engaged while packets flowed, and without the estimator the awake-window bias stays uncorrected. ||| ALSO CLOSED THIS SESSION (patches 0032-0033): m_imu_3dof_reset() silently killed the auto-estimator (cached enable bool wiped by U_ZERO; duplicate state deleted -- one debug-GUI 3dof/SLAM toggle would have disabled it for the session with nothing saying so); the estimator now SMOOTHS (EMA alpha 0.25 over 1 s windows) instead of adopting each estimate whole -- raw estimates of the same motionless device scattered 34.5-63.9 deg/min, smoothed they hold 65.5-65.9; and WMR_CONTROLLER_IMU_TO_DEVICE defaults OFF: it never fixed its target symptom, the symptom MOVED HANDS between sessions (left pointing at the wearer, later right -- a fixed mirrored-calibration error cannot migrate, drift can), and the workflow's frame review argues it double-applies (with eye_params=NULL it collapses to P_imu_ht0, and the controller IMU path mirrors the HMD's plain-3dof path, wmr_hmd.c:1123, which does not apply it -- not the SLAM path at :1184 which legitimately does). Kept as a knob; the computed-but-unused transform is still a real gap. ||| MY OWN ERRORS THIS ARC, recorded: called 'only one device estimating' from interleaved unlabeled counters (all three were -- labels added); predicted the clamp alone would zero the drift (it did not); earlier attributed common-mode rotation to 'the SLAM frame carrying the controllers' (controller orientation never passes through SLAM; the scalar angle-from-start just made independent similar-rate drifts look synchronized). The user's contributions were decisive twice: the single-controller wake test, and moving everything 'para tener referencia' before the final run, which gave the estimator its awake convergence window. ||| WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, so nobody reads 0.00 as 'orientation solved': drift while IN HAND (micro-motion keeps real samples flowing; the estimator only converges during stillness windows -- in-hand yaw behaviour under play is unmeasured on the new binary); the head's own ~65 deg/min bias (now auto-corrected at rest, matches the 3dof roll reports; wear-time behaviour unmeasured); wmr_controller_og.c almost certainly needs the 0035 treatment (no OG hardware to verify); and everything open from T163/T164 (bistable constellation flip, 4/s sample rate with the 5th gate found by the workflow, 6dof pacing, floor calibration design). The head never sends zeroed packets -- its 41/41 stillness diagnostics were all normal -- so 0035 changes nothing for it.

modo: T166: LAB MACHINE -- live in-game verification of the 2026-08-12 6DoF SLAM milestone with the headset on. One new tracking-freeze bug found, the startup divergence reproduced 2/2, and the SLAM CPU cost is reclassified from accepted tradeoff to open bug by explicit user decision
driver: lab-full 2286029f8 (patches 0001-0035 all applied and built), jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof, Aircar (AppID 1073390)
veredicto: USER WEARING THE HEADSET, live session, three fresh 6dof launches in a row. ||| FINDING 1 -- the startup divergence reproduces on every fresh 6dof launch tested tonight (2/2 with a valid camera stream; see Finding 2 for the third). Position runs away 30-134 m within the first 20-30 s of the session, overlapping the CPU-heavy Steam/Proton/DXVK shader-compile window -- the same CPU-load trigger already named in patch 0021's commit message. Run 1 (logs/slam-20260813-004147): excursion to ~80 m over ~20 s at an average implied speed of roughly 1-4 m/s -- never crossed SLAM_AUTO_RESET_MAX_SPEED (10 m/s) in any single step, so the guard never fired and the tracker stayed stuck oscillating around (72-80, -22, 2.5-5) m for the rest of the session (7+ minutes), never recovering. User-reported symptom: 'me estoy yendo hacia un costado derecho'. Confirmed with the raw tracking.csv, not just user impression. Side note the user flagged as worth keeping (see docs/pruebas.jsonl-adjacent idea note): being anchored 80 m from the ship gave an unplanned but liked effect, seeing the ship from outside. Run 2 (logs/slam-20260813-005514): excursion to -104 m over ~28 s, but this time DID cross the auto-reset threshold and recovered to near-origin on its own -- confirms the guard works when the jump is sharp enough, and that Run 1's failure mode (gradual excursion under the per-step speed gate) is real and distinct, not a fluke. OPEN: SLAM_AUTO_RESET only catches instantaneous jumps over 10 m/s; a divergence that unfolds over several seconds at moderate implied speed escapes it entirely, exactly as happened in Run 1. Needs a second detector on cumulative displacement over a short window, not just per-step speed. Also still open from T163/patch 0023: even a successful auto-reset re-anchors at the origin without telling the application, so the world anchor still moves. ||| FINDING 2 -- new bug, not previously documented: a single fatal read error on the Hololens Sensors device killed tracking for an entire session. logs/jack-in-wayland.log (session started ~00:51): 'ERROR [hololens_sensors_read_packets] Error reading from Hololens Sensors device. Call to os_hid_read returned -1', exactly once, near the start of the session (line 681 of 977). After that single error, tracking.csv stayed at 0 lines for the rest of the session -- Basalt never received a first pose, and the compositor kept presenting the last/initial pose forever. User-reported symptom: 'me dejo de funcionar tracking de la cabeza, solo veo la imagen anclada'. monado-service itself stayed alive the whole time (no crash) -- only the sensor read path died. The USB device (045e:0659 HoloLens Sensors) was still enumerated and healthy immediately after, ruling out a physical/electrical cause for that instance. Distinct from the already-tolerated companion/control-channel errors (patches 0001 'Survive transient companion device drops', 0004 'Tolerate transient read errors in the BT controller path'): those cover the HMD control and Bluetooth controller channels, not this one. The main Hololens Sensors stream -- the actual camera+IMU source Basalt depends on -- has no equivalent retry/reconnect around its os_hid_read loop. Recovered only by a full monado-service kill + restart (client reconnect alone would not have helped, since the read thread inside monado-service is what's dead). Reproduced once tonight; not yet root-caused in wmr_hmd.c/the Hololens Sensors driver code, and not yet turned into a patch. NEXT SESSION: grep the read loop around hololens_sensors_read_packets for whether it already retries transient -1s the way the companion path does, and if not, why not -- candidate is the same class of fix as patches 0001/0004 applied to this specific device instead. ||| FINDING 3 -- user directive: the SLAM CPU cost (already measured in T163: Basalt with SLAM_THREADS=2 pins roughly one whole core, 6dof runs ~50-70 fps against ~80-90 fps in 3dof) is explicitly reclassified from an accepted tradeoff to an open bug that needs fixing, not just documenting as a limit. User's own framing: has to be measured against what native Windows WMR inside-out tracking costs on the same headset, and brought in line with it -- 'no podemos gastar un micro entero en hacerlo... lo tendria que poder hacer una tostadora eso'. Read as: there is likely real inefficiency in the current Basalt integration/config (the denser detect_plus feature-detection settings from T162 are the leading suspect for extra unnecessary cost), not that 6dof SLAM is inherently a whole-core-or-nothing problem. NOT DONE YET, and the explicit next step: no Windows-side CPU measurement of the G2's native inside-out tracking exists yet in this project to use as the comparison baseline. Until that number exists there is nothing concrete to optimize toward -- do that measurement first, on the Windows machine, before touching Basalt's threading/detection config again.

modo: T167: LAB MACHINE -- fix batch 0036-0039 written, built and deployed live mid-session; battery-alert chain built (0040, pending rebuild); the never-tried/log-only game round completed with 5 verdicts; Windows tracking-baseline plan documented (docs/30)
driver: lab-full 2d1d53563 (0001-0039 built and running; 0040 written, applies clean, NOT built), jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof + WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS=1
veredicto: FOUR PATCHES FROM TONIGHT'S FOUR INVESTIGATION AGENTS, all built and live by ~01:20. 0036 (from T166 finding 2): hololens_sensors_read_packets tolerates up to 10 consecutive os_hid_read failures with visible WARNs (same shape as wmr_bt_controller.c) instead of dying forever on the first -1 -- the shared read thread in wmr_run_thread() carries IMU + SLAM feed + controller tunnel, and patch 0001's own commit message described this exact risk but only fixed the companion direction. 0037: two constellation mechanisms behind 'one hand anchored, then it jumps'. (a) Deep-search backoff: the depth-8 combinatorial search ran to completion every frame for any device without a strong match -- agent-measured as the dominant share of constellation's ~2 cores, and the searches saturating the slow threads WAS the collapsed solution rate (measured live: 11 and 7 optical fixes per 30 s per device, i.e. one fix every ~3-4 s, against 30 Hz cameras; with the 500 ms freshness gate that IS the anchored hand, and each late fix lands as a jump). Now per-camera-per-device exponential backoff 50->800 ms on the deep pass only; shallow still runs every sample. (b) Staleness-scaled recovery window: tryDeviceBlobRecovery hard-rejects candidates outside prior_pos_error/prior_rot_error, which are +-10cm/30deg literals NEVER written anywhere, against a prior that extrapolates with zero velocity (frozen at the last fix) -- so a hand that moved >10 cm could never reacquire cheaply and every frame fell to the expensive search. Window now grows with sample age (0.5 m/s, 60 deg/s, capped 0.75 m/150 deg). 0038: instrumentation for the 45 fps mechanism found by the pacing agent -- NVIDIA Linux has no VK_GOOGLE_display_timing, so Monado runs the FAKE compositor pacer whose anchor is a free-running software clock with no vblank feedback: one stall shifts the cadence a whole period forward permanently (matches the measured signature exactly: hundreds of frames late by EXACTLY 11.1/33.3/77.7 ms, GPU work at 4 ms of an 11 ms budget, and comp_renderer's independent real-present check firing ZERO times in 307k log lines). The catch-up now logs a WARN with step count + running total. First data: 13 events tonight, all thousands-of-periods idle-resume catch-ups (benign); the signal to watch in a real game session is jumped-1-period events correlating with late frames. THE REAL FIX, designed but not built: feed the VK_KHR_present_wait timestamp (supported by the driver, already collected by comp_renderer) back into the pacer as ground truth. 0039: the per-client wait thread ran SCHED_OTHER while sharing slot_lock/list_and_timing_lock with the SCHED_FIFO(99) main loop -- priority inversion under tracking load, the likely stall trigger that 0038's free-running pacer then makes permanent. Now raised like the main loop. NOTE: CLAUDE.md's 'RT priority for Monado still pending sudo' is stale -- the main threads have had SCHED_FIFO 99 all along (log-confirmed); it was only this wait thread missing. FIRST NUMBERS AFTER THE BATCH, needing a real VR-game session to confirm: monado idle CPU 4.2 -> ~2.2 cores (the backoff working; Basalt's ~2 cores remain), and ZERO 'Frame late by' lines the whole post-patch session against 963+ before -- but tonight's post-patch games all ran 2D, so the fps/pacer verification against a real VR load (Aircar/Propagation) is still pending, as is hand-behavior verification of 0037. BATTERY CHAIN (its own agent, motivated by the user finding the right controller's battery nearly dead -- which also explains that controller's blind/anchored session AND fed the deep-search saturation: dim LEDs = never a strong match = full search every frame): patch 0040 wires the always-parsed-then-discarded battery byte from wmr_controller_hp.c into xrt_device::get_battery_status (IPC already carries it end to end); scripts/controller-battery-check.py reads it via libmonado (monado-gui's own safe pattern) and vr-launcher.py calls it right after monado comes up -- red warning naming the hand and the tracking consequence, never blocks. Applies clean on 2d1d53563, NOT YET BUILT. Scale of the raw byte explicitly unverified (raw/255 conservative; evidence from the Oasis Windows driver -- HID Battery Strength usage + using_1v2_batteries chemistry-curve key, found via xref.py on a local copy -- hints it may be 0-100). wmr_controller_og.c needs the same fix, no OG hardware. GAME ROUND, one at a time, all physically verified, docs/23 updated in place: Chornobayivka re-verified working on the full 6dof stack (~50 fps, head good; that session predates 0037 so controllers were bad project-wide). Surgeon Simulator MTM reclassified from T073's log-only 'crash-loop' to a named xrizer gap: probes the REAL 2014-era IVRSystem_007 four times, unimplemented, concludes no VR, runs 2D at 450 fps with an in-game 'need VR' notice. World of Guns retested: T073's 'never past the probe' no longer holds -- reaches SYNCHRONIZED, abandons in 17 ms (Dagon-class), stays 2D at 144 fps SHOWING its VR UI with a frozen laser pointer and no input. BlazeRush first-ever launch: native Linux binary exits <1 s; VR belongs to its Windows build, needs Proton forced, deferred. InMind + ovrplugin-stub (first try on this title): stub works -- DllNotFoundException gone, boots, music plays; fullscreen dies on Unity-5.3-vs-XWayland XError BadMatch storm + Mono fatal; windowed survives that but OVRManager.Update NREs every frame, renders black, exits after ~20 s. Unlike InCell this build has NO OpenVR plugin -- Oculus-only path, so real VR means the parked LibOVR->OpenVR shim. ALSO: docs/30-windows-tracking-baseline-plan.md written from the Windows-tracing agent (user's strace-on-Windows idea): key framing -- no native WMR runtime exists to trace (closed in docs/19), the baseline target is vrserver.exe hosting driver_oasis.dll; host-Bluetooth tracing is structurally empty (controller tunnel); one-boot 30-40 min checklist with typeperf/wpr/Process Explorer/USBPcap, deliverable in core-equivalents to compare against Linux. Stale-zombie caveat for tonight's numbers: Blast the Past and SUPERHOT processes from earlier sessions were found still alive and burning CPU mid-evening, killed at ~01:15 -- measurements before that point carry unknown contamination.

modo: T168: LAB MACHINE -- the real pacer fix (0041) built and verified in-game the same night; the 90 fps blocker is now isolated to a single named layer
driver: lab-full f24b56701 (0001-0041 built and running), jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof + constellation, Aircar
veredicto: PATCH 0041, the fix 0038's instrumentation was built to justify: comp_target_swapchain_wait_for_present timestamps each successful VK_KHR_present_wait return (the moment the frame actually presented) and feeds it through the previously-no-op u_pc_info into the fake pacer, which re-anchors forward-only (the vblank thread's true scanout times still win when fresh; using_fake_pacer keeps synthesized info away from the real display-timing pacer). MEASURED, 30 s windows during real Aircar gameplay: pacer phase jumps 7-15 -> 1-6 per window; frames late 4-5% (unchanged); monado CPU by true /proc/stat delta 2.2-2.3 cores. USER VERDICT wearing it: 'casi perfecto', ~60 fps (had read 45 early in the session), head tracking good moving inside the cockpit, drift bounded within ~50 cm in-world -- and the visible snap-backs while motionless are NOT the auto-reset (zero SLAM_AUTO_RESET firings in the log) but Basalt's own relocalization pulling ordinary drift back, i.e. T162's documented 'bounded and returns' behaviour seen from inside. CONCLUSION THE NIGHT CONVERGES ON: with the compositor pacer anchor now hardware-grounded and CPU halved, the remaining 60-not-90 lock and residual 4-5% late frames live in ONE remaining layer -- the client-side cadence: the multi-compositor wrapper broadcasts predicted timings the app inherits one-behind and never re-derives from hardware (mechanism already mapped file:line in the pacing agent's report, candidate fixes ranked). That is the named first target of the next session. INCIDENT, self-inflicted and worth the reminder: restarted monado-service for the 0041 deploy while Aircar was still alive -- exactly the standing rule violation ('never restart monado under a live title') -- and the game's OpenXR instance died with ERROR_INSTANCE_LOST, xrizer panicked in WaitGetPoses, and the user had to force-quit. The rule exists because of nights like this; the crash says nothing about 0041 itself. STATIC MEASUREMENT with the game running and headset untouched (pre-0041 build, same night): SLAM drift 0.48 m over 137 s = 0.21 m/min (same order as the historical 0.37; conditions differ, not claimed as an improvement), frames late 4% IDENTICAL to gameplay -- the load-independence datum that pinned the pacer as structural. First static-drift parse was garbage (awk over truncated mid-write CSV rows) and was redone properly by timestamp over complete rows; noted so nobody trusts single tail-line CSV parses again.

modo: T169: LAB MACHINE -- the client-side cadence lock closed in three measured iterations (free-run rejected, pipelined pacing, honest promise); first-ever roll-drift number; the fps ceiling moves from pacing to raw tracking CPU
driver: lab-full 4accebdb4 (0001-0042), jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof + constellation + U_PACING_APP_PIPELINED=true, Aircar
veredicto: THE LAST PACING LAYER, three A/B iterations in one sitting, each measured in 3x30s windows plus the wearer: (1) FREE-RUN REJECTED WITH DATA: U_PACING_APP_IMMEDIATE_WAIT_FRAME_RETURN_BELOW_REFRESH=1 took frames-late from 4-5% to ZERO -- and the wearer's fps fell 60 -> 30 -> 18, worsening as unpaced rendering burned the cores the tracking stack needed. Pacing must stay; the enemy was only its SERIAL assumption. (2) PATCH 0042, U_PACING_APP_PIPELINED: the app pacer's model requires the full cpu+draw+gpu sum to fit before a promised slot, silently forbidding the CPU-vs-GPU overlap OpenXR is designed around -- an app whose serial pipeline exceeds 11.1 ms gets every other slot forever regardless of per-stage times. The pipelined gate uses cpu+draw+margin only. First deploy: wearer 'bastante mas fluido', but 69-71% of frames logged late by exactly one period with compositor CPU climbing window over window (5.5 -> 6.7 cores) -- the promise was one period optimistic by construction, so pose prediction aimed at the wrong time and the delivery queue churned. (3) HONEST PROMISE (amended into 0042): in pipelined mode the promise shifts +1 period to the slot the GPU actually reaches, while the wake stays early. Wearer: 'mucho mejor'. Measured: late 69-71% -> 25-31%, CPU churn spiral gone. WHERE THE CEILING NOW SITS, and it is not pacing anymore: monado at 5.1-5.3 cores in this config (SLAM ~2 + constellation with both controllers live ~2 + compositor at higher delivered rate ~1) against 6 physical cores leaves the game starved -- wearer: 'se arrastra' -- with the GPU at 43%, idle. The serial-mode baseline of 2.2 cores was measured with controllers OFF; not comparable directly, noted. The named next moves are already planned: the docs/30 Windows baseline (what SHOULD tracking cost), the 2-vs-4-camera constellation question (CPU audit row 3), and a Basalt config middle-ground sweep (row 4). FIRST ROLL-DRIFT NUMBER IN PROJECT HISTORY (T162 explicitly left it unmeasured): headset resting on a flat surface, 116 s window, gravity-direction (pitch/roll) drift 1.39 deg/min, yaw component ~0.5 deg/min. That is ~28 deg of tilted horizon per 20 min of play -- exactly the wearer's recurring 'gira sobre roll'. Diagnostic: gravity is accelerometer-observable, a healthy VIO holds pitch/roll near zero drift; 0031-0035 already cleaned the resting-IMU path, so this points at Basalt's gravity alignment, the best-characterised open item for next session. Caveat recorded: the stillness checker's 8mm/10s threshold is tighter than SLAM's own position drift, so its 'moved during window' warning is a probable false positive; the wearer confirmed 'dejo todo fijo'. ALSO SEEN LIVE: pitch-down snap after a position auto-reset -- evidence the 0023 'carry the reset offset through to the output pose' TODO must cover orientation too, not just position (Basalt re-estimates gravity from scratch at whatever head attitude the reset catches). PROCESS INCIDENT, repeated: launching a game in the same breath as a monado restart raced the dying instance TWICE tonight (xrizer panic ERROR_INSTANCE_LOST in WaitGetPoses, user force-quit both times). Rule: restart the stack, verify Socket ready AND wait a beat, then launch -- never chain them.

modo: T170: LAB MACHINE -- first-ever SteamVR-native attempt via Monado's own SteamVR driver plugin: driver loads, G2 recognized, room setup runs; blocked at vrcompositor's display lease. Parked cleanly, user call: 'continuamos luego'
driver: SteamVR 2.16.7 native Linux + driver_monado.so (lab-full 4accebdb4 build), 3dof env (WMR_SLAM=0 WMR_CAMERAS=0), GNOME Wayland session
veredicto: MOTIVATION: the user's stated north star tonight -- build a 'museum' of ALL working VR experiences -- and SteamVR Home is a museum piece AND a simple viewer/launcher. Also corrects stale doc: SteamVR native Linux RUNS on this rig (vrmonitor healthy through every attempt), the old 'vrmonitor broken' framing predates this. CHAIN OF FIXES, each verified: (1) registered /home/iam/vr/monado/build/steamvr-monado with vrpathreg ('monado' now in External Drivers next to the useless Windows-only 'holographic'). (2) driver_monado.so failed to load in vrserver: missing libs in the Steam runtime env -- libhidapi-libusb first, then the OpenCV closure. Copied the full ldd closure (~174 libs, 309 MB) next to the driver (patch 0010's $ORIGIN rpath covers only DIRECT deps) and patchelf'd every copy with rpath $ORIGIN so transitive deps (libwebp via opencv_imgcodecs) resolve too; patchelf installed by the user via sudo for this. (3) driver then LOADED but 'Failed to create system devices' -- fixed by env: WMR_SLAM=0 WMR_CAMERAS=0 via SteamVR's (250820) launch options; the default WMR_SLAM=1 with no VIT/Basalt env in vrserver's context is the likely device-creation killer (not verified to the line, next session can). Env verified reaching vrserver via /proc/PID/environ. RESULT: 'monado: Initializing Monado driver' -> stays resident, SteamVR event stream flowing, 'CheckHmdDriverName: ActualTrackingSystemName: monado', 'Using existing HMD monado.HP Reverb Virtual Reality Headset G2', room setup wizard ran on the desktop (user answered Standing Only per this rig's SLAM-origin model). Panel re-activated by hand (panel.py activate, DP-2 connected) since killing monado-service had screened it off. THE BLOCKER, stated by SteamVR itself: error 498 'Failed to lease display' plus an explicit claim that GNOME Wayland does not support DRM leases required for VR (help.steampowered.com/en/faqs/view/18A4-1E10-8A94-3DDA). THE CLAIM IS FALSE AS STATED for this rig -- GNOME/mutter offers wp_drm_lease_device_v1 and Monado leases the same connector through it every session, all night, tonight included. The real story is almost certainly that VRCOMPOSITOR does not speak the Wayland lease protocol (SteamVR runs under XWayland here; its lease path expects X11/RandR leasing or direct display access). NEXT-SESSION OPTIONS, in order: (a) try the whole thing from an X11 session where RandR leasing exists (the pre-Wayland jack-in.sh path proved NVIDIA X11 direct mode works for Monado); (b) check SteamVR betas/flags for native Wayland lease support; (c) accept SteamVR-native as display-less driver validation only and keep xrizer as the runtime for actual play. ALSO CLOSED: the 'SteamVR setup is incomplete' popup root cause -- vrcompositor-launcher had no capabilities (getcap empty); the FAQ's known Linux issue. User ran sudo setcap CAP_SYS_NICE+ep on it (same class of fix as our patch 0039 for Monado's wait thread, pleasingly). SIDE FINDINGS: 'Windows Mixed Reality for SteamVR' (719950) verified by inspection to be a Windows-only SteamVR driver package, nothing launchable on Linux -- BUT it carries official WMR controller render models + input profiles (resources/rendermodels/hand_controller), noted as assets for showing real G2 controller models through xrizer instead of generic Oculus Touch. The Windows SteamLibrary at /mnt/videos (ntfs-3g, writable) holds never-tried heavyweights incl. Half-Life Alyx (69 GB on disk; Windows depots are Proton-usable directly) -- Steam silently rejected my libraryfolders.vdf edit on restart, and the user deferred ('solo los instalados por ahora'); Alyx launch options are already planted in localconfig for whenever. Steam OVERWRITES localconfig.vdf edits on shutdown from memory -- edit only with Steam fully dead, verified the hard way. A stuck Steam controller-config-sync dialog silently queues all applaunches until clicked -- check the desktop when launches go nowhere.

modo: T171: x3600 after full hardware rearrangement (second Windows system added, single monitor) -- headset 'not detected' on BOTH Windows systems and half-dead on Linux; full physical-layer diagnosis to resolution
driver: User returned from a failed Windows tracking-baseline attempt (docs/30): headset not detected on either the old or the new Windows machine. Same headset+cable on this Linux boot showed the classic USB2-branch error -71 storm at boot with ONLY the SuperSpeed hub (04b4:6504) enumerating -- and even that with an empty downstream (no HoloLens sensors). DP: zero hotplug on all three connectors.
veredicto: RESOLVED, NOTHING IS BROKEN -- it is a marginal C-plug/adapter seat that engages ONE pin subgroup per insertion; the winning move was the docs/06 shortcut, revalidated verbatim: right rear (CPU) port first, then rotate the C plug 180 degrees INSIDE the C-to-A adapter without changing port. Full elimination chain across 10 seatings: (1) xhci controller rebind (software re-enumeration of 0000:09:00.3) reproduced the identical half-dead state -- host stuck-state ruled out; (2) the pattern across seats was EXACTLY ONE branch per seating, never both: rear A#1 gave SS-only (x2), rear A#2 gave USB2-only (x3, perfectly reproducible), native mobo USB-C gave SS-only in BOTH orientations (x3, before and after visor reseat + mains cycle), one chipset/front port gave nothing, so every conductor group in the cable demonstrably works -- this is NOT the T039-T040 wholesale conductor-group death; (3) a 5-minute quiet-watch on a half-dead seat logged ZERO spontaneous events -- the state is stable at rest, no self-recovery, only physical manipulation changes it; (4) control experiment: a Xiaomi phone enumerated instantly on the same native-C port's USB2 pins where the G2 had failed 7 consecutive times -- port absolved, cable seat condemned; (5) visor-end reseat and 220V cycle changed nothing (that contact was not the culprit this time); (6) user's standing rule confirmed: only rear CPU-controller ports work at all, and the mobo USB-C has never carried the G2's USB2 pair on any machine. modo: T172: post-reboot autoboot run hung mid-reseat; Windows side still not working -- root-caused the hang and built the missing Windows manual + diagnostic
driver: vr-boot-selector.service (installed) -> timeout 120 power-on.py --pre-login on tty1, headset half-enumerated after the T171 hardware rearrangement
veredicto: THE HANG WAS TWO SAFETY MECHANISMS FIGHTING EACH OTHER, and the evidence is exact: vr-boot-selector.service ran 13:48:17 -> 13:50:35 = 138 s = 10 s selector prompt + 120 s `timeout` ceiling + 3 s + isolate, and NO verdict line was appended to power-on-stats.jsonl in either location (repo copy last entry 12:26:49, ~/vr copy 2026-08-10) -- give_up(), continue_2d() and the LISTO path all log, so the process was killed mid-run, inside the interactive wait_for_reseat() shipped hours earlier in T171. The wrapper's 120 s was sized in T129/T130 for a fully automatic 10-38 s run; the day the diagnostic learned to wait for a human fixing a cable, that ceiling became a guillotine on the human. SECOND, INDEPENDENT CAUSE of 'no pude apretar enter': console_loglevel is 4, so the kernel writes to /dev/tty1 -- and the fault being fixed produces `usb usb3-port1: Cannot enable. Maybe the USB cable is bad?` about once a second (journal shows bursts at 13:48:36-38 and 13:49:33-36). The reseat instructions and the prompt scrolled away; worse, wait_for_reseat printed its status line ONLY when the status string changed, so an Enter into an unchanged state produced zero output -- indistinguishable from a dead console. FIXES, all in place and exercised through a pty harness (all four exits: fixed / skip / giveup / Enter-rearm): power-on.py now mutes console printk for the duration of each interactive wait and always restores it (finally + a SIGTERM handler, so `timeout`'s TERM can't leave the VT silent for the rest of the boot); the wait has two clocks -- 90 s if nobody ever answers (an unattended boot must not be held hostage) and 300 s rearmed on every Enter (a human with hands in the cable must not be cut off); it answers EVERY keypress and repaints every 10 s with a countdown; give_up()/continue_2d() now print the exact command to retry, since after handing off to graphical.target the console is gone. vr-boot-selector.sh's ceiling goes 120 -> 1200 s (backstop, not normal path) and the run is recorded via `script -q -e -a /var/log/vr-boot-selector.log` -- `script` and not `| tee` on purpose: a pipe makes stdout a non-tty and silently kills every color, and red/yellow carry meaning there. Verified separately that `script -e` propagates 124 from timeout. WINDOWS SIDE, user's ask: the two codes he keeps hitting now have a documented meaning. 108 'Headset not detected' = SteamVR has no HMD at all, and on this hardware it has coincided every time with an incomplete USB census -- the T171 seat lottery leaving the SuperSpeed branch out, which WMR/Oasis requires; it is a cable/port problem, fixed by the docs/06 ladder, and the success criterion is 5/5 devices in Device Manager, not 'the headset shows up'. 422 'unexpected problem' = SteamVR started and the driver failed under it, so reseating cannot fix it: safe-mode-disabled oasis add-on after a crash, a stale unlock (re-required after a GPU change or a Windows in-place upgrade -- both plausible right now after the rearrangement), the SteamVR beta branch, or corrupt WindowsHolographicDevices data. 498 is neither: it is our own Linux-native SteamVR lease failure from T170. ALSO ANSWERED, the user's 'no se bien que funcion cumple Oasis': the driver is a SteamVR DLL that vrserver loads by itself every start (the same driver_oasis disassembled in docs/09); the Steam 'app' is only a setup/unlock/pairing tool, so leaving it installed and closed is the correct steady state, and the unlock is required once per PC, per headset, per newly paired controller, and after GPU or Windows in-place changes. NEW LANDMINE FOUND UPSTREAM, unverified here but cheap to check and directly relevant to our own cable saga: the Oasis unlock tool HANGS at EDID identification with the G2 v1 cable (PN L72080-001) and completes with the v2 (L72080-002), reproduced across three headsets by the reporter -- if the unlock hangs, read the PN off the cable before theorising. SHIPPED: docs/31-windows-bringup-and-errors.md (the Windows manual, [lab] vs [upstream] marked line by line) and windows-kit/power-on.ps1 (same five-step shape as power-on.py: census split by branch, port, Bluetooth pairing, Oasis/SteamVR software state, verdict + error triage; read-only, no admin). The PS1 is WRITTEN BUT NEVER RUN -- there is no PowerShell on this machine to even syntax-check it; first Windows run is a test of the script too. Two index rows added to docs/22 for 108/422. Headset was not connected to this machine at any point during the fixes (0/5 enumerated), so nothing here is hardware-verified.

modo: T173: audit of the Windows install READ OFFLINE FROM LINUX (nvme0n1p3 mounted rw) instead of spending boot cycles -- plus the bring-up kit left on C: for the next reboot
driver: Windows 11 on nvme0n1p3 mounted at /media/iam/78E65676E656349A via udisksctl (ntfs3, rw -- no hiberfil.sys, fast startup already off); SteamVR 2.16.7 + Oasis + the legacy MixedRealityVRDriver, all three installed

So a T171-style seat that engages only the USB2 branch leaves Windows showing audio+companion and leaves SteamVR with no driver claiming a headset: that IS error 108. The seat lottery and the Windows symptom are now connected by the driver's own activation condition, not by inference. REST OF THE AUDIT, all read offline: LastKnown.ActualHMDDriver = 'oasis' with the G2's model and the unit's serial number (value not recorded here -- public repo), so Oasis has already run on this install and the unlock was done here at least once -- 'missing unlock' drops off the top of the 108 list; SteamVR 2.16.7 on the STABLE branch (no betakey in appmanifest 250820/3824490/719950), so the 'beta causes 422' story does not apply here; no ProgramData\WindowsHolographicDevices, only the per-user SpatialStore; no hiberfil.sys. ACTED ON, one hypothesis: the old WMR driver was still both INSTALLED (app 719950) and REGISTERED in openvrpaths.vrpath next to Oasis, and on 24H2 it has no runtime behind it while claiming every headset -- added `"driver_holographic": {"enable": false}` to Steam\config\steamvr.vrsettings, which is what SteamVR itself writes when an add-on is unchecked (revert = re-check it in Manage Add-Ons). Best available 422 candidate from outside Windows; the next boot is the test, and it is labelled as a hypothesis in the doc, not a fix. SHIPPED TO C:\reverb-g2\: LEEME.txt (Spanish quick start), diagnostico.bat, tunear-admin.bat (self-elevating), power-on.ps1 and docs/31. Two encoding decisions made on purpose and worth keeping: the PS1 is stripped to pure ASCII (Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less UTF-8 file as ANSI, and the console codepage mangles accents anyway) and the .bat files are written CRLF (LF-only batch misparses parenthesised if blocks -- the self-elevation wrapper uses one). power-on.ps1 also grew the -Tune mode the user asked for: USB selective suspend off, per-device USB power management off on every USB device, PCIe ASPM off, CPU min/max 100%, sleep/monitor/disk timeouts never, fast startup off, Game DVR off, with the undo commands printed. Current values are read from HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\User\PowerSchemes rather than by parsing `powercfg /query`, whose output is localised -- the GUIDs are not. Rationale recorded in docs/31: a branch that 'disconnects on its own' under selective suspend reads exactly like the docs/22 marginal contact, so this removes a confounder from the oldest open question in the project. The headset was never connected to the Linux side during any of it (0/5 enumerated).

modo: T174: LAB (x3600, dual boot) -- full bring-up from a dead cable to a user-confirmed 90 Hz session, driven by a new AUDIBLE guide; plus the measurement that settles the console-vs-graphical question
driver: lab-full, jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof, GNOME Wayland, Aircar via Steam/Proton/xrizer; new scripts/reseat_audio.py
veredicto: END-TO-END, HUMAN-CONFIRMED: 'panel encendido' and then 'audio perfecto en el casco, todo como esperado' on a real Aircar session. Chain, each link measured: USB 0/5 (nothing enumerated, LED on the inline box OFF -- the fastest discriminator, it only reports USB 5V) -> plugged in -> 2/5 SS-only -> rotate C plug 180 in adapter -> 0/5 -> move to the NEIGHBOURING rear port -> 4/5 but EVERYTHING on the hub's USB2 face with the cameras at 480M -> rotate again -> 5/5 with cameras at 5000M. Four seatings, and the winning cell was again 'other rear port + flipped plug', consistent with T171. THE SEAT LOTTERY IS NOT BENIGN WHILE IT LASTS: on the 4/5 seat the whole USB2 tree dropped and re-enumerated SPONTANEOUSLY at 14:42:19-23 (hub, sensors, audio, companion; `Unable to submit urb #1: -19` mid-stream), which the user detected by ear -- the audio jumped to the speakers for 4 s and came back. That is the T052-T057 signature, not a replug. Then: panel.py activate -> DP-3 connected, 384-byte EDID, fingerprint matches, non-desktop=1, modes 4320x2160@90 present -> jack-in-wayland first try: lease granted, 4320x2160@90.00, 'Using builder wmr' (not the Simulated HMD fallback), BOTH controllers named, Basalt SLAM started. NEW TOOL, the user's own idea while his hands were behind the tower: scripts/reseat_audio.py speaks the census. Ladder is 'more beeps = closer' (1 nothing, 2 one branch, 3 cameras slow, 4 panel dark, 5 'panel ignited', arpeggio 'ready to jack in'), plus one-shot events for gamepad and each controller. Design decisions the user set explicitly and that are worth keeping: it must STAY SILENT when the hardware is healthy (intermediate states only speak after 6 s stuck -- a good boot walks the ladder in two seconds and narrating it is noise), and 'panel ignited' vs 'ready to jack in' are TWO stages because the HP logo is power+HID and lights with no video at all, while the backlight needs a compositor scanning out. Output is pinned to a NON-USB sink (the headset's own speakers hang off the branch being diagnosed and vanish exactly when there is something to report) and speech is rendered to WAV first, since espeak cannot pick a sink. A REAL BUG WAS CAUGHT LIVE by this tool: it reported 'panel dark' during a perfectly healthy session, because once mutter leases the connector /sys/class/drm stops reporting it connected to everyone else -- and in that state the loop would have fired panel.py activate every 8 s INTO a live session. Fixed: a live session outranks sysfs. THE ARCHITECTURE QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED WITH A NUMBER, not an opinion. Under real VR load: monado-service 233% CPU / 374 MB, AirCar 46% / 759 MB, gnome-shell 6.5% / 358 MB. gnome-shell costs 2.8% of what Monado costs and ~2% of the total VR workload -- moving the pipeline to a bare console would buy 0.07 cores and 356 MB of 32 GB, at the price of reopening mutter-bare's two known blockers (no live-hotplug refresh, SDDM autologin won't target it). User's own criterion was 'if it saves almost nothing, we go graphical': DECIDED, graphical, and the effort goes to a nicer activation procedure. ALSO FOUND, cost ~15 minutes and it is not the headset: Aircar launched with audio in the HMD but a flat 2D image and `client_connected` stuck at 0. Cause was the ORDER of `runtime` in ~/.config/openvr/openvrpaths.vrpath -- T170's parked SteamVR-native experiment had left SteamVR ahead of xrizer, and OpenVR takes the first entry, so the title loaded SteamVR's vrclient, found no session, and fell back to flat. Set to xrizer alone (backup kept alongside); relaunch connected immediately. Added to CLAUDE.md's trap list, together with a second one paid for the same session: `pgrep -f "Aircar"` from this agent's shell matches the shell itself and killed it (exit 144) -- bracket game patterns too, not just monado's.

modo: T175: LAB -- the frame-pacing A/B rerun from scratch on a live title, and the artefact the metric cannot see
driver: jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof (no constellation), Aircar via Steam/Proton/xrizer, GNOME Wayland, 4320x2160@90
veredicto: PIPELINED APP PACING IS NOW THE DEFAULT IN jack-in-wayland.sh, and this session is why it had to be: T169 measured patch 0042 and then left it as an env var nobody exports, so today the same fault was rediscovered from zero on a fresh session. Measured, headset held STILL, same title / same cable seat / nothing else changed: serial 12.37% late frames, median lateness 11.12 ms -- pinned at exactly one full 90 Hz period -- against 0.94 / 0.77 / 0.69% over three consecutive 45 s windows with U_PACING_APP_PIPELINED=true. 13-18x. THE DIAGNOSIS THAT MADE IT FINDABLE was measuring the SAME thing twice under different load: playing gave 9.91%, the headset sitting still gave 12.37% -- WORSE. A performance problem gets worse when you push it; this got no worse, and its lateness was quantised to exactly one period rather than spread. That is scheduling, not capacity, and it was visible with the GPU at 56% and the game using 46% of a single core while losing one frame in eight. An app burning half a core while dropping frames is waiting for a slot, not fighting for resources. THE COST, SEEN BY THE WEARER AND NOT BY THE TOOL: in pipelined mode he reports a ghost/trail whose separation from the real image GROWS WITH HEAD ROTATION SPEED. That is the signature of latency -- the frame was rendered against a pose predicted for a moment that has passed -- and it is what pipelined mode adds by construction, since it promises the app a slot one period further out. We traded judder for a stale pose. USER'S VERDICT, and it decides: the 6DoF 'se siente mucho mejor' and this is the new starting point. Ships on by default, VR_PIPELINED=0 reverts. Next target is the pose prediction, which is a different problem from the pacer. THE LESSON ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT, written into both the script and frame-pacing.sh: frame-pacing.sh counts MISSED SLOTS and is blind to LATENCY. A change that trades one for the other therefore reads as a pure 13x win in the tool while the wearer watches a new artefact appear. Both readings were true and neither was sufficient -- the human stays the instrument of record, exactly as CLAUDE.md's core rule says, and this is the first time in the project that rule caught a REGRESSION hiding inside a genuine improvement rather than a false success.

modo: T177: LAB -- the ghost bisected to a single stage with the wearer's eyes, root-caused to filter ORDER, patched, and measured from +42.5 ms behind to 5 ms ahead
driver: lab-full ae2543045 (0001-0044), jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof, SLAM_THREADS=4, play360.sh still photo (native OpenXR) + Aircar (OpenVR/xrizer)
veredicto: THE GHOST IS GONE, and the whole thing was resolved by bisection with the wearer as the instrument rather than by tuning. Symptom, stated precisely by the user and that precision is what cracked it: a trailing image whose SEPARATION FROM THE REAL ONE GROWS WITH HEAD ROTATION SPEED. That is the signature of a fixed time lag (angular separation = angular velocity x lag), not of dropped frames -- which is why the pacing work, real as it was, never touched it. THREE ARMS, same photo, same compositor session, same cable seat: Aircar through xrizer -> ghost; the native OpenXR photo viewer in 6dof -> ghost (xrizer RULED OUT, and with the best possible test case: a still image, scene at infinity, no game logic, no GPU load); the same viewer in 3dof -> NO ghost (compositor, scanout and display RULED OUT). That left the 6dof pose path. A fourth arm, 6dof with SLAM_FILTER=none, was clean too -- naming the one euro filter. ROOT CAUSE IS ORDER, NOT TUNING: the path is predict_pose() -> filter_pose() -> app, so the low pass is the LAST stage and its group delay lands whole on the application with nothing downstream able to pay it back. That is why the parameter sweep failed and had to fail: beta 0.16 -> 60 (375x) only shrank the trail, and raising the derivative cutoff 1 -> 15 did nothing. No gain applied to an output-stage low pass removes that stage's own delay. And it is why filter-on vs filter-off looked like a hard trade all afternoon (ghost vs 12 deg p99 jitter): the filter WAS the continuous motion path. PATCH 0044 moves the filter to the SLAM pose ingest, so the jitter is filtered where it is generated and dead reckoning then integrates the IMU from that pose's own timestamp to the queried time -- which is exactly what cancels the delay. MEASURED, tracking -> delivered pose: +42.5 ms BEHIND -> 5.0 ms AHEAD, residual 0.01%, a 47.5 ms swing; wearer: ghost gone AND resting jitter still suppressed, which no point in the parameter sweep ever achieved. TWO BUGS I INTRODUCED WITH THE NAIVE REORDER, one of them caught by the user within minutes as 'tracking errors when moving fast': the previous pose is read back from the relation history, which now holds FILTERED poses, so the finite-difference angular velocity feeding prediction AND the divergence guard's speed check were measuring raw-minus-filtered -- mostly the filter's own lag, inflating exactly during fast motion (fixed by keeping the last raw pose separately); and tracking.csv plus the EuRoC recorder would have silently started recording filtered poses, redefining the baseline every offline tool in this project compares against -- the next lag measurement would have compared the filter against itself and read a clean, false zero. PARAMETERS STOP BEING COMPILED-IN CONSTANTS, with SEPARATE position and orientation cutoffs because only orientation was swept by a human: 20 Hz, chosen as the LOWEST value that works (30 gave the same verdict), ~8 ms of group delay, under one 90 Hz frame. Wired as the jack-in-wayland.sh default -- the T169 lesson applied on the same day it was written down: a measured fix that nobody activates is not a fix. A VALUE THAT IS ONLY SAFE WITH THE REORDER, stated in the code: at the output stage that same 20 Hz would put Basalt's raw jitter straight into the image. SELF-CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING: earlier the same session I read pose-lag.py's 'prediction leads filtering by 45 ms' as proof the controlled path was healthy and the latency had to be somewhere invisible. Wrong -- prediction.csv is an intermediate that never reaches the app. The number was right and I read its direction backwards; the code, not the CSVs, says which stream is the output. Recorded in docs/32 next to the tool. ALSO THIS SESSION: SLAM_THREADS=4 took the SLAM update rate from 15.07 Hz (dt median 66.4 ms = exactly two camera periods, i.e. every other frame dropped) to 29.75 Hz with zero gaps >300 ms, at 1.5 cores -- a real deficiency fixed, but the hypothesis that it would fix the ghost was FALSIFIED by the wearer, and that negative result is what forced the bisection that actually worked. STILL OPEN, stated as open: a residual wobble when a SLAM correction lands, because the filtered pose is still pushed with the new sample's timestamp while its value is ~8 ms older. Fix is timestamp compensation by the filter's group delay (reconstructible as fc_min + beta*|derivative|), deliberately not attempted -- backdated timestamps risk non-monotonic entries, which burned this project in 0021/0043. Second candidate for the same wobble, not yet separated: Basalt's own 12 deg p99 rotational jitter, which is pathological for a healthy VIO and which filtering only hides. They are separable: if the wobble is synchronised with the 30 Hz corrections it is the first, if continuous it is the second.

modo: T178: LAB -- the fps number nobody had, the render-scale default nobody chose, a position deadband, and a 'roll' that belonged to none of it
driver: lab-full b62a17de2 (0001-0045), jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof, Aircar + play360, GNOME Wayland 4320x2160@90
veredicto: THE REAL FRAME RATE IS 29 fps, AND NO INSTRUMENT WE HAD COULD SEE IT. Three tools disagreed all evening: Steam's overlay said 45, frame-pacing.sh said 0.00% late of 2700 expected, and the wearer said it looked fluid but slow. They were measuring three different things. frame-pacing.sh counts slots the COMPOSITOR missed and is structurally blind to an app that delivers 30 fps punctually -- it reported a flawless 0.00% while the wearer was looking at 30. The real number came from counting the app pacer's per-frame 'Delivered frame' lines (U_PACING_APP_LOG=debug): 29 delivered frames/s. Second blindness of the same instrument in one day, after the latency one; both now written into its header. AND THE APP IS NOT LIMITED BY ANYTHING WE CAN SEE: GPU 34-40% at 60-77 W, its busiest thread at 14% of a core, the pacer promising a full 11.11 ms period. That is the open thread. A WRONG TURN WORTH RECORDING: Monado's App-timing panel shows 'GPU time 10.8 ms' against an 11.11 ms budget, which I read as 'GPU-bound at 97%'. Falsified by measurement -- halving the pixel count changed it by 0.02 ms. The code says why: gpu_time = gpu_done_ns - delivered_ns, i.e. it includes queue wait behind the compositor's own work, so it pins near one period regardless of load. It also explains the 45: the SERIAL pacer sums cpu+draw+gpu = 14.97 ms > 11.11 and halves the app -- counting as work a wait the app does not control, which is exactly what 0042's pipelined gate stopped doing. XRT_COMPOSITOR_SCALE_PERCENTAGE DEFAULTS TO 140, a supersampling factor nobody in this project had ever looked at: 1.96x the pixels, and GPU power halved from ~180 W to 85 W at 100% with the wearer reporting no visual loss. Monado's own counter cannot see that difference; nvidia-smi's power draw can. Late frames also went 1.51% -> 0.00%. PATCH 0045, the wearer's idea: a position deadband with tracking, off by default, which had to go at the OUTPUT stage -- at the SLAM ingest it did nothing at all because dead reckoning adds accelerometer integration on top, and he proved that in one try by setting 30 metres and seeing no change. The rotation/position asymmetry is now documented at both use sites. 0.5 m turns out to be a usable seated mode. THE 'ROLL' BELONGED TO NONE OF THIS, and it took three corrections to find out: it was not the headset (measured at 0.47 deg/min raw / 0.51 delivered, with raw and delivered AGREEING -- so the drift is Basalt's, not our output path, and a third of T169's 1.39), not the VR controllers (their own drift is real but is IMU free-integration with constellation off), and not the Xbox pad (whose left stick IS genuinely 8.9% off-centre and wandering -- worn potentiometer, a 12.21% deadband applied with evdev-joystick, a real fix for a different problem). With the pad unplugged AND both VR controllers off the ship still rolled: it is Aircar's own physics. Four distinct phenomena treated as one for hours. THREE OF MY OWN ERRORS, all caught by measurement within minutes: proposing drift-measure.py for the HEADSET when its first line says it measures CONTROLLERS (it returned zeros with trk 0% and its own 'runs disagree, do not tune on single runs' guard fired correctly); putting the deadband before prediction; and raising 'the CSV writer died mid-session' as a possible regression in my own build when the cause was that VR_VERBOSE=0 -- which I had started using an hour earlier to silence 268 empty-poll log lines/s -- also switched off SLAM_WRITE_CSVS. TOOLING FIXED as a result: pose CSVs decoupled from VR_VERBOSE (VR_POSE_CSVS, default on) because silencing the driver's chatter must not silence the only offline instrument this project has; U_PACING_* log levels now respect externally-set values instead of being hardcoded; and frame-pacing.sh's `grep -c ... || echo 0` bug fixed -- grep prints 0 AND exits non-zero on no matches, so the fallback also fired and the variable held "0\n0", killing the script with a syntax error exactly when the answer was zero late frames, i.e. when the result was perfect. ALSO MEASURED: constellation controller tracking costs ~1.5 cores (monado 4.5 -> 6.88 with 4 SLAM threads, over 6 physical), both controllers registered with 32 LEDs each and pos:OK/trk:OK confirmed working -- but Aircar does not render hands, so it cannot validate them; Propagation VR is the named next bench. And the Steam save-sync dialog silently queued applaunches for the second time (T170), symptom: applaunch does nothing, client count stays 0.

modo: T179: LAB -- first full 6DoF end to end (headset + hands) in a real game, and the constellation's bistability traced to a transform that was already parsed
driver: lab-full a30028f3e (0001-0046), jack-in-wayland.sh 1 6dof, WMR_CONSTELLATION_CONTROLLERS=1, SLAM 2 threads, scale 100, Propagation VR
veredicto: PROJECT FIRST: full 6DoF end to end -- headset AND controllers tracked in position -- in a real game, playable, wearer started an actual match. Controller positional tracking had been parked since docs/03 and every prior session ran 6dof head + 3dof hands. Both controllers registered with the constellation tracker (32 LEDs each), pos:OK with trk:OK landing, and the user's verdict on the game itself was 'anda bien' at monado 4.5-4.8 cores of 6 physical. Propagation VR was chosen deliberately over Aircar because Aircar does not render hands and therefore cannot validate them -- an hour was spent earlier discovering that the hard way. THE HANDS JUMP, AND THE MEASUREMENT REVERSED MY FIRST EXPLANATION. Constellation telemetry already logs 1 in 15 solutions at INFO. Over the session: matched blobs median 8 of 13 visible, reprojection error median 0.15 px, p90 0.34, only 4% above 1 px, ~3.4 solutions/s across both hands. From that I concluded the jumps were the gap between fixes plus accelerometer dead reckoning -- wrong. With EVERYTHING physically still (headset on the desk facing two motionless controllers, 95 s) the solutions themselves scatter: one cluster median 193 mm / p90 321 mm, the tighter one median 32 mm / p90 126 mm, each individual fit reporting an excellent 0.15-0.45 px. A fit can be perfectly self-consistent and in the wrong place: with 5-6 blobs matched out of a 32-LED pattern the pose is under-determined and several blob-to-LED assignments reproject equally well. Caveat recorded: the two hands were separated with a crude 2-means, so the 193 mm cluster probably mixes both and is inflated; the 32 mm one is clean and already explains the symptom. AND THE PATCH I WAS ABOUT TO WRITE WAS ALREADY RULED OUT IN THE CODE. Going to add a quality gate on matched_blobs/reprojection error, I read the surrounding comment first: measured 2026-08-12, a motionless controller had a p99 step of 0.41-0.44 m with HEALTHY metrics on the bad ones (8 blobs at 0.06 px, 45 cm from truth), and the conclusion was explicit -- no threshold on the tracker's own metrics can separate them, only outside information can. Today's numbers reproduce that finding independently. The user had said 'dale derecho, te tengo fe'; the right answer to that trust was not to ship a patch the repo already documents as useless. THE REAL UNBLOCK, and it came from reading a struct rather than running another test: the same comment says an IMU-backed prior is 'NOT a drop-in' because the solve and the fusion live in different frames, and that the fixed transform must be resolved from the factory calibration first. It is already parsed. wmr_controller_config carries the LED model AND the inertial sensors from one CalibrationInformation block, so sensors.accel.pose IS the bridge. Patch 0046 logs it; read off both controllers: 105.3 deg / 85 mm and 105.5 deg / 83 mm, mirror images of each other, nowhere near the identity the default initialiser leaves. AND 105.3 DEG IS THE LOW MODE OF THE 104-161 DEG CONSTELLATION-VS-IMU DISAGREEMENT MEASURED BEFORE, within one degree. That explains the bimodality and hands over a discriminator: applying the transform should collapse the correct pose's gravity-axis disagreement toward zero while the wrong one keeps ~161, which is exactly the outside information the tie needs.
